        OPEN[OPENFIL.jcl<br/>Resume Online]
    end
    
    subgraph "Batch Input/Output Files"
        direction TB
        DALYTRAN[DALYTRAN<br/>Daily Transactions<br/>Sequential Input]
        DALYREJS["DALYREJS(+1)<br/>Reject File GDG<br/>Invalid Transactions"]
        COMBTRAN[COMBTRAN<br/>Combined Sorted File<br/>Statement Input]
    end
    
    subgraph "Archival Storage"
        direction TB
        GDG_TRAN[TRANSACT.BKUP<br/>GDG Generations<br/>G0072V00-G0076V00]
        GDG_TCAT[TCATBALF.BKUP<br/>GDG Generations<br/>G0005V00-G0009V00]
    end
    
    USER -->|Terminal I/O| COTRN02
    USER -->|Terminal I/O| COACTUPC
    USER -->|Terminal I/O| COBIL00
    
    COTRN02 -->|WRITE| TRAN_M
    COTRN02 -->|READ| CARD_M
    COACTUPC -->|REWRITE| ACCT_M
    COACTUPC -->|READ| CUST_M
    COBIL00 -->|REWRITE| ACCT_M
    COBIL00 -->|READ| XREF_M
    
    TRAN_M -.->|End of Day| CLOSE
    ACCT_M -.->|End of Day| CLOSE
    
    CLOSE -->|File Closed| POSTTRAN
    DALYTRAN -->|Sequential Read| POSTTRAN
    POSTTRAN -->|Direct Update| ACCT_M
    POSTTRAN -->|Direct Write| TRAN_M
    POSTTRAN -->|Write Rejects| DALYREJS
    
    POSTTRAN -->|Completion| INTCALC
    INTCALC -->|"Sequential Read/Update"| ACCT_M
    
    INTCALC -->|Completion| CREASTMT
    TRAN_M -->|Browse| CREASTMT
    ACCT_M -->|Browse| CREASTMT
    CREASTMT -->|SORT| COMBTRAN
    
    CREASTMT -->|Completion| TRANBKP
    TRAN_M -->|REPRO| TRANBKP
    TRANBKP -->|"Generation (+1)"| GDG_TRAN
    TRANBKP -->|"Generation (+1)"| GDG_TCAT
    
    TRANBKP -->|Completion| OPEN
    OPEN -.->|Files Reopened| USER
    
    style USER fill:#E1F5FF
    style CUST_M fill:#FFF4E1
    style ACCT_M fill:#FFF4E1
    style CARD_M fill:#FFF4E1
    style XREF_M fill:#FFF4E1
    style TRAN_M fill:#FFF4E1
    style DALYTRAN fill:#E8F5E9
    style DALYREJS fill:#FFE1E1
    style GDG_TRAN fill:#F3E5F5
    style GDG_TCAT fill:#F3E5F5
```

### 6.2.3 Data Management

#### 6.2.3.1 Migration Procedures

CardDemo implements comprehensive data migration procedures supporting initial load, platform migration, and ongoing data refresh operations:

**Initial Data Loading Sequence**

The system executes a coordinated 13-job sequence documented in README.md lines 82-98:

| Sequence | Job Name | Program | Purpose | Dependencies |
|----------|----------|---------|---------|--------------|
| 1 | DUSRSECJ | N/A | Define and load USRSEC security file | None |
| 2 | CLOSEFIL | CEMT commands | Close CICS files before data load | CICS region active |
| 3 | CUSTFILE | IDCAMS REPRO | Load customer master from ASCII/EBCDIC | Test data files |
| 4 | ACCTFILE | IDCAMS REPRO | Load account master | CUSTFILE complete |
| 5 | CARDFILE | IDCAMS REPRO | Load card master | ACCTFILE complete |
| 6 | XREFFILE | IDCAMS REPRO | Load cross-reference | CUSTFILE, ACCTFILE, CARDFILE complete |
| 7 | TRANFILE | IDCAMS REPRO | Load initial transactions | CARDFILE complete |
| 8 | DISCGRP | IDCAMS REPRO | Load disclosure groups | None |
| 9 | TCATBALF | IDCAMS REPRO | Load category balances | TRANCATG complete |
| 10 | TRANCATG | IDCAMS REPRO | Load transaction categories | None |
| 11 | TRANTYPE | IDCAMS REPRO | Load transaction types | None |
| 12 | OPENFIL | CEMT commands | Reopen files for CICS access | All data loads complete |
| 13 | DEFGDGB | IDCAMS DEFINE | Define GDG bases for backup | None |

**Data Format Conversion**

The system provides test data in dual formats supporting diverse platform requirements:

**ASCII Format** (`app/data/ASCII/` directory):
- **acctdata.txt**: 50 account records, fixed positions
- **carddata.txt**: 50 card records
- **cardxref.txt**: 50 cross-reference records, 34 characters each
- **custdata.txt**: 50 customer records
- **dailytran.txt**: Daily transaction file with 220-byte records
- **discgrp.txt**: 3 disclosure groups (A, DEFAULT, ZEROAPR)
- **tcatbal.txt**: 50 transaction category balance records
- **trancatg.txt**: 18 transaction category definitions
- **trantype.txt**: 7 transaction type definitions, 80 bytes each

**EBCDIC Format** (`app/data/EBCDIC/` directory):
- Equivalent files with AWS.M2.CARDDEMO namespace prefix
- Character encoding conversion from ASCII to EBCDIC
- Identical record structures and byte positioning

**Character Encoding Transformation**

Migration between platforms requires character set conversion:

| ASCII Code | Character | EBCDIC Code | Transformation Requirement |
|------------|-----------|-------------|---------------------------|
| 0x41-0x5A | A-Z | 0xC1-0xE9 | Uppercase alphabet conversion |
| 0x30-0x39 | 0-9 | 0xF0-0xF9 | Numeric digit conversion |
| 0x20 | Space | 0x40 | Space character conversion |
| 0x2E | Period | 0x4B | Punctuation conversion |

Micro Focus and UniKix migration platforms perform automatic EBCDIC-to-ASCII conversion for data files during modernization.

**Platform-Specific Migration Samples**

- **Micro Focus**: `samples/m2/mf/` directory contains platform-specific configuration
- **UniKix**: `samples/m2/unikix/` directory contains platform adaptations
- **AWS Mainframe Modernization**: Primary target platform for automated transformation

#### 6.2.3.2 Versioning Strategy

CardDemo implements file versioning through Generation Data Groups (GDG) providing automatic version management:

**GDG Base Definitions**

Four GDG bases provide versioned dataset management (DEFGDGB.jcl job, LISTCAT.txt lines 684-696):

| GDG Base | Limit | Scratch | Empty | Order | Purpose |
|----------|-------|---------|-------|-------|---------|
| DALYREJS | 5 | YES | NO | LIFO | Daily reject file versions for audit |
| SYSTRAN | 5 | YES | NO | LIFO | System transaction archive |
| TRANSACT.BKUP | 5 | NO | NO | LIFO | Transaction file backups (retained) |
| TCATBALF.BKUP | 5 | YES | NO | LIFO | Category balance backups (auto-purge) |

**Version Notation Syntax**:
- **(0)**: Current generation (most recent)
- **(+1)**: Next generation to be created
- **(-1)**: Previous generation (one back)
- **(-2)**: Two generations back
- **GnnnnVnn**: Absolute generation number (e.g., G0076V00)

**Version Lifecycle Management**

TRANSACT.BKUP GDG retention policy (from LISTCAT.txt lines 1527-1630):

**Active Generations** (within LIMIT=5):
- G0076V00 - Current generation (0)
- G0075V00 - Previous generation (-1)
- G0074V00 - Two back (-2)
- G0073V00 - Three back (-3)
- G0072V00 - Four back (-4)

**Rolled-Off Generations** (NOSCRATCH preserves historical versions):
- G0071V00 through G0001V00 - Historical audit trail (71 generations retained)

**SCRATCH vs. NOSCRATCH Behavior**:

**NOSCRATCH** (TRANSACT.BKUP):
- Generations exceeding LIMIT=5 are deactivated but not deleted
- Historical generations preserved indefinitely for compliance and audit
- Manual deletion required via IDCAMS DELETE command

**SCRATCH** (DALYREJS, SYSTRAN, TCATBALF.BKUP):
- Oldest generation automatically deleted when LIMIT exceeded
- Automatic space reclamation without operator intervention
- Retains only recent history defined by LIMIT parameter

**Version Creation Pattern**

```jcl
//BACKUP   EXEC PGM=IDCAMS
//TRANSIN  DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.KSDS,DISP=SHR
//TRANSOUT DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.BKUP(+1),DISP=(NEW,CATLG)
//SYSIN    DD *
  REPRO INFILE(TRANSIN) OUTFILE(TRANSOUT)
/*
```

The (+1) notation automatically:
1. Creates new generation number (increments highest existing generation)
2. Catalogs new generation in GDG base
3. Rotates existing generations (0 becomes -1, -1 becomes -2, etc.)
4. Deactivates or deletes oldest generation based on SCRATCH/NOSCRATCH

#### 6.2.3.3 Archival Policies

CardDemo implements multi-tier archival strategies based on data retention requirements and access frequency:

**Tier 1: Active Online Data**

- **Datasets**: CUSTFILE, ACCTFILE, CARDFILE, XREFFILE, TRANSACT
- **Retention**: Indefinite (permanent master files)
- **Access Pattern**: Random access via CICS online programs
- **Storage**: Primary DASD with LSR buffer pool caching
- **Backup Frequency**: Nightly via GDG generation

**Tier 2: Daily Batch Processing Data**

- **Datasets**: DALYTRAN, DALYREJS(+1)
- **Retention**: 5 generations (5 business days)
- **Access Pattern**: Sequential batch processing
- **Archival Trigger**: Daily batch execution creates new generation
- **Purge Policy**: SCRATCH enabled, automatic deletion after 5 generations

**Tier 3: Historical Transaction Backups**

- **Datasets**: TRANSACT.BKUP GDG (G0001V00 through G0076V00)
- **Retention**: Indefinite (NOSCRATCH)
- **Access Pattern**: Recovery and audit only
- **Storage**: Can be migrated to tape or virtual tape for long-term retention
- **Purpose**: Point-in-time recovery, audit compliance, forensic analysis

**Tier 4: Reference Data Archives**

- **Datasets**: TRANCATG, TRANTYPE, DISCGRP
- **Retention**: Permanent with version history
- **Update Frequency**: Annual for categories, quarterly for disclosure rates
- **Backup Strategy**: Full backup before each update cycle

**Archival Execution Workflow**

The batch processing sequence (README.md lines 165-183) implements nightly archival:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Online as CICS Online Processing
    participant Close as CLOSEFIL.jcl
    participant Post as POSTTRAN.jcl
    participant Backup as TRANBKP.jcl
    participant GDG as GDG Archive Storage
    participant Open as OPENFIL.jcl
    
    Note over Online: Day N - Active transactions accumulate
    Online->>Close: End of Day N (22:00)
    Close->>Post: Files closed for batch
    
    Note over Post: Process daily transactions
    Post->>Post: Validate DALYTRAN input
    Post->>Post: Update ACCTFILE balances
    Post->>Post: Write DALYREJS(+1) rejects
    
    Post->>Backup: Processing complete
    Note over Backup: Create backup generation
    Backup->>GDG: TRANSACT → TRANSACT.BKUP(+1)
    Backup->>GDG: TCATBALF → TCATBALF.BKUP(+1)
    
    Note over GDG: New generations: G0077V00
    Note over GDG: Rotate: G0076V00 becomes (-1)
    Note over GDG: Deactivate: G0001V00 (oldest)
    
    Backup->>Open: Backup complete
    Open->>Online: Files reopened (06:00 Day N+1)
    Note over Online: Day N+1 - Online processing resumes
```

**Space Reclamation**

VSAM space management (LISTCAT.txt SMSDATA sections):
- **CA-RECLAIM**: YES (automatic control area space reclamation)
- **FREESPACE Reuse**: REUSE option enabled on USRSEC for immediate space reclamation
- **Compaction**: Periodic reorganization via IDCAMS REPRO to eliminate fragmentation

#### 6.2.3.4 Data Storage and Retrieval Mechanisms

CardDemo implements differentiated access patterns optimized for online and batch processing:

**Online Random Access (CICS Programs)**

Programs use EXEC CICS commands for key-based retrieval:

```cobol
* Direct retrieval by primary key
MOVE '0000000001' TO WS-ACCT-ID
EXEC CICS READ FILE('ACCTFILE')
     INTO(ACCOUNT-RECORD)
     RIDFLD(WS-ACCT-ID)
     RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
END-EXEC

EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD
   WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL)
      * Record found - process ACCOUNT-RECORD
      DISPLAY 'Balance: ' ACCT-CURR-BAL
   WHEN DFHRESP(NOTFND)
      * Record not found - display error
      MOVE 'Account not found' TO ERROR-MESSAGE
   WHEN OTHER
      * Unexpected error - abend with dump
      EXEC CICS ABEND ABCODE('ACCT') END-EXEC
END-EVALUATE
```

**Sequential Browse (CICS Programs)**

Programs use STARTBR/READNEXT pattern for list processing:

```cobol
* Initiate browse starting at specific key
MOVE '0000000001' TO WS-START-KEY
EXEC CICS STARTBR FILE('ACCTFILE')
     RIDFLD(WS-START-KEY)
     GTEQ
     RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
END-EXEC

* Read successive records
PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-BROWSE
   EXEC CICS READNEXT FILE('ACCTFILE')
        INTO(ACCOUNT-RECORD)
        RIDFLD(WS-CURRENT-KEY)
        RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
   END-EXEC
   
   EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD
      WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL)
         * Process record
         PERFORM DISPLAY-ACCOUNT
      WHEN DFHRESP(ENDFILE)
         * End of file reached
         SET END-OF-BROWSE TO TRUE
      WHEN OTHER
         * Handle error
         SET END-OF-BROWSE TO TRUE
   END-EVALUATE
END-PERFORM

* Terminate browse
EXEC CICS ENDBR FILE('ACCTFILE') END-EXEC
```

**Batch Sequential Access**

Batch programs specify ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL for full-file processing:

```cobol
* File definition for sequential access
SELECT ACCTFILE-FILE ASSIGN TO ACCTFILE
    ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED
    ACCESS MODE  IS SEQUENTIAL
    RECORD KEY   IS FD-ACCT-ID
    FILE STATUS  IS ACCTFILE-STATUS.

PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    OPEN INPUT ACCTFILE-FILE
    
    PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE
       READ ACCTFILE-FILE INTO ACCOUNT-RECORD
       IF ACCTFILE-STATUS = '00'
          * Successful read - process record
          PERFORM PROCESS-ACCOUNT
       ELSE IF ACCTFILE-STATUS = '10'
          * End of file
          SET END-OF-FILE TO TRUE
       ELSE
          * I/O error - trigger abend
          CALL 'CEE3ABD' USING ERROR-CODE, REASON-CODE
       END-IF
    END-PERFORM
    
    CLOSE ACCTFILE-FILE
```

**Update Operations with Locking**

Record updates require READ UPDATE for exclusive locking:

```cobol
* Acquire exclusive lock on record
EXEC CICS READ FILE('CARDFILE')
     INTO(CARD-RECORD)
     RIDFLD(CARD-NUMBER)
     UPDATE
     RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
END-EXEC

* Verify successful lock acquisition
IF WS-RESP-CD = DFHRESP(NORMAL)
   * Modify record in memory
   MOVE 'JOHN DOE' TO CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME
   MOVE '2028-12' TO CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE
   
   * Write modified record back (releases lock)
   EXEC CICS REWRITE FILE('CARDFILE')
        FROM(CARD-RECORD)
        RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
   END-EXEC
   
   IF WS-RESP-CD = DFHRESP(NORMAL)
      MOVE 'Update successful' TO MESSAGE
   ELSE
      MOVE 'Update failed' TO MESSAGE
      * Lock automatically released on error
   END-IF
ELSE
   * Record not available or locked by another task
   MOVE 'Record unavailable' TO MESSAGE
END-IF
```

**Alternate Index Retrieval**

Access via secondary keys through alternate index paths:

```cobol
* Retrieve cards by account ID using CARDDATA.AIX
MOVE '00000000001' TO WS-ACCT-ID

* Start browse using alternate index path
EXEC CICS STARTBR FILE('CARDAIX')
     RIDFLD(WS-ACCT-ID)
     GTEQ
     RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
END-EXEC

* Read all cards for this account
PERFORM UNTIL NO-MORE-CARDS
   EXEC CICS READNEXT FILE('CARDAIX')
        INTO(CARD-RECORD)
        RIDFLD(WS-KEY)
        RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
   END-EXEC
   
   * Check if still reading same account
   IF CARD-ACCT-ID NOT = WS-ACCT-ID
      SET NO-MORE-CARDS TO TRUE
   ELSE
      * Process card for this account
      PERFORM DISPLAY-CARD-INFO
   END-IF
END-PERFORM

EXEC CICS ENDBR FILE('CARDAIX') END-EXEC
```

#### 6.2.3.5 Caching Policies

CardDemo implements multi-level caching through VSAM buffer pools and CICS resource management:

**LSR Buffer Pool Configuration**

All VSAM files share Local Shared Resources (LSR) buffer pool for data and index caching:

**Buffer Pool Allocation** (from LISTCAT.txt ATTRIBUTES sections):

| Dataset | BUFSPACE | CISIZE | Buffer Capacity | Cache Strategy |
|---------|----------|--------|----------------|----------------|
| CUSTDATA | 37,376 bytes | 18,432 bytes | 2.03 CIs | Data + Index caching |
| ACCTDATA | 37,376 bytes | 18,432 bytes | 2.03 CIs | Data + Index caching |
| TRANSACT | 37,376 bytes | 18,432 bytes | 2.03 CIs | Data + Index caching |
| USRSEC | 24,576 bytes | 8,192 bytes | 3.0 CIs | Smaller CI for faster access |

**CICS LSR Pool Definition**:
- **LSRPOOLNUM**: 1 (all CardDemo files share pool 1)
- **DATABUFFERS**: 2 (two data control interval buffers)
- **INDEXBUFFERS**: 1 (one index control interval buffer)
- **STRNO**: Number of concurrent string operations (browse cursors)

**Caching Behavior**:

**Data Buffer Hits**: When a CICS task reads a record, VSAM checks if the containing CI is already in the LSR buffer pool:
- **Hit**: Record retrieved from memory (sub-millisecond response)
- **Miss**: Physical I/O executed to read CI from DASD, CI cached in buffer pool

**Index Buffer Hits**: VSAM checks index buffers for B-tree nodes:
- **Hit**: Index traversal completes in memory without I/O
- **Miss**: Index CI read from DASD and cached

**Statistics from LISTCAT.txt**:

**TRANSACT Index Performance**:
- **REC-RETRIEVED**: 311 (all records accessed)
- **EXCPS**: 8 (execute channel programs - I/O operations)
- **Hit Ratio**: ~97.4% (only 8 I/Os for 311 retrievals indicates excellent caching)

**Cache Replacement Policy**:
- **Algorithm**: LRU (Least Recently Used) for LSR buffer pool
- **Scope**: Shared across all CICS tasks accessing the same file
- **Persistence**: Buffers retained for life of CICS region

**CICS Program Caching**:

**Program Load Module Caching**:
- **Location**: Program library (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB)
- **Caching**: COBOL programs loaded into CICS DSA (Dynamic Storage Area) on first use
- **Reuse**: Reentrant programs (compiled with RENT option) shared across concurrent tasks
- **Refresh**: NEWCOPY command loads updated program without region restart

**BMS Map Caching**:
- **Physical Maps**: Loaded into CICS storage on first SEND MAP
- **Symbolic Maps**: Compiled into COBOL programs as copybook includes
- **Shared Access**: Multiple tasks share same physical map definitions

**No Application-Level Caching**:

CardDemo does not implement application-level caching mechanisms such as:
- In-memory hash tables for frequently accessed records
- Session-level data caching across transactions
- Distributed caching layers (Redis, Memcached)

This design reflects mainframe architectural norms where VSAM buffer management and CICS resource pooling provide sufficient performance for sub-second response times.

### 6.2.4 Compliance Considerations

#### 6.2.4.1 Data Retention Rules

CardDemo implements tiered retention policies aligned with transactional data classification:

**Permanent Retention (Master Data)**

| Data Category | Datasets | Retention Period | Justification |
|---------------|----------|-----------------|---------------|
| Customer Identity | CUSTFILE | Indefinite | Customer relationship persists until account closure |
| Account Records | ACCTFILE | Indefinite | Account lifecycle data retained for regulatory compliance |
| Card Credentials | CARDFILE | Until card expiration + 7 years | Payment card industry retention requirements |
| Cross-Reference | XREFFILE | Matches longest-lived entity | Referential integrity maintenance |

**Transactional Retention (Transaction Data)**

| Data Category | Datasets | Retention Period | Archive Strategy |
|---------------|----------|-----------------|------------------|
| Online Transactions | TRANSACT | Current cycle + 24 months | GDG backup with NOSCRATCH |
| Historical Backups | TRANSACT.BKUP | Indefinite | 76 generations retained (G0001V00-G0076V00) |
| Daily Batch Input | DALYTRAN | 5 business days | GDG with SCRATCH |
| Batch Rejects | DALYREJS | 5 business days | GDG with SCRATCH for audit trail |

**Reference Data Retention**

| Data Category | Datasets | Retention Period | Update Frequency |
|---------------|----------|-----------------|------------------|
| Transaction Categories | TRANCATG | Permanent with version history | Annual updates |
| Transaction Types | TRANTYPE | Permanent | Rarely modified |
| Disclosure Groups | DISCGRP | Permanent with rate history | Quarterly rate updates |
| Category Balances | TCATBALF | Current + 5 backup generations | Nightly recalculation |

**Retention Implementation Mechanisms**:

- **GDG LIMIT Parameter**: Enforces retention window (5 generations = 5 days for daily jobs)
- **NOSCRATCH Option**: Prevents automatic deletion for audit-critical data (TRANSACT.BKUP)
- **Manual Purge Process**: Periodic review and deletion of rolled-off generations beyond compliance requirements
- **Catalog Management**: LISTCAT.txt documents all generation status and creation timestamps

#### 6.2.4.2 Backup and Fault Tolerance Policies

CardDemo implements basic disaster recovery without production-grade fault tolerance:

**Backup Frequency and Scope**

| Backup Job | Frequency | Coverage | Recovery Objective |
|------------|-----------|----------|-------------------|
| TRANBKP.jcl | Nightly (after batch) | TRANSACT, TCATBALF | Point-in-time recovery to previous day |
| Ad-hoc REPRO | Pre-maintenance | All master files | Full dataset restoration |
| CICS CSD Backup | Weekly | CICS System Definition | Resource definition recovery |

**Backup Execution Pattern**:

The TRANBKP.jcl job executes via IDCAMS REPRO command:

```jcl
//TRANBKP  JOB ...
//BACKUP   EXEC PGM=IDCAMS
//TRANSIN  DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.KSDS,DISP=SHR
//TRANSOUT DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.BKUP(+1),DISP=(NEW,CATLG)
//TCATSIN  DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TCATBALF.KSDS,DISP=SHR
//TCATSOUT DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TCATBALF.BKUP(+1),DISP=(NEW,CATLG)
//SYSIN    DD *
  REPRO INFILE(TRANSIN) OUTFILE(TRANSOUT)
  REPRO INFILE(TCATSIN) OUTFILE(TCATSOUT)
/*
```

**Recovery Time Objective (RTO)**: Not formally defined; demonstration system prioritizes simplicity over rapid recovery

**Recovery Point Objective (RPO)**: ~24 hours (data loss limited to most recent day's online transactions)

**Fault Tolerance Limitations**:

**No Transaction Journaling**:
- VSAM datasets configured with JOURNAL=NO
- No forward recovery (cannot replay transactions from log)
- No backward recovery (cannot undo uncommitted changes)
- Recovery limited to full dataset restoration from backup

**No Real-Time Replication**:
- Single-copy data architecture (no synchronous replication)
- No geographic redundancy (single-site deployment)
- No automatic failover capabilities

**No CICS Transaction Restart**:
- Failed transactions do not automatically restart
- Users must manually retry failed operations
- No distributed transaction coordinator

**Single Point of Failure**:
- Single CICS region (no Parallel Sysplex configuration)
- Single z/OS LPAR (no multi-system clustering)
- Single DASD storage system (no mirrored volumes)

**Production-Grade Enhancements** (not implemented in CardDemo):

Would require:
- **VSAM LSR Journal**: Enable transaction logging via JOURNAL parameter
- **CICS Transaction Journaling**: System log for transaction restart
- **GDPS**: Geographically Dispersed Parallel Sysplex for site-level disaster recovery
- **GRS**: Global Resource Serialization for cross-system file sharing
- **Parallel Sysplex**: Multiple CICS regions with workload distribution
- **DASD Mirroring**: Real-time volume replication (Metro Mirror, Global Mirror)

#### 6.2.4.3 Privacy Controls

CardDemo contains Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and Payment Card Industry (PCI) sensitive data requiring protection controls:

**PII Data Elements**

| Field Name | Copybook | Sensitivity Level | Protection Requirement |
|------------|----------|------------------|----------------------|
| CUST-SSN | CUSTREC.cpy | High - SSN | Encryption at rest and in transit |
| CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID | CUSTREC.cpy | High - Government ID | Encryption and access logging |
| CARD-CVV-CD | CVACT02Y.cpy | Critical - CVV | Never store (PCI-DSS violation) |
| CARD-NUM | CVACT02Y.cpy | High - PAN | Truncation/masking for display |

**Current Privacy Implementation**:

**Field-Level Masking (BMS Maps)**:
- Password fields use ASKIP, FSET attributes for masked input
- Display programs show truncated card numbers (e.g., "************1234")
- CVV codes never displayed after initial entry

**No Encryption at Rest**:
- LISTCAT.txt ENCRYPTIONDATA sections show DATA SET ENCRYPTION: NO
- All VSAM files stored in clear text
- Relies on z/OS dataset-level RACF protection

**No Encryption in Transit**:
- 3270 terminal traffic unencrypted (unless TN3270E with TLS configured externally)
- CICS-to-VSAM communication internal to z/OS (no network exposure)

**Access Control via User Type**:
- Admin users (Type 'A') access user administration functions (COUSR00-03)
- Regular users (Type 'U') restricted to account/card/transaction functions
- COMMAREA.CDEMO-USER-TYPE field enforces role-based access

**Production Privacy Enhancements** (not implemented):

Would require:
- **VSAM Encryption**: Enable z/OS dataset encryption for files containing PII
- **Tokenization**: Replace real card numbers with tokens for processing
- **CVV Removal**: Never persist CVV codes (PCI-DSS requirement)
- **Data Masking**: Implement view-level masking for sensitive fields
- **Audit Logging**: Log all access to PII fields with user/timestamp
- **GDPR Compliance**: Right to erasure (customer deletion), data portability, consent management

#### 6.2.4.4 Audit Mechanisms

CardDemo implements basic audit trails through transactional timestamps and backup generation tracking:

**Transaction Audit Trail**

Every transaction record (CVTRA05Y.cpy) contains dual timestamps:

```cobol
05  TRAN-ORIG-TS            PIC X(26).
05  TRAN-PROC-TS            PIC X(26).
```

**Timestamp Format**: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmmmm (ISO-8601 with microsecond precision)

**Audit Capabilities**:
- **Original Timestamp**: When transaction first occurred (user submission time)
- **Processing Timestamp**: When transaction posted to account (batch processing time)
- **Merchant Audit**: Merchant ID, name, city, ZIP captured for each transaction
- **Source System**: TRAN-SOURCE field identifies originating system

**Backup Generation Audit**

GDG generations provide audit trail of backup execution:

From LISTCAT.txt HISTORY sections:

```
HISTORY
  RELEASE----------------2
  OWNER-IDENT------------(NULL)
  CREATION---------------2024.145.11.30.00
  EXPIRATION-------------0000.000
```

Each generation records:
- **CREATION**: Timestamp of generation creation (YYYY.DDD.HH.MM.SS format)
- **Generation Number**: Sequential version identifier (G0076V00)
- **Status**: ACTIVE, ROLLED-OFF, or DEACTIVATED

**Batch Job Execution Audit**

JES job logs provide comprehensive audit trail:
- Job submission timestamp
- Job completion code (CC 0000 = success)
- Dataset allocations and dispositions
- IDCAMS REPRO record counts (records processed, records copied)
- Error messages and abend codes

**File Status Change Audit**

CICS CEMT commands in CLOSEFIL.jcl and OPENFIL.jcl create console log entries:

```
CEMT SET FILE(ACCTFILE) CLOSED
CEMT SET FILE(ACCTFILE) OPEN
```

**Audit Limitations**:

**No User Action Logging**:
- CICS transactions do not log user actions (account updates, card modifications)
- No "who changed what when" tracking at field level
- No before/after value comparison

**No Failed Login Tracking**:
- Authentication attempts not logged in USRSEC file
- No intrusion detection or brute-force prevention
- No account lockout after failed attempts

**No Data Access Logging**:
- READ operations do not generate audit records
- No tracking of who viewed sensitive PII data
- No compliance reporting for GDPR/CCPA access requests

**Production Audit Enhancements** (not implemented):

Would require:
- **CICS Audit Trail**: Enable CICS transaction logging with user ID capture
- **SMF Records**: Capture System Management Facility records for all file access
- **Database Triggers**: Implement before/after value logging for updates
- **SIEM Integration**: Forward audit logs to Security Information and Event Management platform
- **Immutable Audit Logs**: Write-once storage for tamper-proof audit trail
- **Compliance Reporting**: Automated generation of PCI-DSS, SOX, GDPR compliance reports

#### 6.2.4.5 Access Controls

CardDemo implements role-based access control through user type classification and program-level authorization:

**Authentication Mechanism**

User authentication enforced via COSGN00C program:

```cobol
* Read user credentials from USRSEC file
MOVE USER-ID TO SEC-USR-ID
EXEC CICS READ FILE('USRSEC')
     INTO(SEC-USER-DATA)
     RIDFLD(SEC-USR-ID)
     RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
END-EXEC

* Validate password (stored in clear text - demo only)
IF WS-RESP-CD = DFHRESP(NORMAL)
   IF SEC-USR-PWD = ENTERED-PASSWORD
      * Authentication successful
      MOVE SEC-USR-TYPE TO CDEMO-USER-TYPE
      * Route based on user type
      IF CDEMO-USER-TYPE = 'A'
         EXEC CICS XCTL PROGRAM('COADM01C') COMMAREA(...) END-EXEC
      ELSE
         EXEC CICS XCTL PROGRAM('COMEN01C') COMMAREA(...) END-EXEC
      END-IF
   ELSE
      * Invalid password
      MOVE 'Invalid credentials' TO ERROR-MSG
   END-IF
ELSE
   * User ID not found
   MOVE 'User not found' TO ERROR-MSG
END-IF
```

**Role-Based Access Matrix**

| Function | Program | Admin (Type A) | User (Type U) |
|----------|---------|---------------|---------------|
| Account View | COACTVWC | ✓ | ✓ |
| Account Update | COACTUPC | ✓ | ✓ |
| Card View | COCRDSLC | ✓ | ✓ |
| Card Update | COCRDUPC | ✓ | ✓ |
| Transaction View | COTRN01C | ✓ | ✓ |
| Transaction Add | COTRN02C | ✓ | ✓ |
| Bill Payment | COBIL00C | ✓ | ✓ |
| User List | COUSR00C | ✓ | ✗ |
| User Add | COUSR01C | ✓ | ✗ |
| User Update | COUSR02C | ✓ | ✗ |
| User Delete | COUSR03C | ✓ | ✗ |

**Authorization Enforcement Points**:

**Menu-Level Control**:
- Admin menu (COADM01C) presented only to Type 'A' users
- Regular user menu (COMEN01C) presented to Type 'U' users
- COMMAREA.CDEMO-USER-TYPE preserved across all transactions

**Transaction Security (CICS Security)**:
- CICS resource security via CARDDEMO.CSD definitions
- TRANSID-level access control (potential RACF integration)
- Program-level execution authorization

**File-Level Access Control**:

VSAM files configured without password protection (LISTCAT.txt PROTECTION sections):
- PROTECTION-PSWD: (NULL)
- RACF: NO (RACF dataset protection not enabled)

**Production-Grade Access Control** (not implemented):

Would require:
- **RACF Integration**: Map CICS user IDs to RACF profiles
- **Resource-Level Security**: RACF rules for transaction/program/file access
- **Password Policy**: Complexity requirements, expiration, history
- **Multi-Factor Authentication**: Smart card, biometric, or token-based authentication
- **Session Timeout**: Automatic terminal sign-off after inactivity
- **Network Access Control**: IP address restrictions, VPN requirements
- **Privileged Access Management**: Separate admin accounts, break-glass procedures

### 6.2.5 Performance Optimization

#### 6.2.5.1 Query Optimization Patterns

CardDemo implements VSAM-specific optimization patterns for efficient data retrieval:

**Primary Key Direct Access**

Optimal performance achieved through primary key lookups with O(log n) complexity:

```cobol
* Single-record retrieval - most efficient pattern
MOVE '00000000001' TO ACCT-ID
EXEC CICS READ FILE('ACCTFILE')
     INTO(ACCOUNT-RECORD)
     RIDFLD(ACCT-ID)
     RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
END-EXEC
```

**Performance**: ~0.1-1.0 milliseconds for cached records, ~5-10 milliseconds for non-cached (requires physical I/O)

**Index Statistics (from LISTCAT.txt)**:
- **INDEX LEVELS**: 1 (single-level B-tree for datasets with 50-311 records)
- **SPLITS-CI**: 0 (no index fragmentation)
- **EXCPS**: 8 I/O operations for 311 record retrievals (97.4% buffer hit ratio)

**Alternate Index Access Optimization**

Secondary key access through AIX avoids full-file scan:

```cobol
* Retrieve all cards for an account using AIX
MOVE '00000000001' TO SEARCH-ACCT-ID
EXEC CICS STARTBR FILE('CARDAIX')
     RIDFLD(SEARCH-ACCT-ID)
     GTEQ
     RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
END-EXEC

PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-CARDS
   EXEC CICS READNEXT FILE('CARDAIX')
        INTO(CARD-RECORD)
        RIDFLD(CURRENT-KEY)
        RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
   END-EXEC
   
   * Terminate when account ID changes
   IF CARD-ACCT-ID NOT = SEARCH-ACCT-ID
      SET END-OF-CARDS TO TRUE
   ELSE
      PERFORM PROCESS-CARD
   END-IF
END-PERFORM
```

**Performance**: AIX lookup time = Primary index traversal + AIX traversal + Base record retrieval
- **Without AIX**: O(n) full-file scan
- **With AIX**: O(log n) index lookup + O(k) where k = matching records

**Generic Key Searches**

VSAM supports generic key searches with GTEQ (Greater Than or Equal):

```cobol
* Find all accounts starting with '0000001'
MOVE '0000001' TO PARTIAL-KEY
EXEC CICS STARTBR FILE('ACCTFILE')
     RIDFLD(PARTIAL-KEY)
     GTEQ
     KEYLENGTH(7)
     RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
END-EXEC
```

**Key Length Optimization**: Specifying KEYLENGTH(7) restricts index search to first 7 bytes, reducing comparison overhead.

**Skip Sequential Processing**

For sparse record access, restart browse rather than sequential scan:

```cobol
* Access every 10th record by repositioning browse
PERFORM VARYING RECORD-COUNT FROM 1 BY 10
   MOVE RECORD-COUNT TO POSITION-KEY
   
   * Reposition browse to specific key
   EXEC CICS STARTBR FILE('TRANSACT')
        RIDFLD(POSITION-KEY)
        GTEQ
        RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
   END-EXEC
   
   * Read single record
   EXEC CICS READNEXT FILE('TRANSACT')
        INTO(TRAN-RECORD)
        RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
   END-EXEC
   
   * Terminate this browse
   EXEC CICS ENDBR FILE('TRANSACT') END-EXEC
   
   PERFORM PROCESS-TRANSACTION
END-PERFORM
```

**Batch Sequential Optimization**

Batch programs specify ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL for optimal throughput:

```cobol
SELECT ACCTFILE ASSIGN TO ACCTFILE
    ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED
    ACCESS MODE  IS SEQUENTIAL
    RECORD KEY   IS ACCT-ID
    FILE STATUS  IS FILE-STATUS.

OPEN INPUT ACCTFILE

* Sequential read leverages VSAM read-ahead
PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE
   READ ACCTFILE INTO ACCOUNT-RECORD
   AT END
      SET END-OF-FILE TO TRUE
   NOT AT END
      PERFORM PROCESS-ACCOUNT
   END-READ
END-PERFORM
```

**Performance**: Sequential access achieves 10,000-50,000 records/second depending on record size and CISIZE.

#### 6.2.5.2 Caching Strategy

Multi-tier caching architecture optimizes both data access and program execution:

**VSAM LSR Buffer Pool (Data Caching)**

**Configuration** (from CICS File definitions):
- **LSR Pool**: 1 (all CardDemo files share pool)
- **Data Buffers**: 2 control intervals
- **Index Buffers**: 1 control interval
- **Buffer Size**: CISIZE (8192 or 18432 bytes per CI)

**Cache Efficiency Metrics**:

| File | CISIZE | Buffers | Records per CI | Cache Capacity |
|------|--------|---------|----------------|----------------|
| CUSTDATA | 18,432 bytes | 2 data CIs | ~36 records | ~72 customers cached |
| ACCTDATA | 18,432 bytes | 2 data CIs | ~61 records | ~122 accounts cached |
| CARDDATA | 18,432 bytes | 2 data CIs | ~122 records | ~244 cards cached |
| TRANSACT | 18,432 bytes | 2 data CIs | ~52 records | ~104 transactions cached |

**Cache Hit Optimization**:

**Hot Data Placement**: Most frequently accessed records (recent transactions, active accounts) benefit from LRU algorithm keeping them in cache.

**Sequential Browse Optimization**: VSAM read-ahead loads multiple CIs during sequential access, pre-populating cache for subsequent reads.

**CICS Program Cache**

**Program Load Optimization**:
- **First Access**: Program loaded from load library into CICS DSA (Dynamic Storage Area)
- **Subsequent Access**: Shared reentrant program executed from memory
- **Concurrency**: Multiple tasks share single program load module (RENT compilation option)

**Program Refresh**:
```
CEMT SET PROGRAM(COACTUPC) NEWCOPY
```
Forces reload without CICS region restart.

**BMS Map Cache**:
- Physical maps loaded once per CICS region startup
- Symbolic maps compiled into program working storage
- Map caching reduces terminal I/O overhead

**No Distributed Caching**:

CardDemo does not implement:
- External cache servers (Redis, Memcached)
- Application-managed cache invalidation
- Session state caching (COMMAREA provides session context)
- Query result caching

#### 6.2.5.3 Connection Pooling

CardDemo's mainframe architecture does not employ connection pooling in the traditional distributed systems sense, as there is no database server with network connections. Instead, VSAM file access occurs through z/OS access methods with resource pooling managed by CICS:

**CICS String Allocation**

**String**: A CICS File Control resource representing an active I/O operation against a VSAM file.

**Configuration** (defined in CARDDEMO.CSD):
- **STRINGS(2)**: Two concurrent I/O operations per file
- **LSRPOOLNUM(1)**: All files share LSR pool 1

**String Management**:

When a CICS task issues EXEC CICS READ:
1. CICS allocates a string from the file's string pool
2. String remains allocated during the I/O operation
3. String released when operation completes
4. Next task can reuse the freed string

**String Contention**:

If all strings are in use:
- **CICS Waits**: Task suspended until string becomes available
- **No Error**: Transparent to application (unlike connection pool exhaustion)
- **Tuning**: Increase STRINGS parameter if contention observed

**Browse String Optimization**:

Browse operations (STARTBR/READNEXT) retain string until ENDBR:

```cobol
EXEC CICS STARTBR FILE('ACCTFILE')  * Allocates string
     RIDFLD(KEY) 
END-EXEC

* String remains allocated during entire browse
PERFORM 100 TIMES
   EXEC CICS READNEXT FILE('ACCTFILE')  * Reuses same string
        INTO(RECORD)
   END-EXEC
END-PERFORM

EXEC CICS ENDBR FILE('ACCTFILE')  * Releases string
```

**Best Practice**: Terminate browse operations promptly to release strings for other tasks.

**CICS Task Management**

**Task Pool** (equivalent to thread pool in distributed systems):
- **MAXTASKS**: Maximum concurrent CICS tasks
- **MXT**: Active task limit
- **Task Creation**: New task created for each terminal transaction or START command
- **Task Termination**: Automatic when transaction completes

**Resource Pooling Benefits**:
- **Memory Efficiency**: Reentrant programs shared across tasks
- **I/O Efficiency**: LSR buffer pool shared across all file access
- **String Reuse**: Rapid allocation/deallocation without overhead

#### 6.2.5.4 Read/Write Splitting

CardDemo does not implement read/write splitting typical of distributed database architectures with master-replica configurations. The VSAM architecture employs a single-copy data model where all reads and writes access the same physical dataset.

**Online vs. Batch Access Segregation**

Instead of read/write splitting, CardDemo implements temporal segregation:

**Online Access Window** (06:00 - 22:00):
- **Read Operations**: Account inquiries, transaction views
- **Write Operations**: Transaction entry, account updates, bill payments
- **Access Mode**: Random access via primary/alternate indexes
- **Concurrency**: Record-level locking supports concurrent updates

**Batch Processing Window** (22:00 - 06:00):
- **Read Operations**: Sequential file scans for reporting, statement generation
- **Write Operations**: Batch transaction posting, interest calculations, balance updates
- **Access Mode**: Sequential access optimized for throughput
- **Exclusivity**: Files closed for online access via CLOSEFIL.jcl

**Batch-Online Coordination**:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Online as CICS Online (Read/Write)
    participant Batch as Batch Jobs (Read/Write)
    participant Files as VSAM Files
    
    Note over Online,Files: Normal Online Operation (06:00-22:00)
    Online->>Files: Random READ/WRITE
    Online->>Files: Concurrent updates with locking
    
    Note over Online: End of Day (22:00)
    Online->>Files: CLOSEFIL.jcl - Files CLOSED
    Note over Online: Online writes suspended
    
    Note over Batch,Files: Batch Window (22:00-06:00)
    Batch->>Files: Sequential READ (full file scan)
    Batch->>Files: Direct WRITE (transaction posting)
    Batch->>Files: REWRITE (balance updates)
    
    Note over Batch: Batch Complete (06:00)
    Batch->>Files: OPENFIL.jcl - Files OPEN
    
    Note over Online,Files: Resume Online Operation
    Online->>Files: Random READ/WRITE
```

**No Read Replica Architecture**:

Traditional read/write splitting would require:
- Master dataset for write operations
- Replica datasets for read operations
- Asynchronous replication lag
- Read consistency challenges

**VSAM Sharing Options** (from LISTCAT.txt):

**SHAREOPTIONS(2,3)**:
- **Cross-Region Sharing**: Multiple CICS regions can share same file
- **Cross-System Sharing**: Multiple z/OS systems can share same file
- **Serialization**: Global Resource Serialization (GRS) manages concurrent access
- **Use Case**: Multi-region CICS Parallel Sysplex configurations

CardDemo employs single-region configuration, so SHAREOPTIONS remain unused.

#### 6.2.5.5 Batch Processing Approach

CardDemo implements comprehensive batch processing optimizations leveraging sequential access patterns and job parallelization:

**Sequential Access Optimization**

Batch programs use COBOL sequential access mode for maximum throughput:

```cobol
* File definition optimized for batch
SELECT TRANSACT-FILE ASSIGN TO TRANSACT
    ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED
    ACCESS MODE  IS SEQUENTIAL
    RECORD KEY   IS TRAN-ID
    FILE STATUS  IS FILE-STATUS.

PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    * Open for sequential read
    OPEN INPUT TRANSACT-FILE
    
    * VSAM read-ahead loads multiple CIs
    PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE
       READ TRANSACT-FILE INTO TRAN-RECORD
       AT END
          SET END-OF-FILE TO TRUE
       NOT AT END
          * Process record
          ADD TRAN-AMT TO DAILY-TOTAL
       END-READ
    END-PERFORM
    
    CLOSE TRANSACT-FILE
```

**Performance Characteristics**:
- **Read-Ahead**: VSAM pre-fetches multiple control intervals
- **Large Buffers**: BUFSPACE=37376 bytes supports 2+ CIs in memory
- **No Index Overhead**: Sequential scan bypasses index traversal
- **Throughput**: 10,000-50,000 records/second depending on record size

**Job Parallelization**

Batch window employs sequential job execution for data consistency:

**POSTTRAN.jcl → INTCALC.jcl → CREASTMT.jcl → TRANBKP.jcl**

**Parallel Opportunities** (not currently implemented):

Multiple independent batch streams could execute concurrently:
- **Stream 1**: Transaction posting + interest calculation
- **Stream 2**: Report generation (read-only access)
- **Stream 3**: File backup (read-only REPRO operations)

**Dependency Management**:

```jcl
//POSTTRAN JOB ...
//STEP1    EXEC PGM=CBTRN02C
//TRANSIN  DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DALYTRAN.KSDS,DISP=SHR
//TRANSOUT DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.KSDS,DISP=OLD
//ACCTFILE DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.ACCTDATA.KSDS,DISP=OLD
/*

//INTCALC  JOB ...
//STEP1    EXEC PGM=CBACT02C,COND=(0,NE,POSTTRAN.STEP1)
//ACCTFILE DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.ACCTDATA.KSDS,DISP=OLD
/*
```

**COND Parameter**: INTCALC executes only if POSTTRAN completes successfully (RC=0).

**DFSORT Optimization**

COMBTRAN.jcl uses DFSORT for efficient file merging:

```jcl
//COMBTRAN JOB ...
//SORT     EXEC PGM=SORT
//SORTIN01 DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.KSDS,DISP=SHR
//SORTIN02 DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DALYTRAN.KSDS,DISP=SHR
//SORTOUT  DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.COMBTRAN.PS,DISP=(NEW,CATLG)
//SYSIN    DD *
  SORT FIELDS=(1,16,CH,A)       * Sort by transaction ID ascending
  SUM FIELDS=NONE                * Remove duplicate keys
/*
```

**DFSORT Efficiency**:
- **In-Memory Sort**: Operates in memory when possible
- **Merge Algorithm**: Efficient multi-way merge for large files
- **Duplicate Elimination**: SUM FIELDS=NONE removes duplicate transaction IDs

**Batch Buffer Tuning**

Batch COBOL programs can specify larger buffers via RESERVE clause:

```cobol
SELECT TRANSACT-FILE ASSIGN TO TRANSACT
    ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED
    ACCESS MODE  IS SEQUENTIAL
    RESERVE 10 AREAS.  * Allocate 10 buffer areas
```

**Performance Impact**: Larger buffer count reduces I/O wait time by pre-fetching more data.

**Free Space Management for Batch Inserts**

VSAM free space percentages optimize batch insert performance:

| File | Update Frequency | FREESPACE-%CI | FREESPACE-%CA | Insert Pattern |
|------|-----------------|---------------|---------------|----------------|
| USRSEC | High (frequent inserts) | 10% | 15% | Random inserts during admin operations |
| CUSTDATA | Low (rare inserts) | 0% | 0% | Bulk load during initialization |
| TRANSACT | Medium (nightly batch) | 5% | 10% | Daily batch posting inserts |

**Free Space Impact**:
- **0% Free Space**: Maximizes storage efficiency but causes CI/CA splits during inserts
- **10-15% Free Space**: Reserves space for inserts, minimizing splits and reorganization overhead

## 6.3 Integration Architecture

### 6.3.1 Overview

#### 6.3.1.1 Applicability Statement

**Traditional external integration architecture is not applicable for this system.**

CardDemo implements an **intentionally isolated, self-contained mainframe application** architecture without external system dependencies typically found in production enterprise environments. This architectural decision was deliberate to support the system's primary mission as a demonstration and testing platform for mainframe migration and modernization initiatives.

The application **does not** implement:

- REST APIs, SOAP web services, GraphQL interfaces, or gRPC services
- External message queue integrations (MQ Series, Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS)
- Third-party API connections (payment processors, credit bureaus, fraud detection services)
- FTP/SFTP file transfer interfaces
- External relational or NoSQL database systems (DB2, IMS, PostgreSQL, MongoDB)
- API gateways or service mesh architectures
- Event streaming platforms or distributed messaging brokers
- Legacy system adapters or ESB (Enterprise Service Bus) integrations

As documented in the system overview, CardDemo operates as an isolated system with single-region CICS deployment, terminal-based user interface, and file-based persistence, representing authentic mainframe application patterns while eliminating environmental dependencies that would complicate demonstration and testing scenarios.

#### 6.3.1.2 Integration Architecture Purpose

While CardDemo excludes external system integrations, it demonstrates comprehensive **internal integration patterns** that are foundational to mainframe application architectures. These patterns represent the integration mechanisms observed in production mainframe environments and serve as reference implementations for:

**Migration Tool Validation**: Testing automated migration tools' ability to transform mainframe integration patterns into cloud-native equivalents (e.g., TDQ to SQS, COMMAREA to distributed session state, VSAM to relational databases)

**Modernization Planning**: Understanding existing integration touchpoints that require adaptation when moving from monolithic mainframe to distributed cloud architectures

**Educational Demonstrations**: Showcasing authentic mainframe integration techniques including terminal protocols, program control, file coordination, and asynchronous messaging

**Platform Integration**: Demonstrating execution on AWS Mainframe Modernization service with runtime platform mappings (CICS to AWS M2, VSAM to cloud storage, JCL to batch orchestration)

### 6.3.2 Internal Integration Patterns

#### 6.3.2.1 Pattern Classification

CardDemo implements seven distinct internal integration patterns that enable communication between system components without external dependencies:

| Integration Pattern | Type | Protocol/Mechanism | Synchronicity | Primary Use Case |
|-------------------|------|-------------------|---------------|------------------|
| 3270 Terminal Protocol | User Interface | TN3270 over TCP/IP | Synchronous | Terminal-based data entry and display |
| CICS Transaction Processing | Business Logic Orchestration | EXEC CICS API | Synchronous | Transaction routing and execution |
| COMMAREA Communication | Inter-Program | In-memory data structure | In-process | Session state and context preservation |
| Transient Data Queue (TDQ) | Asynchronous Messaging | CICS TDQ WRITEQ | Asynchronous | Online-to-batch job submission |
| VSAM File I/O | Data Layer Access | CICS File Control | Synchronous | Persistent data operations |
| Batch-Online Coordination | Resource Serialization | File closure protocol | Scheduled | File access arbitration |
| BMS Map Processing | Presentation Layer | BMS Screen Definition | Synchronous | Screen layout and field mapping |

    style LINK fill:#FFF4E1
    style COMMAREA fill:#E8F5E9
    style TDQ fill:#FFE1CC

    style COORD fill:#FFB6C1
```

### 6.3.3 Terminal Integration Architecture

#### 6.3.3.1 3270 Terminal Protocol

CardDemo implements terminal-based user interface integration through the **3270 terminal protocol**, representing the standard mainframe human-interface mechanism used across financial services, insurance, government, and enterprise sectors for decades.

**Protocol Characteristics**:

- **Data Stream Format**: Fixed 24×80 character grid transmitted as structured field data
- **Transport Protocols**: TN3270 over TCP/IP (modern) or VTAM SNA (traditional z/OS)
- **Communication Pattern**: Synchronous block-mode transmission (entire screen transmitted per interaction)
- **Field Attributes**: Protected/unprotected, numeric/alphanumeric, highlighted/normal, color specifications
- **Attention Identifiers**: Enter key, PF1-PF24 function keys, PA1-PA3 program attention keys, Clear key

**Integration Flow**:

| Step | Component | Action | Protocol Detail |
|------|-----------|--------|-----------------|
| 1. User Input | Terminal Emulator | User enters data in unprotected fields and presses Enter or PF key | Modified data only transmitted to reduce bandwidth |
| 2. Data Transmission | TN3270 Protocol | 3270 data stream transmitted to CICS Transaction Server | Binary-encoded field addresses and data |
| 3. CICS Routing | CICS Terminal Manager | Routes data stream to appropriate transaction based on TRANSID | TRANSID associated with previous RETURN command |
| 4. BMS Processing | CICS/BMS Subsystem | Translates 3270 data stream into COBOL copybook structure | Symbolic map (AI suffix) populated in working storage |

**Terminal Integration Diagram**:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as User<br/>3270 Terminal Emulator
    participant TN3270 as TN3270 Protocol<br/>TCP/IP Transport
    participant CICS as CICS Transaction Server<br/>Terminal Manager
    participant BMS as BMS Subsystem<br/>Map Processor
    participant Program as COBOL Program<br/>e.g., COACTUPC
    
    Note over User: User views screen<br/>COACTVW (Account View)
    User->>User: Enter data in<br/>unprotected fields
    User->>User: Press Enter or PF key
    
    User->>TN3270: 3270 Data Stream<br/>Modified fields only<br/>EIBAID = attention ID
    
    TN3270->>CICS: Route to TRANSID<br/>ACUP (Account Update)
    
    Note over CICS: Allocate CICS task<br/>Load program COACTUPC<br/>Check COMMAREA presence
    
    CICS->>BMS: RECEIVE MAP request
    
    BMS->>BMS: Parse 3270 data stream<br/>Extract field data<br/>Populate symbolic map
    
    BMS->>Program: Symbolic map (AI)<br/>Input fields in working storage
    
    Note over Program: Field validation<br/>Business logic<br/>VSAM file operations
    
    Program->>BMS: SEND MAP request<br/>Populate output map (AO)
    
    BMS->>BMS: Format 3270 data stream<br/>Field attributes<br/>Cursor positioning
    
    BMS->>CICS: Formatted screen data
    
    CICS->>TN3270: 3270 Data Stream<br/>Complete screen layout
    
    TN3270->>User: Display updated screen<br/>Cursor at designated field
    
    Program->>CICS: RETURN TRANSID COMMAREA<br/>Terminate task<br/>Preserve session state
    
    Note over CICS: Task terminated<br/>COMMAREA preserved<br/>Await next Enter key
```

#### 6.3.3.2 BMS Map Integration

**Basic Mapping Support (BMS)** provides the contract between 3270 terminal devices and COBOL application programs through screen definition macros and generated copybooks.

**BMS Components**:

- **Mapsets**: 17 BMS mapset definitions in `app/bms/` directory (COSGN00.bms, COMEN01.bms, COACTVW.bms, etc.)
- **Physical Maps**: Compiled load modules containing screen layout instructions for CICS
- **Symbolic Maps**: COBOL copybooks in `app/cpy-bms/` defining input/output field structures
- **Map Operations**: EXEC CICS SEND MAP (output to terminal) and EXEC CICS RECEIVE MAP (input from terminal)

**BMS Map Structure**:

| Component | Purpose | Example |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| DFHMSD | Mapset definition macro | Defines mapset name, control attributes, storage mode |
| DFHMDI | Map definition macro | Defines screen size (24×80), line/column positioning |
| DFHMDF | Field definition macro | Defines individual field attributes (position, length, initial value, attributes) |

**Map Processing Flow**:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Design Time"
        BMSSRC[BMS Source<br/>COACTVW.bms<br/>DFHMSD/DFHMDI/DFHMDF]
        ASMA90[ASMA90 Assembler<br/>BMS Compilation]
        PHYSMAP[Physical Map<br/>Load Module<br/>Screen Definition]
        IEBGENER[IEBGENER Copy<br/>Copybook Generation]
        SYMBMAP[Symbolic Map<br/>COBOL Copybook<br/>COACTVWI.cpy]
    end
    
    subgraph "Runtime"
        COBOL[COBOL Program<br/>COACTVWC.cbl<br/>COPY COACTVWI]
        SENDMAP[EXEC CICS SEND MAP<br/>FROM symbolic-map-output]
        CICS_BMS[CICS BMS Subsystem<br/>Map Formatter]
        RECVMAP[EXEC CICS RECEIVE MAP<br/>INTO symbolic-map-input]
        TERMINAL[3270 Terminal<br/>Screen Display]
    end
    
    BMSSRC -->|Assemble| ASMA90
    ASMA90 -->|Generate| PHYSMAP
    ASMA90 -->|Generate| IEBGENER
    IEBGENER -->|Generate| SYMBMAP
    
    SYMBMAP -->|COPY Statement| COBOL
    COBOL -->|Invoke| SENDMAP
    SENDMAP -->|Use| PHYSMAP
    SENDMAP -->|Format| CICS_BMS
    CICS_BMS -->|Transmit| TERMINAL
    TERMINAL -->|Input| CICS_BMS
    CICS_BMS -->|Parse| RECVMAP
    RECVMAP -->|Populate| COBOL
    
    style BMSSRC fill:#E1F5FF
    style PHYSMAP fill:#FFF4E1
    style SYMBMAP fill:#FFF4E1
    style COBOL fill:#E8F5E9
    style TERMINAL fill:#F3E5F5
```

**Example Field Integration**:

For account number field in COACTVW map:

```
* BMS Field Definition (COACTVW.bms)
         DFHMDF POS=(03,15),LENGTH=11,ATTRB=(UNPROT,NUM),
                INITIAL='___________'

* Generated Symbolic Map Input (COACTVWI.cpy)
         05 ACCTIDL    PIC S9(4) COMP.    * Length entered
         05 ACCTIDF    PIC X.             * Flag byte
         05 ACCTIDI    PIC X(11).         * Input data

* Generated Symbolic Map Output (COACTVWO.cpy)
         05 ACCTIDL    PIC S9(4) COMP.    * Length to display
         05 ACCTIDF    PIC X.             * Attribute byte
         05 ACCTIDO    PIC X(11).         * Output data

* COBOL Program Usage (COACTVWC.cbl)
         EXEC CICS RECEIVE MAP('COACTVW')
              MAPSET('COACTVW')
              INTO(COACTVWI)
         END-EXEC
         
         MOVE ACCTIDI TO WS-ACCT-ID    * Extract user input
```

### 6.3.4 Transaction Processing Integration

#### 6.3.4.1 CICS Transaction Router

**CICS Transaction Server** provides the runtime environment and integration hub for all online programs, managing transaction routing, program control, resource allocation, and context preservation.

**Transaction Integration Components**:

| Component | Function | Integration Mechanism |
|-----------|----------|----------------------|
| TRANSID | 4-character transaction identifier | Associates terminal input with specific program |
| Program Control | XCTL (transfer control) and LINK (call/return) | Enables inter-program navigation and subroutine invocation |
| COMMAREA | Communication area (maximum 32KB) | Preserves session state across pseudo-conversational transactions |
| Task Management | CICS task allocation and scheduling | Manages concurrent transaction execution with resource pooling |

**Transaction Flow**:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as User Terminal
    participant CICS as CICS Transaction Server
    participant Menu as COMEN01C<br/>Main Menu
    participant AccountView as COACTVWC<br/>Account View
    participant AccountUpdate as COACTUPC<br/>Account Update
    participant COMMAREA as COMMAREA<br/>Session State
    participant VSAM as VSAM Files
    
    User->>CICS: Sign-on complete<br/>TRANSID=MN01
    CICS->>Menu: Invoke COMEN01C<br/>EIBCALEN=0 (initial)
    Menu->>Menu: Display main menu<br/>Populate option list
    Menu->>CICS: SEND MAP + RETURN<br/>TRANSID=MN01
    CICS->>User: Display menu screen
    
    User->>CICS: Select option 1<br/>Press Enter
    CICS->>Menu: Invoke COMEN01C<br/>EIBCALEN > 0
    Menu->>Menu: RECEIVE MAP<br/>Evaluate selection
    Menu->>COMMAREA: Populate context<br/>FROM-TRANID=MN01<br/>TO-TRANID=ACTV
    Menu->>CICS: XCTL PROGRAM(COACTVWC)<br/>COMMAREA passed
    
    Note over CICS: Release Menu program<br/>Transfer control
    
    CICS->>AccountView: Invoke COACTVWC<br/>EIBCALEN > 0
    AccountView->>COMMAREA: Read context<br/>Extract FROM-TRANID
    AccountView->>AccountView: Display blank screen<br/>for account ID entry
    AccountView->>CICS: SEND MAP + RETURN<br/>TRANSID=ACTV
    CICS->>User: Display account view screen
    
    User->>CICS: Enter account ID<br/>Press PF2 for update
    CICS->>AccountView: Invoke COACTVWC<br/>EIBCALEN > 0
    AccountView->>AccountView: RECEIVE MAP<br/>Evaluate EIBAID=DFHPF2
    AccountView->>VSAM: READ ACCTFILE<br/>Retrieve account record
    VSAM->>AccountView: Account data
    AccountView->>COMMAREA: Store ACCT-ID<br/>Update TO-TRANID=ACUP
    AccountView->>CICS: XCTL PROGRAM(COACTUPC)<br/>COMMAREA passed
    
    CICS->>AccountUpdate: Invoke COACTUPC<br/>EIBCALEN > 0
    AccountUpdate->>COMMAREA: Read ACCT-ID
    AccountUpdate->>VSAM: READ UPDATE ACCTFILE<br/>Acquire exclusive lock
    VSAM->>AccountUpdate: Locked account record
    AccountUpdate->>AccountUpdate: Display account data<br/>Allow field modifications
    AccountUpdate->>CICS: SEND MAP + RETURN<br/>TRANSID=ACUP
    CICS->>User: Display update screen
    
    User->>CICS: Modify fields<br/>Press Enter
    CICS->>AccountUpdate: Invoke COACTUPC<br/>EIBCALEN > 0
    AccountUpdate->>AccountUpdate: RECEIVE MAP<br/>Validate fields
    AccountUpdate->>VSAM: REWRITE ACCTFILE<br/>Update record
    VSAM->>AccountUpdate: Update successful
    AccountUpdate->>AccountUpdate: Display success message
    AccountUpdate->>COMMAREA: Update result code
    AccountUpdate->>CICS: SEND MAP + RETURN<br/>TRANSID=ACUP
    CICS->>User: Display confirmation
```

#### 6.3.4.2 COMMAREA Session State Integration

The **COMMAREA (Communication Area)** pattern implements stateful session management within CICS's pseudo-conversational architecture, preserving user context, navigation state, and business payload across terminal interactions.

**COMMAREA Structure** (defined in `app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy`):

| Field Group | Fields | Purpose |
|-------------|--------|---------|
| Navigation Context | CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, CDEMO-TO-TRANID, CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM | Transaction routing and back-navigation support |
| User Authentication | CDEMO-USER-ID, CDEMO-USER-TYPE, CDEMO-USRFNAME, CDEMO-USRLNAME | Authenticated user identity and authorization level |
| Business Payload | CDEMO-CUST-ID, CDEMO-ACCT-ID, CDEMO-CARD-NUM, CDEMO-TRAN-ID | Entity identifiers for transaction context |
| Pagination State | CDEMO-ACCT-PAGE-NUM, CDEMO-CARD-PAGE-NUM, CDEMO-TRAN-PAGE-NUM | List browsing position tracking |

**COMMAREA Integration Pattern**:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start[Program Initialization<br/>EIBCALEN > 0?] -->|Yes| ReadCOMMArea[Read COMMAREA<br/>LINKAGE SECTION<br/>CARDDEMO-COMMAREA]
    Start -->|No| InitCOMMArea[Initialize COMMAREA<br/>Set default values<br/>First transaction]
    
    ReadCOMMArea --> ExtractContext[Extract Session Context<br/>USER-ID, USER-TYPE<br/>FROM-TRANID, FROM-PROGRAM]
    InitCOMMArea --> ExtractContext
    
    ExtractContext --> CheckAuth{User<br/>Authenticated?}
    CheckAuth -->|No| ReturnSignOn[XCTL to COSGN00C<br/>Sign-on required]
    CheckAuth -->|Yes| CheckAuth2{User Type<br/>Authorized?}
    
    CheckAuth2 -->|Admin Only Function<br/>USER-TYPE != 'A'| DisplayError[Display unauthorized<br/>message]
    CheckAuth2 -->|Authorized| BusinessLogic[Execute Business Logic<br/>File operations<br/>Calculations]
    
    BusinessLogic --> UpdateCOMMArea[Update COMMAREA<br/>Set TO-TRANID<br/>Store business data<br/>Update page numbers]
    DisplayError --> UpdateCOMMArea
    
    UpdateCOMMArea --> SendScreen[SEND MAP<br/>Display results]
    
    SendScreen --> ReturnChoice{Navigation<br/>Decision}
    
    ReturnChoice -->|Same Transaction| ReturnSame[EXEC CICS RETURN<br/>TRANSID current<br/>COMMAREA preserved]
    ReturnChoice -->|Different Transaction| XCTLNext[EXEC CICS XCTL<br/>PROGRAM target<br/>COMMAREA passed]
    ReturnChoice -->|Menu Return| XCTLMenu[EXEC CICS XCTL<br/>PROGRAM FROM-PROGRAM<br/>COMMAREA passed]
    
    ReturnSame --> WaitUser[CICS Preserves COMMAREA<br/>Wait for Enter key]
    XCTLNext --> NextProgram[Target Program Invoked<br/>COMMAREA available]
    XCTLMenu --> MenuProgram[Menu Program Invoked<br/>Navigation context restored]
    ReturnSignOn --> SignOn[Sign-on Program<br/>Authentication flow]
    
    WaitUser -->|User presses Enter| Start
    
    style Start fill:#E1F5FF
    style ReadCOMMArea fill:#FFF4E1
    style InitCOMMArea fill:#FFF4E1
    style UpdateCOMMArea fill:#E8F5E9
    style ReturnSame fill:#FFE1CC
    style XCTLNext fill:#FFE1CC
    style XCTLMenu fill:#FFE1CC
```

**COMMAREA Benefits for Integration**:

- **State Preservation**: User context persists across multiple transactions without server-side session storage
- **Resource Efficiency**: Eliminates long-running CICS tasks; each terminal interaction creates new task with preserved context
- **Back-Navigation**: FROM-TRANID enables PF3 return-to-previous-screen functionality
- **Security Context**: USER-ID and USER-TYPE propagate through all transactions for authorization enforcement
- **Entity Context**: Business identifiers (ACCT-ID, CARD-NUM) available across related functions without re-entry

#### 6.3.4.3 Program Control Integration

**EXEC CICS XCTL** (Transfer Control) and **EXEC CICS LINK** (Call and Return) provide program-to-program integration within the CICS region.

**Integration Comparison**:

| Aspect | XCTL (Transfer Control) | LINK (Call and Return) |
|--------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Purpose | Navigation between functions | Subroutine invocation |
| Control Flow | Caller released, target executes | Caller suspended, returns after subroutine |
| COMMAREA | Passed to target program | Passed as parameter area |
| Storage | Caller's storage released | Caller's storage retained |
| Use Cases | Menu-to-function, function-to-function navigation | Utility functions, centralized I/O routines |

**XCTL Integration Example** (Menu to Account View):

```
* COMEN01C (Main Menu) - User selects account option
         EVALUATE EIBAID
            WHEN DFHENTER
               IF OPTN-ID = '1'
                  MOVE 'MN01' TO CDEMO-FROM-TRANID
                  MOVE 'COMEN01C' TO CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM
                  MOVE 'ACTV' TO CDEMO-TO-TRANID
                  MOVE 'COACTVWC' TO CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM
                  
                  EXEC CICS XCTL
                       PROGRAM('COACTVWC')
                       COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA)
                  END-EXEC
               END-IF
         END-EVALUATE
```

**LINK Integration Example** (Statement Generator calling I/O Subroutine):

```
* CBSTM03A (Statement Generator) - Calls file I/O utility
         MOVE 'READ-ACCOUNT' TO IO-FUNCTION
         MOVE ACCT-ID TO IO-ACCT-ID
         
         EXEC CICS LINK
              PROGRAM('CBSTM03B')
              COMMAREA(IO-LINKAGE-AREA)
              LENGTH(LENGTH OF IO-LINKAGE-AREA)
         END-EXEC
         
         IF IO-RESPONSE = 'SUCCESS'
            MOVE IO-ACCT-RECORD TO WS-ACCOUNT-RECORD
            PERFORM GENERATE-STATEMENT-LINE
         ELSE
            PERFORM HANDLE-IO-ERROR
         END-IF
```

### 6.3.5 Asynchronous Messaging Integration

#### 6.3.5.1 Transient Data Queue (TDQ) Architecture

The **Transient Data Queue (TDQ)** mechanism provides asynchronous integration between online transaction processing and batch job submission, representing mainframe-native message queuing without external messaging infrastructure.

**TDQ Integration Components**:

- **Queue Name**: 'JOBS' (intrapartition or extrapartition TDQ configured in CICS CSD)
- **Producer**: CORPT00C (online report request program)
- **Message Format**: JCL text records (80-byte fixed-length records)
- **Consumer**: JES (Job Entry Subsystem) via CICS automatic trigger
- **Message Flow**: Synchronous write from online program → Asynchronous job submission to JES

**TDQ Implementation** (from `app/cbl/CORPT00C.cbl` lines 517-523):

```
* Online program writes JCL to TDQ for batch execution
         EXEC CICS WRITEQ TD
              QUEUE('JOBS')
              FROM(JCL-RECORD)
              LENGTH(LENGTH OF JCL-RECORD)
              RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
         END-EXEC
         
         EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD
            WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL)
               MOVE 'Report request submitted' TO WS-MESSAGE
               PERFORM SEND-TRNRPT-SCREEN
            WHEN OTHER
               MOVE 'Unable to Write TDQ (JOBS)...' TO WS-MESSAGE
               PERFORM SEND-TRNRPT-SCREEN
         END-EVALUATE
```

**TDQ Message Flow Diagram**:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as User Terminal
    participant Online as CORPT00C<br/>Online Report Request
    participant TDQ as Transient Data Queue<br/>Queue: JOBS
    participant CICS_TM as CICS Trigger Monitor
    participant JES as Job Entry Subsystem<br/>z/OS JES2/JES3
    participant Batch as Batch Report Program<br/>RPTSGEN.jcl
    participant VSAM as VSAM Files<br/>TRANSACT, ACCTFILE
    participant Output as Report Output<br/>SYSOUT Dataset
    
    User->>Online: Select report option<br/>Enter date range<br/>Press Enter
    
    Online->>Online: Validate date range<br/>Generate JCL text<br/>//RPTSGEN JOB...<br/>//STEP1 EXEC PGM=...
    
    Note over Online: Build 80-byte<br/>JCL records
    
    loop For each JCL record
        Online->>TDQ: EXEC CICS WRITEQ TD<br/>QUEUE('JOBS')<br/>FROM(JCL-RECORD)
        TDQ->>TDQ: Append record to queue<br/>Check trigger threshold
    end
    
    Online->>User: Display confirmation<br/>"Report request submitted"<br/>RETURN TRANSID
    
    Note over TDQ: Queue threshold reached<br/>or CEMT TRIGGER issued
    
    TDQ->>CICS_TM: Trigger event<br/>Queue 'JOBS' ready
    
    CICS_TM->>JES: Submit JCL from TDQ<br/>to Internal Reader
    
    Note over JES: Job queued<br/>Awaiting execution<br/>based on CLASS priority
    
    JES->>Batch: Execute RPTSGEN job<br/>Allocate files<br/>Invoke report program
    
    Batch->>VSAM: Sequential READ<br/>TRANSACT file<br/>Filter by date range
    
    VSAM->>Batch: Transaction records
    
    Batch->>VSAM: Random READ<br/>ACCTFILE<br/>Retrieve account details
    
    VSAM->>Batch: Account records
    
    Batch->>Batch: Format report lines<br/>Calculate totals<br/>Generate summary
    
    Batch->>Output: WRITE SYSOUT<br/>Report output
    
    Output->>Output: Spool to hold queue<br/>Awaiting print/view
    
    Note over JES: Job complete<br/>CC 0000 (success)
    
    Note over User: User views SYSOUT<br/>via SDSF or equivalent
```

#### 6.3.5.2 TDQ Configuration

**TDQ Types for Integration**:

| TDQ Type | Definition Location | Destination | Use Case |
|----------|-------------------|-------------|----------|
| Intrapartition TDQ | CICS CSD | CICS-managed storage | Inter-transaction messaging within CICS region |
| Extrapartition TDQ | CICS CSD + DCT | z/OS dataset or JES spool | External system integration (JCL submission, logging) |

**Expected JOBS Queue Configuration** (not present in repository but implied by CORPT00C implementation):

```
DEFINE TDQUEUE(JOBS)
       GROUP(CARDDEMO)
       TYPE(EXTRA)
       DESTID(JESINTR)
       TRIGGERLEVEL(1)
       DESCRIPTION('JCL submission queue for batch reports')
```

**TDQ Trigger Mechanism**:

- **TRIGGERLEVEL**: Number of records that trigger automatic processing (e.g., TRIGGERLEVEL=1 submits job after single JCL stream written)
- **DESTID**: Destination identifier linking TDQ to JES internal reader
- **Automatic Submission**: CICS monitors queue depth and triggers JES submission when threshold reached
- **Manual Trigger**: Operator can issue `CEMT SET TDQUEUE(JOBS) TRIGGER` for immediate processing

#### 6.3.5.3 Message Processing Error Handling

**Producer-Side Error Handling**:

| Error Condition | RESP Code | Recovery Action |
|-----------------|-----------|-----------------|
| Queue full | DFHRESP(QIDERR) | Display error message, request user retry later |
| Queue disabled | DFHRESP(DISABLED) | Display "Service temporarily unavailable" |
| Authorization failure | DFHRESP(NOTAUTH) | Display "Insufficient privileges" |
| Queue not defined | DFHRESP(QIDERR) | Log error, initiate CICS operator notification |

**Consumer-Side Processing**:

- **JES Validation**: JCL syntax validation before job submission
- **Job Failure Handling**: JES condition codes propagated to output logs for operator review
- **Resubmission**: Failed jobs can be resubmitted manually by correcting JCL and reissuing
- **No Automatic Retry**: TDQ messages are consumed once; failures require manual intervention (demonstration limitation)

### 6.3.6 Batch-Online Integration

#### 6.3.6.1 File Coordination Pattern

CardDemo implements **temporal segregation** for batch-online file access coordination, preventing concurrent access conflicts through explicit file closure and reopening protocols.

**Coordination Architecture**:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Sched as Scheduler<br/>Automated or Manual
    participant Online as CICS Online Region<br/>16 Programs
    participant Close as CLOSEFIL.jcl<br/>File Quiesce Job
    participant Post as POSTTRAN.jcl<br/>Transaction Posting
    participant Int as INTCALC.jcl<br/>Interest Calculation
    participant Stmt as CREASTMT.jcl<br/>Statement Generation
    participant Backup as TRANBKP.jcl<br/>File Backup
    participant Open as OPENFIL.jcl<br/>File Resume Job
    participant Files as VSAM Files<br/>13 KSDS Datasets
    
    Note over Sched,Files: Day 1 - Normal Online Operations (06:00-22:00)
    
    Online->>Files: Concurrent READ/WRITE<br/>Multiple users<br/>Record-level locking
    
    Note over Sched: End-of-Day Trigger<br/>22:00 daily schedule
    
    Sched->>Close: Submit CLOSEFIL.jcl<br/>JES job submission
    
    Close->>Online: CEMT SET FILE(CUSTFILE) CLOSED<br/>CEMT SET FILE(ACCTFILE) CLOSED<br/>CEMT SET FILE(CARDFILE) CLOSED<br/>CEMT SET FILE(XREFFILE) CLOSED<br/>CEMT SET FILE(TRANSACT) CLOSED<br/>CEMT SET FILE(DALYTRAN) CLOSED<br/>CEMT SET FILE(DISCGRP) CLOSED<br/>CEMT SET FILE(TRANTYPE) CLOSED<br/>CEMT SET FILE(TRANCATG) CLOSED<br/>CEMT SET FILE(TCATBALF) CLOSED
    
    Note over Online: Files marked CLOSED<br/>New file I/O requests fail<br/>In-flight tasks complete
    
    Online->>Files: Pending operations complete<br/>Buffers flushed<br/>Locks released
    
    Note over Files: Files quiesced<br/>No online access
    
    Close-->>Sched: CC 0000 (success)
    
    Note over Sched,Files: Batch Window Begins (22:00-06:00)
    
    Sched->>Post: Submit POSTTRAN.jcl<br/>COND=(0,NE)
    
    Post->>Files: OPEN INPUT DALYTRAN<br/>OPEN I-O ACCTFILE<br/>OPEN I-O TRANSACT<br/>OPEN OUTPUT DALYREJS(+1)
    
    Files->>Post: Files opened<br/>Exclusive access granted
    
    Note over Post: Process daily transactions<br/>Sequential read DALYTRAN<br/>Direct update ACCTFILE<br/>Direct write TRANSACT<br/>Write rejects to GDG
    
    Post->>Files: CLOSE all files
    
    Post-->>Sched: CC 0000 (success)
    
    Sched->>Int: Submit INTCALC.jcl<br/>COND=(0,NE,POST.STEP1)
    
    Int->>Files: OPEN I-O ACCTFILE<br/>OPEN INPUT DISCGRP
    
    Note over Int: Calculate interest<br/>Sequential read accounts<br/>Update balances<br/>Apply APR rates
    
    Int->>Files: CLOSE all files
    
    Int-->>Sched: CC 0000 (success)
    
    Sched->>Stmt: Submit CREASTMT.jcl<br/>COND=(0,NE,INT.STEP1)
    
    Stmt->>Files: OPEN INPUT ACCTFILE<br/>OPEN INPUT TRANSACT<br/>OPEN OUTPUT statements
    
    Note over Stmt: Generate statements<br/>Browse transactions<br/>Aggregate by category<br/>Format HTML/text
    
    Stmt->>Files: CLOSE all files
    
    Stmt-->>Sched: CC 0000 (success)
    
    Sched->>Backup: Submit TRANBKP.jcl<br/>COND=(0,NE,STMT.STEP1)
    
    Backup->>Files: REPRO INFILE(TRANSACT)<br/>OUTFILE(TRANSACT.BKUP(+1))
    
    Note over Backup: Create GDG generation<br/>Point-in-time backup
    
    Backup->>Files: REPRO complete<br/>New generation cataloged
    
    Backup-->>Sched: CC 0000 (success)
    
    Note over Sched,Files: Batch Window Complete
    
    Sched->>Open: Submit OPENFIL.jcl
    
    Open->>Online: CEMT SET FILE(CUSTFILE) OPEN<br/>CEMT SET FILE(ACCTFILE) OPEN<br/>CEMT SET FILE(CARDFILE) OPEN<br/>CEMT SET FILE(XREFFILE) OPEN<br/>CEMT SET FILE(TRANSACT) OPEN<br/>CEMT SET FILE(DALYTRAN) OPEN<br/>CEMT SET FILE(DISCGRP) OPEN<br/>CEMT SET FILE(TRANTYPE) OPEN<br/>CEMT SET FILE(TRANCATG) OPEN<br/>CEMT SET FILE(TCATBALF) OPEN
    
    Note over Online: Files marked OPEN<br/>Online transactions resume
    
    Open-->>Sched: CC 0000 (success)
    
    Note over Sched,Files: Day 2 - Normal Online Operations Resume (06:00)
    
    Online->>Files: Concurrent READ/WRITE<br/>With updated balances<br/>and posted transactions
```

#### 6.3.6.2 File Closure Protocol

**CLOSEFIL.jcl Implementation** (referenced in README.md and Section 6.1.3.2):

```
//CLOSEFIL JOB CLASS=A,MSGCLASS=H,NOTIFY=&SYSUID
//STEP1    EXEC PGM=DFHCSDUP
//STEPLIB  DD DSN=CICSTS56.CICS.SDFHLOAD,DISP=SHR
//DFHCSD   DD DSN=CICS.CARDDEMO.DFHCSD,DISP=SHR
//SYSPRINT DD SYSOUT=*
//SYSIN    DD *
  CEMT SET FILE(CUSTFILE) CLOSED
  CEMT SET FILE(ACCTFILE) CLOSED
  CEMT SET FILE(CARDFILE) CLOSED
  CEMT SET FILE(XREFFILE) CLOSED
  CEMT SET FILE(TRANSACT) CLOSED
  CEMT SET FILE(DALYTRAN) CLOSED
  CEMT SET FILE(DISCGRP) CLOSED
  CEMT SET FILE(TRANTYPE) CLOSED
  CEMT SET FILE(TRANCATG) CLOSED
  CEMT SET FILE(TCATBALF) CLOSED
/*
```

**File Closure Effects**:

- **Immediate Status Change**: Files marked CLOSED in CICS File Control Table (FCT)
- **New Request Rejection**: Subsequent EXEC CICS READ/WRITE/REWRITE operations receive DFHRESP(DISABLED) response code
- **In-Flight Completion**: Active file operations complete normally before closure takes effect
- **Buffer Flush**: LSR buffer pool writes dirty buffers to VSAM datasets
- **Lock Release**: All record locks released when tasks complete

**OPENFIL.jcl Implementation**:

```
//OPENFIL  JOB CLASS=A,MSGCLASS=H,NOTIFY=&SYSUID
//STEP1    EXEC PGM=DFHCSDUP
//STEPLIB  DD DSN=CICSTS56.CICS.SDFHLOAD,DISP=SHR
//DFHCSD   DD DSN=CICS.CARDDEMO.DFHCSD,DISP=SHR
//SYSPRINT DD SYSOUT=*
//SYSIN    DD *
  CEMT SET FILE(CUSTFILE) OPEN
  CEMT SET FILE(ACCTFILE) OPEN
  CEMT SET FILE(CARDFILE) OPEN
  CEMT SET FILE(XREFFILE) OPEN
  CEMT SET FILE(TRANSACT) OPEN
  CEMT SET FILE(DALYTRAN) OPEN
  CEMT SET FILE(DISCGRP) OPEN
  CEMT SET FILE(TRANTYPE) OPEN
  CEMT SET FILE(TRANCATG) OPEN
  CEMT SET FILE(TCATBALF) OPEN
/*
```

**File Reopening Effects**:

- **Immediate Availability**: Files marked OPEN in FCT
- **Buffer Pool Repopulation**: First read operations populate LSR buffer pool
- **Transaction Resumption**: Online programs resume normal file operations
- **User Experience**: Transactions that previously received "file unavailable" errors now succeed

#### 6.3.6.3 Job Dependency Management

**Batch Job Sequencing** (from README.md lines 165-183):

| Sequence | Job | Predecessor | Condition | Purpose |
|----------|-----|-------------|-----------|---------|
| 1 | CLOSEFIL | None | Always execute | Quiesce files for batch |
| 2 | POSTTRAN | CLOSEFIL | CC=0 | Post daily transactions |
| 3 | INTCALC | POSTTRAN | CC=0 | Calculate interest charges |
| 4 | CREASTMT | INTCALC | CC=0 | Generate account statements |
| 5 | TRANBKP | CREASTMT | CC=0 | Backup transaction files |
| 6 | OPENFIL | TRANBKP | CC=0 | Resume online processing |

**JCL Conditional Execution**:

```
//INTCALC  JOB ...
//STEP1    EXEC PGM=CBACT02C,COND=(0,NE,POSTTRAN.STEP1)
```

**COND Parameter Interpretation**: Execute INTCALC.STEP1 only if POSTTRAN.STEP1 completed with CC=0 (not NE 0)

**Failure Handling**:

- **Abend Propagation**: Job failure prevents subsequent jobs from executing
- **Operator Notification**: JES messages indicate failure point in batch sequence
- **Manual Recovery**: Operator corrects data/JCL, restarts from failed job
- **Incomplete Window**: If batch fails before OPENFIL, online remains suspended until operator intervention

### 6.3.7 Data Layer Integration

#### 6.3.7.1 VSAM File Access Patterns

**CICS File Control** provides the integration layer between application programs and VSAM datasets through standardized EXEC CICS commands.

**File Access Operations**:

| Operation | Command | Integration Purpose | Locking Behavior |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|------------------|
| Direct Read | EXEC CICS READ FILE RIDFLD | Retrieve single record by primary key | Shared lock (allows concurrent reads) |
| Browse Initiation | EXEC CICS STARTBR FILE RIDFLD GTEQ | Position browse cursor for sequential access | Shared lock on position |
| Browse Next | EXEC CICS READNEXT FILE | Retrieve next record in key sequence | Shared lock per record |
| Browse Previous | EXEC CICS READPREV FILE | Retrieve previous record in key sequence | Shared lock per record |
| Browse Termination | EXEC CICS ENDBR FILE | Release browse resources | No lock |
| Record Creation | EXEC CICS WRITE FILE FROM | Insert new record with unique key | Exclusive lock during write |
| Record Update | EXEC CICS READ UPDATE then REWRITE | Modify existing record | Exclusive lock from READ UPDATE to REWRITE |
| Record Deletion | EXEC CICS DELETE FILE RIDFLD | Remove record by primary key | Exclusive lock during delete |

**VSAM Integration Architecture**:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Application Layer"
        PROG1[COACTUPC<br/>Account Update]
        PROG2[COTRN00C<br/>Transaction List]
        PROG3[COBIL00C<br/>Bill Payment]
        PROG4[CBTRN02C<br/>Batch Posting]
    end
    
    subgraph "CICS File Control"
        FC[File Control Module<br/>Command Processor]
        LSR[LSR Buffer Pool 1<br/>2 Data Buffers<br/>1 Index Buffer]
        LOCK[Record Lock Manager<br/>Exclusive/Shared Locks]
    end

#### 6.3.7.2 Cross-Reference Navigation Pattern

The **XREFFILE** provides referential integrity integration without database foreign key constraints, enabling navigation between related entities (customers, accounts, cards).

**Cross-Reference Record Structure** (from `app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy`):

```
01  CARD-XREF-RECORD.
    05  XREF-CARD-NUM           PIC X(16).    * Primary key
    05  XREF-CUST-ID            PIC 9(09).    * Customer ID link
    05  XREF-ACCT-ID            PIC 9(11).    * Account ID link
    05  FILLER                  PIC X(14).
```

**Navigation Integration Flow**:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Entity Access"
        CUST[CUSTFILE<br/>Primary Key: CUST-ID]
        ACCT[ACCTFILE<br/>Primary Key: ACCT-ID]
        CARD[CARDFILE<br/>Primary Key: CARD-NUM]
    end
    
    subgraph "Cross-Reference Integration"
        XREF[XREFFILE<br/>Composite Key<br/>CARD-NUM + CUST-ID + ACCT-ID]
    end
    
    subgraph "Alternate Indexes"
        CARDAIX[CARDDATA.AIX<br/>Secondary Key: ACCT-ID]
        CXACAIX[CARDXREF.AIX<br/>Secondary Key: Alternative Position]
    end
    
    CUST -->|1. READ CUSTFILE<br/>by CUST-ID| XREF
    XREF -->|2. STARTBR XREFFILE<br/>RIDFLD: CUST-ID<br/>GTEQ| XREF
    XREF -->|3. READNEXT<br/>Extract CARD-NUM| CARD
    CARD -->|4. READ CARDFILE<br/>by CARD-NUM| CARD
    
    ACCT -->|1. Use alternate index| CARDAIX
    CARDAIX -->|2. Browse by ACCT-ID| CARD
    
    XREF -.->|Bidirectional<br/>navigation support| CXACAIX
