#### 6.3.7.2 Cross-Reference Navigation Pattern

The **XREFFILE** provides referential integrity integration without database foreign key constraints, enabling navigation between related entities (customers, accounts, cards).

**Cross-Reference Record Structure** (from `app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy`):

```
01  CARD-XREF-RECORD.
    05  XREF-CARD-NUM           PIC X(16).    * Primary key
    05  XREF-CUST-ID            PIC 9(09).    * Customer ID link
    05  XREF-ACCT-ID            PIC 9(11).    * Account ID link
    05  FILLER                  PIC X(14).
```

**Navigation Integration Flow**:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Entity Access"
        CUST[CUSTFILE<br/>Primary Key: CUST-ID]
        ACCT[ACCTFILE<br/>Primary Key: ACCT-ID]
        CARD[CARDFILE<br/>Primary Key: CARD-NUM]
    end
    
    subgraph "Cross-Reference Integration"
        XREF[XREFFILE<br/>Composite Key<br/>CARD-NUM + CUST-ID + ACCT-ID]
    end
    
    subgraph "Alternate Indexes"
        CARDAIX[CARDDATA.AIX<br/>Secondary Key: ACCT-ID]
        CXACAIX[CARDXREF.AIX<br/>Secondary Key: Alternative Position]
    end
    
    CUST -->|1. READ CUSTFILE<br/>by CUST-ID| XREF
    XREF -->|2. STARTBR XREFFILE<br/>RIDFLD: CUST-ID<br/>GTEQ| XREF
    XREF -->|3. READNEXT<br/>Extract CARD-NUM| CARD
    CARD -->|4. READ CARDFILE<br/>by CARD-NUM| CARD
    
    ACCT -->|1. Use alternate index| CARDAIX
    CARDAIX -->|2. Browse by ACCT-ID| CARD
    
    XREF -.->|Bidirectional<br/>navigation support| CXACAIX
    
    style CUST fill:#E1F5FF
    style ACCT fill:#E1F5FF
    style CARD fill:#E1F5FF
    style XREF fill:#FFF4E1
    style CARDAIX fill:#E8F5E9
    style CXACAIX fill:#E8F5E9
```

**Browse Integration Example** (retrieving all cards for a customer):

```
* Position browse at first record for customer
         MOVE CUSTOMER-ID TO XREF-CUST-ID
         EXEC CICS STARTBR FILE('XREFFILE')
              RIDFLD(XREF-CUST-ID)
              GTEQ
              RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
         END-EXEC
         
* Loop through all cards for this customer
         PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-BROWSE
            EXEC CICS READNEXT FILE('XREFFILE')
                 INTO(CARD-XREF-RECORD)
                 RIDFLD(XREF-KEY)
                 RESP(WS-RESP-CD)
            END-EXEC
            
            IF WS-RESP-CD = DFHRESP(NORMAL)
               * Check if still same customer
               IF XREF-CUST-ID = CUSTOMER-ID
                  * Retrieve card details using extracted card number
                  MOVE XREF-CARD-NUM TO CARD-NUMBER
                  EXEC CICS READ FILE('CARDFILE')
                       INTO(CARD-RECORD)
                       RIDFLD(CARD-NUMBER)
                       RESP(WS-RESP-CD2)
                  END-EXEC
                  
                  IF WS-RESP-CD2 = DFHRESP(NORMAL)
                     PERFORM PROCESS-CARD-DETAILS
                  END-IF
               ELSE
                  * Moved to different customer, end browse
                  SET END-OF-BROWSE TO TRUE
               END-IF
            ELSE
               * End of file or error
               SET END-OF-BROWSE TO TRUE
            END-IF
         END-PERFORM
         
         EXEC CICS ENDBR FILE('XREFFILE') END-EXEC
```

#### 6.3.7.3 Record Locking Integration

**CICS Record-Level Locking** prevents concurrent update conflicts without application-level serialization logic:

| Lock Type | Acquisition | Release | Concurrent Access |
|-----------|-------------|---------|------------------|
| Shared Lock | EXEC CICS READ (without UPDATE) | Automatic after read completes | Multiple readers allowed, no writers |
| Exclusive Lock | EXEC CICS READ UPDATE | EXEC CICS REWRITE or UNLOCK | Single writer, no other readers or writers |
| Implicit Lock | EXEC CICS WRITE/DELETE | Automatic after operation completes | Short-duration exclusive lock |

**Locking Integration Flow**:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Task1 as CICS Task 1<br/>COACTUPC
    participant Task2 as CICS Task 2<br/>COACTUPC
    participant LockMgr as Record Lock Manager
    participant VSAM as VSAM ACCTFILE
    
    Note over Task1,VSAM: Scenario: Concurrent Account Update Attempts
    
    Task1->>LockMgr: READ UPDATE ACCTFILE<br/>ACCT-ID=00000000001
    LockMgr->>LockMgr: Check lock status<br/>Record not locked
    LockMgr->>VSAM: Physical READ<br/>Retrieve record
    VSAM->>LockMgr: Account record
    LockMgr->>Task1: Record + Exclusive Lock<br/>RESP=NORMAL
    
    Note over Task1: User modifying fields<br/>Account record in memory
    
    Task2->>LockMgr: READ UPDATE ACCTFILE<br/>ACCT-ID=00000000001<br/>(Same account)
    LockMgr->>LockMgr: Check lock status<br/>Exclusive lock held by Task 1
    LockMgr->>Task2: RESP=LOCKED<br/>Record unavailable
    
    Note over Task2: Handle lock conflict
    Task2->>Task2: Display message:<br/>"Record being updated by another user"<br/>SEND MAP with error
    Task2->>Task2: RETURN TRANSID<br/>Allow retry
    
    Note over Task1: User completes changes<br/>Presses Enter to save
    
    Task1->>LockMgr: REWRITE ACCTFILE<br/>FROM(updated-record)
    LockMgr->>VSAM: Physical REWRITE<br/>Update record
    VSAM->>LockMgr: Update successful
    LockMgr->>LockMgr: Release exclusive lock<br/>Record now available
    LockMgr->>Task1: RESP=NORMAL
    
    Task1->>Task1: Display success message<br/>SEND MAP<br/>RETURN TRANSID
    
    Note over Task2: User retries after<br/>first user completes
    
    Task2->>LockMgr: READ UPDATE ACCTFILE<br/>ACCT-ID=00000000001
    LockMgr->>LockMgr: Check lock status<br/>No lock present
    LockMgr->>VSAM: Physical READ<br/>Retrieve updated record
    VSAM->>LockMgr: Account record (with Task 1 changes)
    LockMgr->>Task2: Record + Exclusive Lock<br/>RESP=NORMAL
    
    Note over Task2: Success - User 2 can now update
```

**Deadlock Prevention**:

CardDemo's simple transaction patterns prevent deadlocks through:
- **Single Record Updates**: Each transaction updates at most one master record
- **Short Hold Times**: Locks held only during terminal interaction (pseudo-conversational model)
- **No Nested Locks**: Programs don't acquire multiple exclusive locks simultaneously
- **Automatic Timeout**: CICS task timeout releases locks if user abandons terminal

#### 6.3.8.2 Dataset Naming Convention Integration

**AWS.M2 High-Level Qualifier (HLQ)** identifies datasets managed by AWS Mainframe Modernization service, enabling platform-specific integration:

**Example Dataset Names** (from `app/jcl/POSTTRAN.jcl`):

```
//TRANSACT DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.KSDS,DISP=SHR
//DALYTRAN DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DALYTRAN.KSDS,DISP=SHR

#### 6.3.10.3 Key Architectural Findings

**Critical Finding**: CardDemo implements **internal integration patterns** within a self-contained mainframe architecture without external system dependencies. This design decision supports the system's demonstration mission by providing authentic mainframe integration mechanisms (TDQ messaging, COMMAREA session state, VSAM file coordination, batch-online segregation) that serve as reference implementations for migration tool validation and modernization planning.

**Integration Pattern Authenticity**: The seven documented integration patterns (3270 terminal protocol, CICS transaction processing, COMMAREA communication, TDQ messaging, VSAM file I/O, batch-online coordination, BMS map processing) represent production-grade mainframe integration techniques observed across financial services, insurance, government, and enterprise sectors, providing valuable educational and testing value for organizations planning mainframe modernization initiatives.

**Platform Integration Capability**: AWS Mainframe Modernization service integration through dataset naming conventions (AWS.M2.* HLQ) and runtime packages (Micro Focus, UniKix) demonstrates cloud migration feasibility without application code changes, validating lift-and-shift modernization strategies for mainframe applications.

## 6.4 Security Architecture

### 6.4.1 Security Architecture Overview

#### 6.4.1.1 Security Context and Design Philosophy

CardDemo implements a **demonstration-grade security architecture** designed for educational and testing purposes rather than production deployment. The security framework intentionally incorporates simplified patterns that represent authentic mainframe security structures while avoiding the complexity required for production-grade systems handling sensitive financial data.

**System Security Classification:**

| Classification Aspect | CardDemo Implementation | Production Requirement |
|----------------------|-------------------------|------------------------|
| **Deployment Context** | Testing and demonstration platform | Production financial services |
| **Data Sensitivity** | Synthetic test data (50 records) | Real customer financial data |
| **Threat Model** | Educational environment | Internet-facing, high-threat |
| **Compliance Scope** | Not applicable | PCI-DSS, GDPR, SOX |

The security architecture serves two primary objectives:

1. **Educational Demonstration**: Illustrate typical mainframe security patterns including user authentication via VSAM security files, session management through COMMAREA structures, and role-based access control through user type segregation

2. **Migration Testing Support**: Provide realistic security integration points for testing migration tools' ability to handle authentication flows, authorization checks, and session state management during modernization initiatives

**Intentional Security Limitations:**

CardDemo explicitly excludes production-grade security controls to maintain simplicity and focus on mainframe application patterns. These limitations include plaintext password storage, absence of encryption at rest and in transit, no audit logging infrastructure, unlimited authentication attempts without account lockout, and simplified two-tier authorization model. The README.md documentation clearly identifies the system as a "demonstration and testing platform" to establish appropriate security expectations for users.

#### 6.4.1.2 Security Architecture Principles

The security architecture adheres to three foundational principles:

**Principle 1: Authenticity Over Security Hardening**

CardDemo prioritizes authentic representation of mainframe security patterns over implementing comprehensive security controls. The authentication implementation using USRSEC VSAM files, password validation in COBOL programs, and session context propagation through COMMAREA structures reflect genuine mainframe development practices. This authenticity enables migration tools to encounter realistic security integration challenges.

**Principle 2: Transparency and Documentation**

All security limitations are explicitly documented in repository documentation, source code comments, and this technical specification. The system does not attempt to obscure security weaknesses or present a false sense of security hardening. This transparency ensures that evaluators, developers, and migration architects understand the security baseline and can plan appropriate enhancements during modernization.

**Principle 3: Extensibility for Enhancement**

The architecture provides clear extension points where production-grade security controls could be integrated. These extension points include password hashing in COSGN00C authentication logic, encryption enablement through z/OS data set encryption, audit logging insertion points in transaction programs, and authorization framework expansion in menu routing logic.

#### 6.4.1.3 Security Components Overview

The security architecture comprises four interconnected components:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Security Architecture Components"
        direction TB
        
        subgraph "Authentication Layer"
            AUTH[COSGN00C<br/>Authentication Program]
            USRSEC[USRSEC VSAM File<br/>User Credentials]

        end

### 6.4.2 Authentication Framework

#### 6.4.2.1 Identity Management

**User Repository Architecture:**

CardDemo implements a VSAM-based user identity repository through the USRSEC file, a Key-Sequenced Data Set (KSDS) defined with 80-byte fixed-length records. The file structure, specified in `app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy`, provides persistent storage for user credentials and attributes without integration to external identity providers.

**User Record Structure:**

```
SEC-USER-DATA (80 bytes total):
  SEC-USR-ID        PIC X(08)   [Bytes 0-7]    Primary key, unique identifier
  SEC-USR-FNAME     PIC X(20)   [Bytes 8-27]   First name
  SEC-USR-LNAME     PIC X(20)   [Bytes 28-47]  Last name
  SEC-USR-PWD       PIC X(08)   [Bytes 48-55]  Password (plaintext)
  SEC-USR-TYPE      PIC X(01)   [Bytes 56]     User type ('A'=Admin, 'U'=User)
  SEC-USR-FILLER    PIC X(23)   [Bytes 57-79]  Reserved for future use
```

**Default User Accounts:**

Per README.md documentation, the system initializes with two default accounts:

| User ID | Password | Type | Purpose |
|---------|----------|------|---------|
| ADMIN001 | PASSWORD | A | Administrative user with access to user management functions |
| USER0001 | PASSWORD | U | Regular user with access to business functions |

**Storage Security Posture:**

Analysis of LISTCAT.txt catalog information reveals critical security configuration gaps:

- **Data Set Encryption**: NO - All user credentials stored unencrypted on disk
- **RACF Protection**: NO - No Resource Access Control Facility protection enabled
- **Password Protection**: NULL - No dataset password protection configured
- **Current Population**: 10 user records loaded from test data

**Identity Management Limitations:**

The current implementation lacks several production-grade identity management capabilities:

- ❌ No integration with enterprise directory services (LDAP, Active Directory)
- ❌ No federated identity support (SAML, OAuth, OpenID Connect)
- ❌ No self-service password reset capability
- ❌ No user provisioning workflow or approval process
- ❌ No user lifecycle management (automatic deactivation, periodic review)
- ❌ No separation of user identity from authentication credentials

#### 6.4.2.2 Authentication Process

**Authentication Flow Implementation:**

The authentication process, implemented in `app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl` and invoked via CICS transaction CC00, performs credential validation through direct VSAM file access and plaintext password comparison.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User as 3270 Terminal User
    participant Map as COSGN00 BMS Map
    participant Auth as COSGN00C Program
    participant USRSEC as USRSEC VSAM File
    participant Menu as Menu Program
    
    User->>Auth: Invoke CC00 Transaction
    Auth->>Map: EXEC CICS SEND MAP<br/>(Display sign-on screen)
    Map->>User: Present User ID & Password Fields<br/>(Password masked with DRK)
    
    User->>Map: Enter Credentials
    Map->>Auth: EXEC CICS RECEIVE MAP<br/>(Capture input)
    
    Auth->>Auth: Convert input to UPPERCASE<br/>FUNCTION UPPER-CASE
    
    Auth->>Auth: Validate User ID not empty
    alt User ID Empty
        Auth->>Map: Error: "Please enter User ID"
        Map->>User: Cursor positioned at User ID field
    end
    
    Auth->>Auth: Validate Password not empty
    alt Password Empty
        Auth->>Map: Error: "Please enter Password"
        Map->>User: Cursor positioned at Password field
    end
    
    Auth->>USRSEC: EXEC CICS READ<br/>FILE('USRSEC')<br/>RIDFLD(User ID)
    
    alt User Not Found (RESP=13)
        USRSEC-->>Auth: NOTFND Response
        Auth->>Map: Error: "User not found. Try again..."
        Map->>User: Allow retry with cursor at User ID
    else User Found
        USRSEC-->>Auth: SEC-USER-DATA Record
        
        Auth->>Auth: Compare Plaintext Passwords<br/>IF SEC-USR-PWD = WS-USER-PWD
        
        alt Password Mismatch
            Auth->>Map: Error: "Wrong Password. Try again..."
            Map->>User: Allow retry with cursor at Password
        else Password Match
            Auth->>Auth: Populate CARDDEMO-COMMAREA<br/>- CDEMO-USER-ID<br/>- CDEMO-USER-TYPE<br/>- CDEMO-FROM-TRANID = 'CC00'
            
            alt User Type = 'A' (Admin)
                Auth->>Menu: EXEC CICS XCTL<br/>PROGRAM('COADM01C')<br/>Transaction CA00
                Menu->>User: Display Admin Menu
            else User Type = 'U' (Regular)
                Auth->>Menu: EXEC CICS XCTL<br/>PROGRAM('COMEN01C')<br/>Transaction CM00
                Menu->>User: Display Main Menu
            end
        end
    end
    
    alt System Error
        USRSEC-->>Auth: Unexpected RESP Code
        Auth->>Map: Error: "Unable to verify the User..."
        Map->>User: Display system error message
    end
```

**Authentication Logic Details:**

**Step 1: Input Capture and Normalization**
The program receives user input via EXEC CICS RECEIVE MAP, capturing USRIDIN (user ID) and PASSWDI (password) from the COSGN0AI input map structure. Both fields undergo uppercase conversion using COBOL FUNCTION UPPER-CASE, reducing password entropy by eliminating case sensitivity.

**Step 2: Field-Level Validation**
Sequential validation checks ensure both user ID and password fields contain non-empty values. Empty or space-filled fields trigger error messages with cursor repositioning to the invalid field, implemented by setting the field's length attribute (USRIDL or PASSWDL) to -1.

**Step 3: User Record Retrieval**
The program executes EXEC CICS READ against the USRSEC file using the entered user ID as RIDFLD (Record Identification Field). Response code evaluation distinguishes between successful retrieval (DFHRESP(NORMAL)), user not found (DFHRESP(NOTFND)), and system errors.

**Step 4: Credential Verification**
For successfully retrieved user records, the program performs direct string comparison: `IF SEC-USR-PWD = WS-USER-PWD`. This plaintext comparison represents the most significant security vulnerability in the authentication framework.

**Step 5: Session Establishment**
Upon successful authentication, the program populates the CARDDEMO-COMMAREA structure defined in `app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy` with authenticated user context, including user ID, user type, originating transaction, and program context indicators.

**Step 6: User Type-Based Routing**
The program evaluates CDEMO-USER-TYPE to determine routing destination. Admin users (type 'A') transfer control to COADM01C via EXEC CICS XCTL, while regular users (type 'U') transfer to COMEN01C, establishing the authorization boundary.

**Critical Security Vulnerabilities:**

| Vulnerability | Impact | Risk Level |
|--------------|--------|------------|
| **Plaintext Password Storage** | Passwords readable in VSAM file by any CICS program with file access | Critical |
| **No Password Hashing** | Database breach exposes all credentials immediately | Critical |
| **Uppercase Conversion** | Reduces password entropy and eliminates case as complexity factor | High |
| **No Account Lockout** | Unlimited authentication attempts enable brute force attacks | High |

#### 6.4.2.3 Multi-Factor Authentication

**Current State: Not Implemented**

CardDemo implements single-factor authentication exclusively through user ID and password credentials. No multi-factor authentication (MFA) capabilities exist in the current architecture.

**Missing MFA Capabilities:**

- ❌ No time-based one-time password (TOTP) support
- ❌ No SMS or email verification codes
- ❌ No hardware token integration (RSA SecurID, YubiKey)
- ❌ No biometric authentication
- ❌ No push notification approval mechanisms
- ❌ No risk-based authentication triggering additional factors

**Extension Points for MFA Integration:**

The authentication logic in COSGN00C provides clear extension points where MFA could be integrated during modernization:

1. **Post-Password Validation**: After successful password comparison, invoke MFA verification routine
2. **COMMAREA Extension**: Add MFA-verified flag to session context
3. **BMS Map Enhancement**: Create additional screens for MFA code entry
4. **USRSEC Extension**: Add MFA enrollment data (phone number, device ID) to user records

#### 6.4.2.4 Session Management

**Session Context Structure:**

CardDemo implements stateless session management through the CARDDEMO-COMMAREA structure, a communication area passed between programs via EXEC CICS XCTL and RETURN commands. This structure, defined in `app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy`, persists user context without requiring server-side session storage.

**Session State Fields:**

```
CARDDEMO-COMMAREA Structure:
  
  CDEMO-GENERAL-INFO:
    CDEMO-FROM-TRANID       PIC X(04)    Calling transaction identifier
    CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM      PIC X(08)    Calling program name
    CDEMO-TO-TRANID         PIC X(04)    Target transaction identifier
    CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM        PIC X(08)    Target program name
    CDEMO-USER-ID           PIC X(08)    Authenticated user identifier
    CDEMO-USER-TYPE         PIC X(01)    User type: 'A'=Admin, 'U'=User
    CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT       PIC 9(01)    0=First entry, 1=Re-entry
  
  CDEMO-CUSTOMER-INFO:
    CDEMO-CUST-ID           PIC 9(09)    Current customer identifier
    CDEMO-CUST-FNAME        PIC X(25)    Customer first name
    CDEMO-CUST-MNAME        PIC X(25)    Customer middle name
    CDEMO-CUST-LNAME        PIC X(25)    Customer last name
  
  CDEMO-ACCOUNT-INFO:
    CDEMO-ACCT-ID           PIC 9(11)    Current account identifier
    CDEMO-ACCT-STATUS       PIC X(01)    Account status code
  
  CDEMO-CARD-INFO:
    CDEMO-CARD-NUM          PIC 9(16)    Current card number
  
  CDEMO-MORE-INFO:
    CDEMO-LAST-MAP          PIC X(07)    Last displayed map name
    CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET       PIC X(07)    Last displayed mapset name
```

**Session Propagation Mechanisms:**

**EXEC CICS XCTL (Transfer Control)**: Permanently transfers control to target program while preserving COMMAREA contents. The calling program terminates, and the target program receives the COMMAREA in its LINKAGE SECTION DFHCOMMAREA structure.

**EXEC CICS RETURN with TRANSID**: Terminates current program instance and schedules next transaction. The COMMAREA parameter specifies data to preserve for the next invocation, enabling conversation-style interactions.

**Session Validation Pattern:**

All business function programs implement session validation by checking EIBCALEN (EXEC Interface Block Communication Area Length). Programs detecting EIBCALEN = 0 indicate unauthenticated entry, typically triggering EXEC CICS XCTL back to COSGN00C to force authentication.

**Session Lifecycle:**

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Unauthenticated: Program Start<br/>EIBCALEN = 0
    
    Unauthenticated --> Authenticated: COSGN00C Success<br/>COMMAREA Populated
    
    state Authenticated {
        [*] --> SessionActive
        
        SessionActive --> SessionActive: XCTL/RETURN<br/>COMMAREA Preserved
        
        note right of SessionActive
            CDEMO-USER-ID available
            CDEMO-USER-TYPE enforced
            Business context accumulated
        end note
    }
    
    Authenticated --> Unauthenticated: PF3 from Menu<br/>COMMAREA Discarded
    
    Authenticated --> Timeout: CICS DTIMOUT<br/>Exceeded
    
    Timeout --> Unauthenticated: Forced Re-authentication
    
    Unauthenticated --> [*]: Terminal Disconnect
```

**Session Timeout Configuration:**

CardDemo relies on CICS system-level transaction timeout (DTIMOUT parameter) without implementing application-level idle timeout logic. No explicit session expiration timestamp exists in the COMMAREA structure, and no re-authentication trigger occurs after prolonged inactivity beyond CICS infrastructure timeout.

**Session Security Limitations:**

| Limitation | Security Impact |
|-----------|-----------------|
| **No Session Token** | No cryptographic session identifier; COMMAREA contents could be manipulated if interception possible |
| **No Idle Timeout** | Sessions persist indefinitely until CICS timeout or explicit logout |
| **No Concurrent Session Control** | Single user can establish multiple simultaneous sessions without detection |
| **No Session Invalidation** | No mechanism to revoke active sessions (e.g., after password change) |

#### 6.4.2.5 Token Handling

**Current State: Not Implemented**

CardDemo does not implement token-based authentication mechanisms. The system uses traditional mainframe session management without cryptographic tokens.

**Absent Token Technologies:**

- ❌ No JSON Web Tokens (JWT) for session representation
- ❌ No OAuth 2.0 access tokens or refresh tokens
- ❌ No API keys for programmatic access
- ❌ No SAML assertions for federated authentication
- ❌ No bearer tokens for REST API authentication

The COMMAREA structure serves as an implicit session token, but lacks cryptographic signatures, expiration timestamps, or tamper-evident characteristics of modern token systems.

#### 6.4.2.6 Password Policies

**Current Password Requirements:**

The password policy implementation in CardDemo, primarily enforced in `app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl` (User Add program), applies minimal validation rules:

| Policy Aspect | Implementation | Assessment |
|---------------|----------------|------------|
| **Length** | Fixed 8 characters (field size) | ⚠️ No minimum enforcement beyond field length |
| **Complexity** | None | ❌ No uppercase, lowercase, number, or special character requirements |
| **Validation** | Non-empty check only | ❌ Insufficient validation |
| **Storage Format** | Plaintext | ❌ Critical vulnerability |

**Password Validation Logic:**

From COUSR01C.cbl User Add program:
```
WHEN PASSWDI OF COUSR1AI = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES
    MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG
    MOVE 'Password can NOT be empty...' TO WS-MESSAGE
...
MOVE PASSWDI OF COUSR1AI TO SEC-USR-PWD  [Direct storage, no transformation]
```

**Missing Password Controls:**

The password policy framework lacks comprehensive controls found in production systems:

- ❌ **No Password History**: Users can reuse previous passwords immediately
- ❌ **No Password Expiration**: Passwords never require periodic change
- ❌ **No Complexity Requirements**: Any 8-character string accepted
- ❌ **No Dictionary Checking**: Common passwords (PASSWORD, 12345678) permitted
- ❌ **No Minimum Length**: No enforcement beyond 8-character field size
- ❌ **No Password Confirmation**: Single entry field without verification
- ❌ **No First-Login Password Change**: Default passwords persist without forced change

**Default Password Security Risk:**

The README.md documents default passwords (ADMIN001/PASSWORD, USER0001/PASSWORD), representing a critical security risk if deployed unchanged. No forced password change occurs on first login.

---

### 6.4.3 Authorization System

#### 6.4.3.1 Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

**Authorization Model:**

CardDemo implements a simplified two-tier role-based access control model using the SEC-USR-TYPE field in user records. This binary model segregates administrative functions from business operations without granular permission management.

**Role Definitions:**

| Role | Code | Entry Point | Accessible Functions | Function Count |
|------|------|-------------|---------------------|----------------|
| **Administrator** | A | COADM01C (CA00) | User management only: List, Add, Update, Delete users | 4 |
| **Regular User** | U | COMEN01C (CM00) | All business functions: Account, Card, Transaction, Billing, Reporting | 10+ |

**Authorization Architecture:**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Authorization Flow"
        AUTH[COSGN00C<br/>Authentication]
        
        AUTH -->|User Type 'A'| ADMIN_MENU[COADM01C<br/>Admin Menu CA00]
        AUTH -->|User Type 'U'| USER_MENU[COMEN01C<br/>Main Menu CM00]
        
        subgraph "Admin Role Functions"
            ADMIN_MENU --> USR_LIST[COUSR00C CU00<br/>List Users]
            ADMIN_MENU --> USR_ADD[COUSR01C CU01<br/>Add User]
            ADMIN_MENU --> USR_UPD[COUSR02C CU02<br/>Update User]
            ADMIN_MENU --> USR_DEL[COUSR03C CU03<br/>Delete User]
        end
        
        subgraph "Regular User Functions"
            USER_MENU --> ACCT[Account Functions<br/>COACTVWC COACTUPC]
            USER_MENU --> CARD[Card Functions<br/>COCRDLIC COCRDSLC COCRDUPC]
            USER_MENU --> TRAN[Transaction Functions<br/>COTRN00C-02C]
            USER_MENU --> BILL[Bill Payment<br/>COBIL00C]
            USER_MENU --> RPT[Reporting<br/>CORPT00C]
        end
    end
    
    style AUTH fill:#FFE1E1
    style ADMIN_MENU fill:#E1EFFF
    style USER_MENU fill:#E1FFE1
```

**Authorization Enforcement Points:**

**Entry-Point Routing (COSGN00C.cbl):**
The authentication program performs initial authorization routing based on user type:
```
IF CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN
    EXEC CICS XCTL PROGRAM('COADM01C') COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA)
ELSE
    EXEC CICS XCTL PROGRAM('COMEN01C') COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA)
END-IF
```

**Menu-Level Segregation:**
Admin users routed to COADM01C access only user management transactions (CU00-CU03). Regular users routed to COMEN01C access business function transactions (account, card, transaction, billing, reporting).

**Implicit Program-Level Authorization:**
User management programs (COUSR00C-03C) are accessible exclusively through the admin menu. No explicit user type validation exists within these programs—authorization relies on menu routing preventing regular users from reaching these functions.

**Authorization Model Limitations:**

| Limitation | Impact | Risk Level |
|-----------|--------|------------|
| **No Granular Permissions** | Cannot restrict individual functions within role | Medium |
| **Implicit Authorization** | Relies on menu structure, not explicit checks | High |
| **No Function-Level Validation** | Programs don't verify user authorization | High |
| **Binary Role Model** | Only two roles, no intermediate permissions | Medium |
| **No Least Privilege** | Admin users cannot access business functions they may need | Low |

#### 6.4.3.2 Permission Management

**Current State: No Explicit Permission System**

CardDemo does not implement a formal permission management system with granular access controls. Authorization operates through role assignment (user type) without function-level permissions.

**Implicit Access Control Matrix:**

| Function | Admin (A) | User (U) | Enforcement Mechanism |
|----------|-----------|----------|----------------------|
| **User Administration** | ✓ | ✗ | Menu routing only |
| **Account View** | ✗ | ✓ | Menu routing only |
| **Account Update** | ✗ | ✓ | Menu routing only |
| **Card Management** | ✗ | ✓ | Menu routing only |
| **Transaction Processing** | ✗ | ✓ | Menu routing only |
| **Bill Payment** | ✗ | ✓ | Menu routing only |
| **Reporting** | ✗ | ✓ | Menu routing only |

**User Administration Functions (Admin-Only):**

From `app/cbl/COUSR00C.cbl` through `app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl`:

- **COUSR00C (CU00)**: List all users with search capability, paginated display (7 users per screen), shows user ID, name, and user type
- **COUSR01C (CU01)**: Add new users with password initialization, validates unique user ID, captures first name, last name, user type
- **COUSR02C (CU02)**: Update existing user details including password changes, name modifications, user type reassignment
- **COUSR03C (CU03)**: Delete users from USRSEC file with confirmation workflow

**Permission Assignment Mechanism:**

Permissions (user type) are assigned at user creation time through COUSR01C. The SEC-USR-TYPE field is set to 'A' or 'U' and persists in the USRSEC VSAM record. Modification occurs exclusively through COUSR02C (Update User), accessible only to admin users.

**Missing Permission Capabilities:**

- ❌ No runtime permission evaluation beyond user type
- ❌ No temporary privilege elevation or delegation
- ❌ No time-bound permissions
- ❌ No context-aware authorization (e.g., restrict by account ownership)
- ❌ No permission inheritance or role hierarchy
- ❌ No permission templates or groups

#### 6.4.3.3 Resource Authorization

**VSAM File Access Control:**

CardDemo implements no file-level access controls within the application layer. All authenticated users with CICS file authorization can access all VSAM datasets.

**Missing Resource Authorization:**

- ❌ **No File-Level Access Control**: All authenticated users can access all VSAM files
- ❌ **No Row-Level Security**: Users can access any customer/account/card record if ID known
- ❌ **No Column-Level Security**: All fields visible to users with record access
- ❌ **No Ownership Model**: No concept of user-owned records vs. system-wide records
- ❌ **No Data Tenancy**: No segregation between different user populations

**Transaction Authorization Vulnerability:**

Any user who knows a transaction ID can invoke it directly, bypassing menu-based access control. For example, a regular user could invoke CA00 (admin menu transaction) directly from the terminal, though CICS security could prevent this with proper transaction security definitions.

**Data-Level Authorization Absence:**

Programs do not validate that users should access specific records. For instance, COACTVWC (Account View) accepts any account ID without verifying user relationship to that account. This design assumes a trusted operator model where authenticated users are authorized to view all data.

#### 6.4.3.4 Policy Enforcement Points

**Identified Enforcement Locations:**

**1. Authentication Gateway (COSGN00C):**
- **Enforcement**: Validates credentials against USRSEC file
- **Action**: Establishes user session with user type in COMMAREA
- **Routing**: Directs users to appropriate menu based on type

**2. Menu Programs (COADM01C, COMEN01C):**
- **Enforcement**: Control function availability through option display
- **Action**: Filter displayed options based on user type
- **Routing**: EXEC CICS XCTL to authorized programs only

**3. Individual Programs (implicit):**
- **Enforcement**: Check EIBCALEN for session presence
- **Action**: Access CDEMO-USER-TYPE from COMMAREA if needed
- **Limitation**: No explicit authorization enforcement code found

**Missing Centralized Policy Enforcement:**

The current architecture lacks centralized authorization services that would provide:
- ❌ Centralized policy decision point (PDP)
- ❌ Policy enforcement point (PEP) framework
- ❌ Attribute-based access control (ABAC) evaluation
- ❌ Dynamic policy updates without code changes
- ❌ Policy externalization in configuration

#### 6.4.3.5 Audit Logging

**Critical Finding: No Audit Logging Implemented**

CardDemo does not implement security audit logging capabilities. No application-level tracking exists for authentication attempts, authorization decisions, data access patterns, or administrative actions.

**Missing Audit Capabilities:**

| Audit Category | Required Capability | Current State |
|----------------|-------------------|---------------|
| **Authentication Logging** | Track all login attempts (success/failure), source terminal, timestamp | ❌ Not implemented |
| **Authorization Logging** | Record all access control decisions, denied operations | ❌ Not implemented |
| **Data Access Logging** | Track record reads/writes with user ID, timestamp, data identifiers | ❌ Not implemented |
| **Administrative Actions** | Log user additions, deletions, modifications, password changes | ❌ Not implemented |
| **Security Events** | Record lockouts, privilege escalations, configuration changes | ❌ Not implemented |

**System-Level Monitoring Available:**

While application-level audit logging is absent, z/OS and CICS provide infrastructure-level monitoring:

**CICS Auxiliary Trace**: Captures technical transaction flow including EXEC CICS commands, file operations, program control operations. This provides technical troubleshooting data but not security audit trails.

**CICS Transaction Dumps**: Generated automatically on ABEND (abnormal end), capturing program state, working storage, and COMMAREA contents for failure analysis.

**Batch SYSOUT**: Batch programs write operational messages to SYSOUT datasets showing program execution milestones and record counts.

**Compliance Impact:**

The absence of audit logging creates critical compliance gaps:

- ❌ **PCI-DSS Requirement 10**: "Track and monitor all access to network resources and cardholder data" not met
- ❌ **GDPR Article 30**: Records of processing activities not maintained
- ❌ **SOX Controls**: No evidence trail for financial data access
- ❌ **Forensic Investigation**: Insufficient data for security incident investigation
- ❌ **Insider Threat Detection**: Cannot identify unusual access patterns

---

### 6.4.4 Data Protection

#### 6.4.4.1 Encryption Standards

**Data at Rest: No Encryption Implemented**

Analysis of VSAM dataset catalog information from LISTCAT.txt reveals that all datasets storing sensitive information lack encryption protection:

**Encryption Status Summary:**

| Dataset | Contents | Encryption | RACF Protection |
|---------|----------|------------|-----------------|
| **USRSEC** | User IDs, passwords (plaintext), names | NO | NO |
| **CUSTFILE** | SSN, DOB, Government IDs, FICO scores | NO | NO |
| **CARDFILE** | 16-digit PANs, CVV codes, cardholder names | NO | NO |
| **ACCTFILE** | Account balances, credit limits | NO | NO |
| **TRANSACT** | Transaction amounts, merchant details | NO | NO |

**LISTCAT Output Analysis:**

All datasets show identical encryption configuration:
```
ENCRYPTIONDATA
    DATA SET ENCRYPTION-----(NO)
PROTECTION-PSWD-----(NULL)
RACF----------------(NO)
```

**Sensitive Data Exposure:**

**CUSTFILE Record (CVCUS01Y.cpy)** exposes personally identifiable information without protection:
- CUST-SSN (PIC 9(09)): Social Security Number in cleartext
- CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID (PIC X(20)): Government identification documents
- CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD (PIC X(10)): Date of birth
- CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE (PIC 9(03)): Credit score
- CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID (PIC X(10)): Bank account identifier

**CARDFILE Record (CVACT02Y.cpy)** exposes payment card information without protection:
- CARD-NUM (PIC X(16)): Primary Account Number (PAN) in cleartext
- CARD-CVV-CD (PIC 9(03)): Card Verification Value in cleartext

**Data in Transit: No Explicit Encryption**

**3270 Terminal Communication**: Uses TN3270 (Telnet 3270) protocol without encryption. Terminal sessions transmit credentials and sensitive data in cleartext across the network unless TLS/SSL configured at infrastructure level.

**CICS Inter-Program Communication**: EXEC CICS XCTL and LINK commands pass COMMAREA in CICS region memory. Data protection relies on CICS region isolation without message-level encryption.

**Batch-Online File Sharing**: VSAM files accessed by both CICS online programs and batch jobs through standard file I/O without encryption layer.

**Available But Unused Encryption Capabilities:**

z/OS provides encryption capabilities not implemented in CardDemo:

- **z/OS Data Set Encryption**: Could be enabled for VSAM datasets through system administration
- **RACF Policy Enforcement**: Could mandate encryption for datasets containing sensitive data
- **CICS SSL/TLS Support**: Could encrypt terminal connections through CICS configuration
- **Hardware Acceleration**: z/OS CPACF (CP Assist for Cryptographic Functions) available for performance

#### 6.4.4.2 Key Management

**Current State: Not Applicable**

Since no encryption is implemented, CardDemo has no encryption key management requirements or infrastructure.

**Missing Key Management Capabilities:**

- ❌ No encryption key generation
- ❌ No key storage mechanisms (keystores, key databases)
- ❌ No key rotation procedures or policies
- ❌ No Hardware Security Module (HSM) integration
- ❌ No key lifecycle management (creation, distribution, archival, destruction)
- ❌ No key escrow or recovery procedures
- ❌ No separation of key management from key usage

**Extension Point for Key Management:**

If encryption were implemented during modernization, z/OS Integrated Cryptographic Service Facility (ICSF) would provide comprehensive key management including:
- Master key management for data set encryption
- Key generation and distribution services
- Hardware security module integration
- Key lifecycle management
- Cryptographic key database (CKDS)

#### 6.4.4.3 Data Masking Rules

**Minimal Data Masking Implemented**

CardDemo implements minimal data masking limited to password entry fields without broader personally identifiable information (PII) protection.

**Password Field Masking:**

BMS map definitions use the DRK (dark) attribute for password fields, preventing on-screen display during entry. However, passwords remain visible in USRSEC file to CICS programs with file access.

Example from COSGN0A.cpy:
```
Password field defined with:
  ATTR: DRK (dark attribute)
  FSET: Field set attribute
  ASKIP: Auto-skip after entry
```

**PII Data Display (No Masking):**

Sensitive fields display in full without masking:

- **Social Security Numbers**: Displayed as 123456789, not XXX-XX-6789
- **Primary Account Numbers**: Displayed as full 16-digit card number, not ****-****-****-1234
- **Card Verification Values**: Displayed as 3-digit CVV without restriction
- **Date of Birth**: Displayed in full without partial masking
- **Government IDs**: Displayed in full without redaction

**Data Masking Gaps:**

| Data Type | Current Display | Production Standard | Gap |
|-----------|----------------|-------------------|-----|
| SSN | 123-45-6789 | XXX-XX-6789 | No masking |
| PAN | 1234567890123456 | ****-****-****-3456 | No masking |
| CVV | 123 | *** or hidden | No masking |
| Password | DRK attribute (entry only) | Masked everywhere | Partial masking |

#### 6.4.4.4 Secure Communication

**Terminal Communication:**

**Protocol**: TN3270 (Telnet 3270) for terminal connectivity
**Encryption**: Not specified in application configuration, typically unencrypted unless TLS configured at infrastructure level
**Authentication**: User ID and password transmitted during sign-on process
**Session Protection**: Relies on network security controls external to application

**Inter-Program Communication:**

**Mechanism**: EXEC CICS XCTL (transfer control) and LINK (call/return) commands
**Data Transfer**: COMMAREA passed in CICS region memory space
**Protection**: Relies on CICS region isolation and z/OS address space protection
**Interception Risk**: Low within single CICS region; no cross-region communication implemented

**Batch-Online Integration:**

**Transient Data Queue (TDQ)**: Online programs submit batch jobs via TDQ (CORPT00C report generation)
**VSAM File Sharing**: Coordinated through CLOSEFIL/OPENFIL JCL ensuring serialized access
**Protection**: Physical file access controls (not implemented in CardDemo)

**Missing Secure Communication Controls:**

- ❌ **No TLS/SSL for Terminal Sessions**: 3270 terminal traffic unencrypted
- ❌ **No Message-Level Encryption**: Inter-program communication unprotected
- ❌ **No Secure File Transfer**: No SFTP or encrypted batch file transfer
- ❌ **No API Encryption**: No REST/SOAP APIs exist; future APIs would require TLS
- ❌ **No Certificate Management**: No PKI infrastructure for certificate-based authentication

#### 6.4.4.5 Compliance Controls

**Critical: No Compliance Controls Implemented**

CardDemo lacks compliance controls required for production financial systems handling sensitive customer data.

**PCI-DSS Requirements (Not Met):**

| Requirement | Status | Gap Description |
|-------------|--------|-----------------|
| **Req 3**: Protect stored cardholder data | ❌ Failed | PANs and CVVs stored unencrypted in CARDFILE |
| **Req 4**: Encrypt transmission of cardholder data | ❌ Failed | TN3270 terminal sessions unencrypted |
| **Req 8**: Assign unique ID to each person | ⚠️ Partial | User IDs implemented but passwords plaintext |
| **Req 10**: Track and monitor all access | ❌ Failed | No audit logging implemented |

**GDPR Requirements (Not Met for European Deployment):**

- ❌ **Article 32 - Security of Processing**: No encryption of personal data
- ❌ **Article 30 - Records of Processing Activities**: No audit trail maintained
- ❌ **Article 17 - Right to Erasure**: No documented deletion procedures
- ❌ **Article 33 - Data Breach Notification**: No breach detection mechanism

**SOX Controls (Not Applicable):**

CardDemo is not designed for financial reporting systems subject to Sarbanes-Oxley Act. Missing controls include:
- No segregation of duties enforcement beyond basic role separation
- No change management audit trail
- No IT general controls framework

**System Purpose Disclaimer:**

The README.md explicitly states: "CardDemo is a demonstration and testing platform designed for mainframe migration and modernization use cases." The security limitations are intentional for educational and testing purposes, not production deployment.

**Security Zone Characteristics:**

**Single-Tier Architecture**: All components reside within a single security zone without demilitarized zones (DMZ) or network segmentation. Online and batch components share direct file access without intermediate security boundaries.

**No Network Segregation**: The architecture lacks internal network segregation between presentation, application, and data layers. All components operate within the same trust boundary once past initial authentication.

**Trust Boundary**: The primary trust boundary exists at terminal authentication (COSGN00C). Once authenticated, users gain trusted status for all subsequent operations within their role's scope.

**External Security Not Configured**: RACF (Resource Access Control Facility) is available on z/OS but not enabled for CardDemo datasets. No dataset-level protection, no password protection, and no access control beyond CICS file definitions.

**Authorization Flow Characteristics:**

**Entry-Point Authorization**: COSGN00C performs the only explicit authorization check, routing users based on type. Subsequent authorization relies on menu structure.

**Implicit Authorization Model**: Individual programs do not re-validate user authorization. They trust that menu-based routing ensures only authorized users reach specific functions.

**Session Validation**: Programs check EIBCALEN > 0 to verify COMMAREA presence (indicating authenticated session) but do not verify authorization for the requested function.

**No Authorization Audit**: No logging occurs for authorization decisions or denied access attempts.

### 6.4.6 Security Control Matrices

#### 6.4.6.1 Authentication Controls

| Control | Implementation Status | Evidence Location | Effectiveness |
|---------|---------------------|-------------------|---------------|
| **User Identification** | ✓ Implemented | USRSEC file, CSUSR01Y.cpy | Basic: 8-character user IDs |
| **Password Authentication** | ⚠️ Weak Implementation | COSGN00C.cbl plaintext comparison | Ineffective: No hashing |

### 6.4.7 Security Recommendations for Modernization

#### 6.4.7.1 Critical Security Enhancements

For organizations using CardDemo as a modernization reference, the following critical enhancements should be implemented before production deployment:

**Priority 1 - Authentication Hardening:**
- Implement password hashing using bcrypt, PBKDF2, or Argon2
- Establish password complexity requirements (minimum 12 characters, mixed case, numbers, special characters)
- Implement account lockout after failed authentication attempts (e.g., 5 attempts, 15-minute lockout)
- Add failed login tracking and notification
- Implement password expiration and history (e.g., 90-day expiration, prevent reuse of last 10 passwords)

**Priority 2 - Data Protection:**
- Enable z/OS data set encryption for all VSAM files containing sensitive data
- Implement TLS/SSL for terminal connections (TN3270E with SSL)
- Add data masking for PII display (SSN, PAN, CVV)
- Implement field-level encryption for highly sensitive fields
- Enable RACF protection for all datasets

**Priority 3 - Audit Logging:**
- Implement comprehensive security event logging (authentication, authorization, data access)
- Add timestamp and user ID to all audit records
- Create audit log retention and archival procedures
- Implement log analysis and alerting for suspicious patterns
- Establish audit log integrity protection

**Priority 4 - Authorization Enhancement:**
- Implement granular permission model beyond two-tier roles
- Add function-level authorization checks in all programs
- Implement data-level authorization based on ownership
- Add runtime authorization verification
- Create centralized authorization service

#### 6.4.7.2 Compliance Roadmap

Organizations targeting specific compliance frameworks should implement controls aligned with:

**PCI-DSS Requirements:**
- Requirement 3: Implement strong cryptography for stored cardholder data
- Requirement 4: Encrypt cardholder data transmission across public networks
- Requirement 8: Implement multi-factor authentication for all access
- Requirement 10: Implement comprehensive audit logging and monitoring

**GDPR Requirements:**
- Article 32: Implement encryption and pseudonymization of personal data
- Article 30: Maintain records of processing activities
- Article 17: Implement right to erasure procedures
- Article 33: Implement data breach detection and notification
