#### 7.6.4.2 Initial Page Load

# 8. Infrastructure

## 8.1 Overview

### 8.1.1 Infrastructure Applicability Statement

CardDemo is a **native z/OS mainframe application** designed to operate on traditional IBM mainframe infrastructure. The system intentionally implements pre-modernization deployment patterns typical of legacy credit card processing applications, making it an ideal reference implementation for mainframe migration and modernization testing initiatives.

**Critical Infrastructure Characteristics:**

- **Deployment Model:** Single-region z/OS mainframe deployment with CICS Transaction Server
- **Modern Cloud Infrastructure:** Not applicable (no containers, orchestration, or cloud services)
- **CI/CD Automation:** Not applicable (manual JCL-based deployment processes)
- **Monitoring Approach:** Native z/OS and CICS facilities exclusively

This infrastructure intentionally represents the "before" state of mainframe modernization projects. Organizations evaluating migration to AWS Mainframe Modernization (M2), containerized platforms, or cloud-native architectures use CardDemo to test migration tools, validate transformation methodologies, and train personnel on mainframe-to-cloud migration patterns.

### 8.1.2 Architectural Context

As documented in `Section 5.1 High-Level Architecture`, CardDemo implements a **three-tier monolithic mainframe application** consisting of:

- **Presentation Layer:** 17 BMS (Basic Mapping Support) maps for 3270 terminal interaction
- **Business Logic Layer:** 28 COBOL programs (16 online, 11 batch, 1 utility) executing in CICS or JES
- **Data Layer:** 13 VSAM KSDS (Key-Sequenced Data Set) files on DASD storage

This monolithic single-region deployment eliminates distributed systems infrastructure complexity including service mesh, container orchestration, load balancing, and distributed storage coordination. All components execute within a single CICS address space or JES-managed batch jobs on a single z/OS LPAR (Logical Partition).

### 8.1.3 AWS Mainframe Modernization Context

The repository includes AWS Mainframe Modernization runtime packages in `samples/m2/`:

- **CardDemo_runtime.zip** - Micro Focus Enterprise Analyzer runtime package
- **UniKix_CardDemo_runtime_v1.zip** - UniKix Mainframe Connector runtime package

These artifacts represent **future-state migration targets** for AWS M2 deployment but are not currently operational infrastructure. The current system state operates on traditional z/OS mainframe infrastructure as documented in this section.

## 8.2 Deployment Environment

### 8.2.1 Target Environment Assessment

#### 8.2.1.1 Environment Type

**Primary Deployment Target:** IBM z/OS Mainframe (On-Premises or Cloud)

CardDemo operates on IBM z/OS operating system with the following infrastructure components:

| Component | Technology | Version/Configuration | Purpose |
|-----------|-----------|----------------------|---------|
| **Operating System** | IBM z/OS | z/OS 2.x or higher | Mainframe operating system providing VSAM, JES, and CICS hosting |
| **Transaction Server** | IBM CICS Transaction Server | V5.6 | Real-time online transaction processing environment |
| **Job Scheduler** | JES2 or JES3 | z/OS integrated | Batch job scheduling, execution, and output management |
| **File System** | VSAM (Virtual Storage Access Method) | KSDS clusters | Indexed file storage with record-level locking |

**Deployment Topology:**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "z/OS LPAR - Logical Partition"
        subgraph "CICS Region - CICSPROD"
            direction TB
            CICS_Kernel[CICS Transaction Server V5.6]
            Online_Programs[16 Online COBOL Programs<br/>COSGN00C, COMEN01C, COACTUPC, etc.]
            BMS_Maps[17 BMS Mapsets<br/>COSGN00, COMEN01, COACTUPM, etc.]
            File_Control[CICS File Control<br/>LSR Pool Manager]
            
            CICS_Kernel --> Online_Programs
            CICS_Kernel --> BMS_Maps
            CICS_Kernel --> File_Control
        end
        
        subgraph "JES Batch Processing"
            direction TB
            JES_Scheduler[JES Job Entry Subsystem]
            Batch_Programs[11 Batch COBOL Programs<br/>CBTRN02C, CBACT02C, CBSTM03A, etc.]
            
            JES_Scheduler --> Batch_Programs
        end
        
        subgraph "DASD Storage - Direct Access Storage"
            direction TB
            VSAM_Files[13 VSAM KSDS Files<br/>CUSTFILE, ACCTFILE, CARDFILE<br/>TRANSACT, XREFFILE, etc.]
            Load_Libraries[Load Libraries<br/>AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB]
            Source_Libraries[Source Libraries<br/>COBSRC, BMS, COBCOPY]
        end
        
        Terminal_Network[3270 Terminal Network<br/>TN3270 Emulator Access]
        
        Terminal_Network --> BMS_Maps
        File_Control --> VSAM_Files
        Batch_Programs --> VSAM_Files
        Online_Programs -.->|Loaded from| Load_Libraries
        Batch_Programs -.->|Loaded from| Load_Libraries
    end
    
    style CICS_Kernel fill:#4A90E2
    style Online_Programs fill:#F5A623
    style Batch_Programs fill:#D0021B
    style VSAM_Files fill:#7ED321
    style Terminal_Network fill:#BD10E0
```

#### 8.2.1.2 Geographic Distribution Requirements

**Single-Region Deployment:** CardDemo operates as a monolithic application within a single z/OS LPAR with no geographic distribution requirements.

**Characteristics:**
- No multi-region deployment
- No data replication across geographic locations
- No distributed transaction coordination
- All processing occurs within single CICS region or JES job scheduler

**Production Patterns (Reference Only):**

Production mainframe systems typically implement geographic redundancy through:
- **Parallel Sysplex:** Multi-system clustering with shared DASD and coupling facility
- **GDPS (Geographically Dispersed Parallel Sysplex):** Active-active or active-passive configurations across data centers
- **Remote Data Replication:** PPRC (Peer-to-Peer Remote Copy) or XRC (Extended Remote Copy)

CardDemo excludes these patterns as a demonstration system with synthetic data.

#### 8.2.1.3 Resource Requirements

**Compute Resources:**

| Resource Type | Specification | Purpose | Scaling Considerations |
|--------------|---------------|---------|------------------------|
| **CICS Region Memory** | 512 MB - 2 GB | CICS kernel, program storage, buffer pools | Scales with concurrent user count and LSR buffer pool size |
| **Language Environment** | z/OS LE runtime | COBOL program execution environment | Minimal overhead with RENT (reentrant) programs |
| **CPU Capacity** | MIPS-based allocation | Transaction processing, batch job execution | Scales linearly with transaction volume and batch record counts |

**Memory Allocation Patterns:**

As documented in `Section 5.4.4.2 Performance Design Patterns`, programs specify `CONCURRENCY=QUASIRENT` enabling multiple concurrent task executions sharing executable code, minimizing per-user memory overhead.

**Storage Resources:**

| Dataset Type | Primary Allocation | Secondary Allocation | Organization | Purpose |
|-------------|-------------------|---------------------|--------------|---------|
| **VSAM Master Files** | 1-5 cylinders | 1 cylinder | KSDS with alternate indexes | Customer, account, card, transaction data |
| **VSAM Reference Files** | 1 cylinder | 1 cylinder | KSDS | Discount groups, transaction categories, type codes |
| **Load Libraries** | 10-20 cylinders | 5 cylinders | PDS/PDSE | Executable program modules and BMS maps |
| **Source Libraries** | 5-10 cylinders | 2 cylinders | PDS | COBOL source, BMS source, copybooks |
| **GDG Files** | 1 cylinder per generation | 1 cylinder | LIMIT(5) | Transaction backups, reject files, archived data |

**VSAM Dataset Sizing Example (from `app/jcl/ACCTFILE.jcl`):**

```
DEFINE CLUSTER (
  NAME(AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.ACCTFILE.KSDS)
  VOLUMES(CARDEM)
  RECORDSIZE(300 300)
  KEYS(11 0)
  INDEXED
  SHAREOPTIONS(2 3)
  FREESPACE(10 10)
  CYLINDERS(5 1)
)
```

**Network Resources:**

- **3270 Terminal Network:** TN3270 protocol over TCP/IP for terminal emulation
- **Terminal Types:** IBM 3278/3279 model 2 or higher (24x80 character display minimum)
- **Network Latency:** Sub-second response times for typical mainframe terminal networks
- **Concurrent Users:** CICS MAXTASKS parameter governs maximum concurrent terminal sessions

#### 8.2.1.4 Compliance and Regulatory Requirements

**RACF Integration Pattern:**

CardDemo simulates RACF (Resource Access Control Facility) authentication through the **USRSEC VSAM file**. As documented in `Section 3.7.4.1 RACF Integration Pattern`, production systems integrate with actual RACF for:

- **Authentication:** User ID and password verification
- **Authorization:** Resource-level access control (datasets, transactions, programs)
- **Audit Logging:** Security event logging for compliance (SOX, PCI-DSS, HIPAA)

**CardDemo Security Limitations (Intentional):**

- No password encryption (plaintext storage in USRSEC)
- No audit trail logging of authentication attempts or data access
- No password complexity requirements or expiration policies
- No account lockout after failed authentication attempts

These limitations reflect demonstration system characteristics with synthetic test users (50 user records maximum).

### 8.2.2 Environment Management

#### 8.2.2.1 Infrastructure as Code Approach

**NOT APPLICABLE** - Traditional mainframe infrastructure does not use modern IaC tooling.

**Infrastructure Definition Method:**

Infrastructure configuration occurs through **JCL dataset definitions** using IDCAMS (Access Method Services). The `app/jcl/` directory contains 28+ JCL jobs defining datasets, loading data, and managing VSAM clusters.

**VSAM Dataset Definition Pattern (from `app/jcl/CUSTFILE.jcl`):**

```jcl
//DEFCUST  JOB
//DELETE   EXEC PGM=IDCAMS
//SYSPRINT DD SYSOUT=*
//SYSIN    DD *
  DELETE AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTFILE.KSDS CLUSTER
  SET MAXCC=0
/*
//DEFINE   EXEC PGM=IDCAMS
//SYSPRINT DD SYSOUT=*
//SYSIN    DD *
  DEFINE CLUSTER (
    NAME(AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTFILE.KSDS)
    VOLUMES(CARDEM)
    RECORDSIZE(500 500)
    KEYS(9 0)
    INDEXED
    SHAREOPTIONS(2 3)
    FREESPACE(10 10)
    CYLINDERS(1 5)
  ) DATA (
    NAME(AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTFILE.KSDS.DATA)
  ) INDEX (
    NAME(AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CUSTFILE.KSDS.INDEX)
  )
/*
```

**CICS Resource Definition:**

The `app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD` file (29,940 bytes) contains CICS resource definitions processed by **DFHCSDUP** utility:

- 13 VSAM file definitions with FCT (File Control Table) attributes
- 17 BMS mapset definitions with physical and symbolic map associations
- 16 transaction definitions with program associations and attributes
- 28 program definitions with language, concurrency, and execution parameters

**Comparison to Modern IaC:**

| Traditional Mainframe | Modern IaC (Terraform, CloudFormation) |
|----------------------|----------------------------------------|
| JCL with IDCAMS commands | HCL or YAML declarative syntax |
| Manual job submission | Automated plan/apply workflows |
| No version control of infrastructure state | State file version tracking |
| No drift detection | Automatic drift detection and correction |
| Operator expertise required | Self-service infrastructure provisioning |

#### 8.2.2.2 Configuration Management Strategy

**Source Library Management:**

Configuration resides in partitioned datasets (PDS) with member-level version control:

| Library | Dataset Name | Content | Members |
|---------|-------------|---------|---------|
| **COBOL Source** | AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.COBSRC | COBOL program source code | 28 programs (COSGN00C, COMEN01C, etc.) |
| **BMS Source** | AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.BMS | BMS map definitions | 17 mapsets (COSGN00, COMEN01, etc.) |
| **Copybooks** | AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.COBCOPY | COBOL copybook definitions | 40+ copybooks (CVACT01Y, CVTRA05Y, etc.) |
| **JCL Library** | AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.JCL | Job control language scripts | 28+ jobs (ACCTFILE, CLOSEFIL, POSTTRAN, etc.) |
| **Load Library** | AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB | Executable programs and maps | 45 load modules |

**Version Control Integration:**

As documented in `Section 3.7.5.3 Version Control`, source code version control uses **Git** with embedded version metadata in source files:

```
* Ver: CardDemo_v1.0-15-g27d6c6f-68 Date: 2022-07-19 23:23:06 CDT
```

Version metadata indicates:
- **Base Version:** CardDemo_v1.0
- **Commits Since Tag:** 15 commits since v1.0 tag
- **Git Commit Hash:** g27d6c6f (short hash)
- **Build Number:** 68
- **Compilation Timestamp:** 2022-07-19 23:23:06 CDT

**Configuration Change Workflow:**

1. Developer modifies source in Git repository
2. Source uploaded to mainframe using $INDFILE or FTP
3. Compilation JCL submitted (CICCMP.jcl, BATCMP.jcl, BMSCMP.jcl)
4. Load module updated in LOADLIB
5. CEMT SET PROG(programname) NEWCOPY refreshes in CICS
6. Testing performed via 3270 terminal

#### 8.2.2.3 Environment Promotion Strategy

**MANUAL PROMOTION PROCESS** - No automated dev/staging/prod environment promotion.

**Environment Characteristics:**

CardDemo documentation assumes a **single environment** for demonstration purposes. Production mainframe systems typically maintain separate environments:

| Environment | Purpose | Refresh Strategy | Access Control |
|------------|---------|------------------|----------------|
| **Development** | Program development and unit testing | Developers compile and test programs | Developer access via TSO/ISPF |
| **Test/QA** | Integration testing and user acceptance | Periodic refresh from production data | QA team access, limited production data |
| **Production** | Live transaction processing | Change management controlled | Operations staff only, full RACF audit |

**Manual Promotion Workflow (Reference Only):**

1. **Development Compilation:** Developer submits compilation JCL in development region
2. **Testing:** Developer executes test transactions, validates functionality
3. **Promotion Request:** Developer submits change request through change management system
4. **Code Review:** Senior developer or architect reviews source code changes
5. **Staging Deployment:** Operations staff compiles program in staging CICS region
6. **Staging Testing:** QA team executes regression tests in staging environment
7. **Production Deployment:** Operations staff compiles program in production region during change window
8. **Production Validation:** Operations staff executes smoke tests post-deployment
9. **Monitoring:** Operations staff monitors CICS messages and transaction response times

#### 8.2.2.4 Backup and Disaster Recovery Plans

**VSAM Dataset Backup:**

The `app/jcl/TRANBKP.jcl` job demonstrates VSAM backup using **IDCAMS REPRO** command:

```jcl
//BACKUP   EXEC PGM=IDCAMS
//SYSPRINT DD SYSOUT=*
//SYSIN    DD *
  REPRO INFILE(TRANSIN) OUTFILE(TRANSOUT)
/*
//TRANSIN  DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.KSDS,DISP=SHR
//TRANSOUT DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.TRANSACT.BACKUP,DISP=(NEW,CATLG)
```

**Backup Strategy:**

| Backup Type | Method | Frequency | Retention | Purpose |
|------------|--------|-----------|-----------|---------|
| **VSAM Full Backup** | IDCAMS REPRO to backup clusters | Daily (batch window) | 7 days | Full dataset recovery |
| **GDG Versioning** | Generation Data Groups with LIMIT(5) | Per batch execution | 5 generations | Transaction reject file history |
| **CICS CSD Backup** | Copy CARDDEMO.CSD to backup dataset | After configuration changes | 30 days | CICS resource definition recovery |
| **Source Code Backup** | Git repository with remote origin | Continuous | Indefinite | Source code version history |

**Generation Data Group Configuration (from `app/jcl/DEFGDGB.jcl`):**

```jcl
//DEFGDG   EXEC PGM=IDCAMS
//SYSPRINT DD SYSOUT=*
//SYSIN    DD *
  DEFINE GENERATIONDATAGROUP (
    NAME(AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DALYREJS)
    LIMIT(5)
    SCRATCH
    NOEMPTY
  )
/*
```

GDG LIMIT(5) retains 5 most recent generations, automatically deleting older generations.

**Recovery Procedures:**

As documented in `Section 5.4.5.2 Recovery Procedures`, VSAM file recovery follows this workflow:

1. **Quiesce Online Processing:** Execute `app/jcl/CLOSEFIL.jcl` to close VSAM files in CICS
2. **Restore from Backup:** Execute IDCAMS REPRO to copy backup cluster to production cluster
3. **Verify Integrity:** Execute IDCAMS VERIFY to check VSAM cluster integrity
4. **Resume Online Processing:** Execute `app/jcl/OPENFIL.jcl` to reopen files for CICS
5. **Validate Recovery:** Execute test transactions (CC00 sign-on, account inquiry) to verify data accessibility

**Data Reload from Test Data:**

For complete dataset recreation after catastrophic failure:

1. Delete existing VSAM clusters using IDCAMS DELETE
2. Redefine clusters using dataset definition JCL (ACCTFILE.jcl, CARDFILE.jcl, etc.)
3. Load test data using IDCAMS REPRO from sequential files
4. Rebuild alternate indexes using IDCAMS BLDINDEX (TRANIDX.jcl)
5. Install CICS resources using DFHCSDUP or CEDA INSTALL GROUP(CARDDEMO)

**Recovery Limitations:**

As documented in `Section 5.4.5.3 Recovery Limitations`, CardDemo implements demonstration-level disaster recovery:

- **No RPO (Recovery Point Objective):** No specific data loss tolerance defined
- **No RTO (Recovery Time Objective):** No specific recovery time commitment
- **No Automated Failover:** Manual recovery procedures only
- **No Geographic Redundancy:** Single-site deployment assumption
- **No Transaction Journaling:** JOURNAL=NO in VSAM file definitions
- **No Point-in-Time Recovery:** No transaction log replay capability

Production systems require comprehensive backup automation, geographic redundancy through Parallel Sysplex or GDPS, transaction journaling with forward recovery capability, and RPO/RTO objectives aligned with business requirements.

## 8.3 Cloud Services

### 8.3.1 Cloud Services Applicability

**CLOUD SERVICES ARE NOT USED IN CURRENT IMPLEMENTATION**

CardDemo is a native z/OS mainframe application with **no cloud service dependencies**. The system operates entirely on traditional mainframe infrastructure using z/OS operating system facilities, CICS Transaction Server, and VSAM file storage.

**Why Cloud Services Are Not Used:**

1. **Mainframe-Native Architecture:** Application designed for z/OS execution environment with CICS transaction processing and VSAM data access
2. **Demonstration Purpose:** System represents pre-modernization state for testing migration tools and methodologies
3. **Self-Contained Design:** No external dependencies on databases, message queues, object storage, or API gateways
4. **Traditional Deployment Model:** Reflects authentic 1990s-2000s mainframe application patterns before cloud adoption

### 8.3.2 AWS Mainframe Modernization (M2) Target

The repository includes AWS Mainframe Modernization runtime packages in `samples/m2/`:

| Package | Runtime Platform | Purpose | Status |
|---------|-----------------|---------|--------|
| **CardDemo_runtime.zip** | Micro Focus Enterprise Analyzer | Micro Focus COBOL runtime for M2 | Future migration target |
| **UniKix_CardDemo_runtime_v1.zip** | UniKix Mainframe Connector | UniKix runtime for M2 | Future migration target |

**AWS M2 Service Overview (Reference Only):**

AWS Mainframe Modernization provides managed runtime environments for migrated mainframe applications:

- **Micro Focus Runtime:** Executes Micro Focus COBOL applications with CICS emulation
- **Blu Age Runtime:** Converts COBOL to Java with Spring Boot framework
- **UniKix Runtime:** Executes IBM COBOL applications with CICS compatibility layer

These packages represent the **"after" state** of migration projects but are not currently deployed infrastructure.

### 8.3.3 Cloud Service Patterns for Modernized Deployments

Organizations migrating CardDemo-like applications to cloud typically introduce these services:

| Cloud Service Category | AWS Example Services | Use Case in Modernized Deployment |
|----------------------|---------------------|----------------------------------|
| **Managed Databases** | Amazon RDS, Amazon DynamoDB | Replace VSAM files with relational or NoSQL databases |
| **Object Storage** | Amazon S3 | Store batch input/output files, statement PDFs, archived data |
| **Message Queuing** | Amazon SQS, Amazon MQ | Decouple batch processing, enable asynchronous transaction posting |
| **API Gateway** | Amazon API Gateway | Expose modernized transactions as REST APIs |
| **Authentication** | Amazon Cognito, IAM | Replace USRSEC file with managed authentication service |
| **Monitoring** | Amazon CloudWatch, X-Ray | Replace native z/OS monitoring with cloud observability |
| **Serverless Compute** | AWS Lambda | Execute batch jobs serverlessly for cost optimization |

These patterns represent modernization opportunities evaluated during cloud migration planning but are not part of the current infrastructure.

## 8.4 Containerization

### 8.4.1 Containerization Applicability

**CONTAINERIZATION IS NOT USED**

CardDemo does not use Docker containers, container images, or container registries. No Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, or container manifest files exist in the repository.

**Evidence of No Containerization:**

- No `Dockerfile` in repository root or subdirectories
- No `docker-compose.yml` for multi-container orchestration
- No `.dockerignore` file
- No container registry references (ECR, Docker Hub, etc.)
- No container-specific build scripts

**Why Containerization Is Not Used:**

1. **Mainframe Execution Model:** z/OS does not natively support Docker containers or container runtimes
2. **CICS Region Architecture:** Programs execute in CICS transaction server address space, not containers
3. **Traditional Deployment:** Load modules deployed to PDS/PDSE libraries, not container images
4. **Pre-Modernization State:** Application represents pre-containerization mainframe patterns

### 8.4.2 Container Patterns for Modernized Deployments

Organizations migrating mainframe applications to containerized platforms typically follow these patterns:

**Phase 1: Lift-and-Shift Container Packaging**

- Package Micro Focus COBOL runtime with application load modules in Docker image
- Use official Micro Focus base images with CICS emulation layer
- Deploy containers to AWS ECS or Amazon EKS
- Replace VSAM with containerized database (PostgreSQL, MySQL)

**Phase 2: Microservices Decomposition**

- Decompose monolithic COBOL into microservices (account service, transaction service, card service)
- Create separate Docker images per microservice
- Implement REST APIs using Spring Boot or Node.js
- Deploy to Kubernetes with service mesh (Istio, AWS App Mesh)

**Phase 3: Cloud-Native Refactoring**

- Rewrite critical components in modern languages (Java, Python, Go)
- Use multi-stage Docker builds for optimized image sizes
- Implement CI/CD pipelines with container security scanning
- Deploy to serverless container platforms (AWS Fargate, Google Cloud Run)

These patterns represent modernization trajectories but are not applicable to current traditional mainframe deployment.

## 8.5 Orchestration

### 8.5.1 Orchestration Applicability

**ORCHESTRATION IS NOT REQUIRED**

CardDemo does not use Kubernetes, Amazon ECS, Docker Swarm, or other container orchestration platforms. The mainframe architecture uses native z/OS resource management instead of distributed orchestration.

**Evidence of No Orchestration:**

- No Kubernetes manifests (deployment.yaml, service.yaml, configmap.yaml)
- No Helm charts or Kustomize configurations
- No ECS task definitions or service definitions
- No Docker Swarm stack files

**Why Orchestration Is Not Used:**

1. **Single-Region Deployment:** Application executes in single CICS region, no distributed services requiring orchestration
2. **z/OS Resource Management:** z/OS Workload Manager (WLM) and CICS resource management provide native orchestration
3. **JES Batch Scheduling:** JES provides batch job orchestration without Kubernetes CronJobs or similar
4. **Monolithic Architecture:** No microservices requiring service discovery, load balancing, or auto-scaling

### 8.5.2 Native z/OS Orchestration Mechanisms

**CICS Region Management:**

CICS provides native resource orchestration for online transactions:

| CICS Capability | Orchestration Function | Configuration Method |
|----------------|------------------------|---------------------|
| **Transaction Routing** | Route transactions to appropriate programs | Transaction definitions in CARDDEMO.CSD |
| **Program Load Management** | Load programs on demand, share code across tasks | CONCURRENCY=QUASIRENT in program definitions |
| **File Resource Allocation** | Manage VSAM file access, buffer pools, string allocation | File definitions with LSRPOOLNUM, STRINGS parameters |
| **Transaction Priority** | Prioritize critical transactions over batch-like transactions | PRIORITY parameter in transaction definitions |

**JES Batch Job Orchestration:**

As documented in `Section 3.8.2.2 Batch Job Workflow`, JES provides batch job orchestration:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant JES as JES Job Scheduler
    participant CLOSE as CLOSEFIL.jcl
    participant POST as POSTTRAN.jcl
    participant CALC as INTCALC.jcl
    participant STMT as CREASTMT.JCL
    participant OPEN as OPENFIL.jcl
    
    Note over JES: End-of-Day Processing
    
    JES->>CLOSE: Submit CLOSEFIL<br/>Close VSAM files
    CLOSE-->>JES: RC=0
    
    JES->>POST: Submit POSTTRAN<br/>Post transactions
    POST-->>JES: RC=0
    
    JES->>CALC: Submit INTCALC<br/>Calculate interest
    CALC-->>JES: RC=0
    
    JES->>STMT: Submit CREASTMT<br/>Generate statements
    STMT-->>JES: RC=0
    
    JES->>OPEN: Submit OPENFIL<br/>Reopen files
    OPEN-->>JES: RC=0
    
    Note over JES: Batch Cycle Complete
```

**Job Dependency Management:**

JCL supports conditional execution through COND parameter and IF/THEN/ELSE constructs:

```jcl
//STEP02  EXEC PGM=CBTRN02C,COND=(4,LT,STEP01)
```

Execute STEP02 only if STEP01 return code is less than 4.

```jcl
//IF1     IF (STEP01.RC = 0) THEN
//STEP02  EXEC PGM=CBTRN02C
//ENDIF   ENDIF
```

Conditional execution based on previous step success.

**Orchestration Comparison:**

| Traditional z/OS | Modern Kubernetes |
|-----------------|-------------------|
| CICS region hosts multiple programs | Kubernetes cluster hosts multiple pods |
| JES schedules batch jobs | CronJobs schedule periodic tasks |
| COND parameters manage dependencies | Init containers and job dependencies manage sequencing |
| z/OS WLM manages resource allocation | Resource requests/limits and pod priority manage allocation |
| Manual job submission through TSO/SDSF | kubectl or CI/CD pipelines submit jobs |

### 8.5.3 Orchestration Patterns for Modernized Deployments

Organizations modernizing to microservices architectures typically implement:

- **Amazon EKS:** Managed Kubernetes for containerized COBOL or rewritten microservices
- **Amazon ECS with Fargate:** Serverless container orchestration for simplified operations
- **AWS App Mesh:** Service mesh for microservices communication and observability
- **AWS Step Functions:** Serverless orchestration for multi-step batch workflows replacing JCL job streams

These patterns apply to modernized deployments, not current mainframe infrastructure.

## 8.6 CI/CD Pipeline

### 8.6.1 CI/CD Applicability

**NO AUTOMATED CI/CD PIPELINE EXISTS**

CardDemo intentionally lacks automated CI/CD infrastructure, reflecting traditional mainframe development paradigms where compilation and deployment occur through manual JCL job submission.

**Evidence of No CI/CD:**

- No `.github/workflows/` directory (GitHub Actions)
- No `.gitlab-ci.yml` file (GitLab CI)
- No `Jenkinsfile` (Jenkins Pipeline)
- No `.circleci/config.yml` (CircleCI)
- No `.travis.yml` (Travis CI)
- No AWS CodePipeline or Azure DevOps pipeline definitions

**Rationale (from `Section 3.7.5.3 Version Control`):**

> "CardDemo intentionally lacks automated CI/CD infrastructure: No GitHub Actions workflows, No Jenkins pipelines, No automated testing frameworks, No deployment automation. This absence reflects the mainframe development paradigm where compilation and deployment traditionally occur through manual JCL job submission rather than automated pipelines."

### 8.6.2 Build Pipeline (Manual Process)

#### 8.6.2.1 Source Control Integration

**Version Control:** Git repository with GitHub remote origin

**Version Metadata Embedded in Source Files:**

```
* Ver: CardDemo_v1.0-15-g27d6c6f-68 Date: 2022-07-19 23:23:06 CDT
```

Metadata components:
- **CardDemo_v1.0:** Base version tag
- **15:** Commits since v1.0 tag
- **g27d6c6f:** Git commit hash (short form)
- **68:** Build number
- **2022-07-19 23:23:06 CDT:** Compilation timestamp

**Source Upload Methods:**

1. **File Transfer Protocol (FTP):** Upload source members to mainframe PDS libraries
2. **$INDFILE Utility:** z/OS utility for batch source upload
3. **ISPF Edit:** Direct terminal-based source editing via TSO/ISPF
4. **Zowe CLI:** Modern z/OS CLI for programmatic source upload (optional)

#### 8.6.2.2 Build Environment Requirements

**Mainframe Compilation Toolchain:**

As documented in `Section 3.7.1 Compilation Toolchain`, compilation requires:

| Tool | Product | Library | Purpose |
|------|---------|---------|---------|
| **COBOL Compiler** | IBM Enterprise COBOL V6.3 | IGY.SIGYCOMP.V63 | Compile COBOL source to object modules |
| **CICS Translator** | CICS Transaction Server V5.6 | SDFHLOAD | Expand EXEC CICS commands to COBOL CALL statements |
| **Assembler** | IBM High Level Assembler | ASMA90 | Assemble BMS macros to map modules and copybooks |
| **Linkage Editor** | IBM Binder (HEWL) | CEE.SCEELKED | Link object modules to executable load modules |

**Compilation Procedures:**

Three cataloged procedures automate compilation workflows:

1. **BUILDONL.prc** (Online CICS Programs):
   - Step 1: CICS Translation (expand EXEC CICS commands)
   - Step 2: COBOL Compilation (IGYCRCTL with CICS,RENT,NODYNAM parameters)
   - Step 3: Linkage Editing (HEWL with AMODE(31),RMODE(ANY),LET parameters)

2. **BUILDBAT.prc** (Batch Programs):
   - Step 1: COBOL Compilation (IGYCRCTL with APOST,LIST,MAP,NUMBER parameters)
   - Step 2: Linkage Editing (HEWL with LIST,XREF parameters)

3. **BUILDBMS.prc** (BMS Maps):
   - Step 1: Map Assembly (ASMA90 with SYSPARM(MAP))
   - Step 2: Map Linkage Editing (HEWL)
   - Step 3: Copybook Assembly (ASMA90 with SYSPARM(DSECT))
   - Step 4: Copybook Copy (IEBGENER to COBCOPY library)

#### 8.6.2.3 Dependency Management

**No External Dependency Management Tools**

CardDemo has no external dependencies requiring package managers (npm, Maven, pip, NuGet). All dependencies are mainframe-native libraries:

| Dependency Type | Library | Resolution Method |
|----------------|---------|-------------------|
| **Copybooks** | AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.COBCOPY | SYSLIB DD in compilation JCL |
| **BMS Copybooks** | AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.COBCOPY | Generated from BMS source via BUILDBMS.prc |
| **CICS Runtime** | SDFHLOAD, SDFHCOB | STEPLIB DD in compilation JCL |
| **Language Environment** | CEE.SCEELKED, CEE.SCEELKEX | SYSLIB DD in linkage editor step |

**Copybook Dependency Example:**

COBOL programs reference copybooks via COPY statements:

```cobol
       COPY CVACT01Y.    * Account record structure
       COPY CVTRA05Y.    * Transaction record structure
       COPY CVCUS01Y.    * Customer record structure
```

Compilation JCL resolves copybooks through SYSLIB concatenation:

```jcl
//SYSLIB   DD DSN=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.COBCOPY,DISP=SHR
//         DD DSN=SDFHCOB,DISP=SHR
```

#### 8.6.2.4 Artifact Generation and Storage

**Build Artifacts:**

| Artifact Type | Storage Location | Format | Purpose |
|--------------|------------------|--------|---------|
| **Online Program Modules** | AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB | PDS members | CICS-executable programs (COSGN00C, COMEN01C, etc.) |
| **Batch Program Modules** | AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB | PDS members | JES-executable programs (CBTRN02C, CBACT02C, etc.) |
| **BMS Map Modules** | AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB | PDS members | Physical maps for SEND MAP/RECEIVE MAP (COSGN00, COMEN01, etc.) |
| **BMS Copybooks** | AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.COBCOPY | PDS members | Symbolic maps for COBOL programs (COSGN00, COMEN01, etc.) |
| **Compiler Listings** | SYSOUT | Spool files | Cross-reference, data division map, diagnostics |

**Load Module Characteristics:**

Programs linked with specific attributes for CICS execution:

- **AMODE(31):** 31-bit addressing mode (access extended storage above 16MB line)
- **RMODE(ANY):** Load module can reside anywhere in virtual storage
- **RENT:** Reentrant (multiple tasks can execute same load module concurrently)
- **LET:** Allow unresolved externals (resolved at runtime by CICS)

#### 8.6.2.5 Quality Gates

**NO AUTOMATED QUALITY GATES**

CardDemo excludes automated testing and quality analysis:

- No unit tests (JUnit, pytest, Mocha, etc.)
- No integration tests
- No code coverage analysis
- No static code analysis (SonarQube, Checkmarx, Fortify)
- No security scanning (Snyk, WhiteSource, Black Duck)
- No performance testing (JMeter, LoadRunner)

**Manual Quality Validation:**

Developers perform manual testing:

1. Compile program and review compiler diagnostics for warnings/errors
2. Execute CEMT SET PROG(programname) NEWCOPY to refresh in CICS
3. Invoke transaction from 3270 terminal
4. Navigate through screen flows, enter test data
5. Verify expected behavior through visual inspection
6. Review CICS auxiliary trace for unexpected errors

**Production Quality Patterns (Reference Only):**

Production mainframe development typically implements:

- **COBOL Unit Testing:** IBM Debug Tool or Micro Focus Unit Testing Framework
- **Static Analysis:** IBM Application Discovery and Delivery Intelligence (ADDI)
- **Code Review:** Peer review before production promotion
- **Regression Testing:** Automated test scripts using terminal emulation (Micro Focus Verastream, IBM Rational Functional Tester)

### 8.6.3 Deployment Pipeline (Manual Process)

#### 8.6.3.1 Deployment Strategy

**MANUAL JCL SUBMISSION** - No blue-green, canary, or rolling deployment patterns.

**Online Program Deployment:**

1. Developer modifies COBOL source in Git repository
2. Source uploaded to `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.COBSRC(programname)` via FTP or $INDFILE
3. Developer submits `samples/jcl/CICCMP.jcl` with program name parameter
4. Compilation JCL executes three-step build (translate, compile, link-edit)
5. Load module updated in `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB(programname)`
6. JCL executes SDSF command: `EXEC 'CEMT SET PROG(programname) NEW'`
7. CICS discards old program copy, marks for reload
8. Next transaction invocation loads updated program from LOADLIB

**CICCMP.jcl Automated NEWCOPY (from `samples/jcl/CICCMP.jcl`):**

```jcl
//CICSCMD EXEC PGM=SDSF
//ISFPARMS DD *
  OWNER *
  FILTER JOBNAME EQ 'CICCMP'
  ST
  SELECT CICS01
  EXEC 'CEMT SET PROG(COSGN00C) NEW'
  END
/*
//SYSPRINT DD SYSOUT=*
```

This technique automates NEWCOPY as part of compilation job, eliminating manual terminal commands.

**Batch Program Deployment:**

1. Developer modifies batch COBOL source
2. Source uploaded to `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.COBSRC(programname)`
3. Developer submits `samples/jcl/BATCMP.jcl` with program name parameter
4. Compilation JCL executes two-step build (compile, link-edit)
5. Load module replaced in `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB(programname)`
6. Next batch job execution uses updated program automatically

No NEWCOPY required for batch programs - JES loads latest version from LOADLIB each execution.

**BMS Map Deployment:**

1. Developer modifies BMS map source
2. Source uploaded to `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.BMS(mapname)`
3. Developer submits `samples/jcl/BMSCMP.jcl` with map name parameter
4. Compilation JCL generates physical map load module and symbolic copybook
5. Physical map updated in `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.LOADLIB(mapname)`
6. Symbolic copybook updated in `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.COBCOPY(mapname)`
7. Programs using map must be recompiled to reflect copybook changes
8. CEMT SET MAPSET(mapname) NEWCOPY refreshes map in CICS

#### 8.6.3.2 Environment Promotion Workflow

**NO AUTOMATED PROMOTION**

Manual promotion workflow (typical production pattern):

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Dev[Development<br/>Environment] -->|Manual Process| Test[Test/QA<br/>Environment]
    Test -->|Change Request| Staging[Staging<br/>Environment]
    Staging -->|Change Approval| Prod[Production<br/>Environment]
    
    Dev -.->|1. Developer Compiles| Dev
    Test -.->|2. QA Tests| Test
    Staging -.->|3. UAT Validates| Staging
    Prod -.->|4. Operations Deploys| Prod
    
    style Dev fill:#E1F5FF
    style Test fill:#FFF4E1
    style Staging fill:#FFE1E1
    style Prod fill:#E8F5E9
```

**Promotion Steps:**

1. **Development → Test:**
   - Developer exports source from Git
   - Uploads to test region source libraries
   - Submits compilation JCL in test environment
   - QA team executes regression tests

2. **Test → Staging:**
   - Change request submitted through change management system
   - Change Advisory Board (CAB) reviews and approves
   - Operations staff uploads source to staging libraries
   - Compiles programs in staging CICS region
   - User Acceptance Testing (UAT) team validates

3. **Staging → Production:**
   - Production change request submitted with CAB approval
   - Operations staff schedules deployment during change window
   - Source uploaded to production libraries
   - Compilation executed in production region
   - NEWCOPY commands refresh programs in production CICS
   - Smoke tests executed to verify deployment

#### 8.6.3.3 Rollback Procedures

**MANUAL ROLLBACK**

**Online Program Rollback:**

1. Identify previous version load module in LOADLIB history or backup
2. Copy previous version to current member name: `IEBCOPY FROM(backup) TO(current)`
3. Execute `CEMT SET PROG(programname) NEWCOPY` to reload previous version
4. Verify rollback through test transaction execution

**Alternative Rollback Method:**

Maintain numbered versions in LOADLIB:

- `COSGN00C` - Current production version
- `COSGN00C.V01` - Previous version 1
- `COSGN00C.V02` - Previous version 2

Rollback by copying `COSGN00C.V01` to `COSGN00C` and executing NEWCOPY.

**VSAM File Rollback:**

If deployment includes data changes requiring rollback:

1. Execute `app/jcl/CLOSEFIL.jcl` to close files in CICS
2. Restore from backup using IDCAMS REPRO
3. Execute `app/jcl/OPENFIL.jcl` to reopen files
4. Rollback programs to previous versions
5. Validate data integrity through test transactions

**No Automated Rollback:**

- No deployment pipelines with automatic rollback on failure detection
- No feature flags or canary deployments enabling gradual rollout
- No blue-green deployment switching between environments

#### 8.6.3.4 Post-Deployment Validation

**Manual Validation Process:**

1. **Program Availability Check:**
   - Execute `CEMT INQ PROG(programname)` to verify ENABLED status
   - Verify LOADLIB member updated with correct timestamp
   - Review compiler listing for successful compilation (RC=0)

2. **File Availability Check:**
   - Execute `CEMT INQ FILE(filename)` to verify OPEN, ENABLED status
   - Verify all required files accessible

3. **Transaction Smoke Tests:**
   - Invoke sign-on transaction CC00
   - Authenticate with test user credentials
   - Navigate main menu (COMEN01C)
   - Execute sample inquiry transaction (account inquiry, card list)
   - Verify expected screen displays and data retrieval

4. **CICS Message Log Review:**
   - Review CICS message log via SDSF or CEMT for error messages
   - Verify no ABEND messages for deployed programs
   - Check for file open/close messages confirming proper initialization

5. **Auxiliary Trace Review:**
   - Enable auxiliary trace for deployed transaction: `CEMT SET TRAN(xxxx) TRACENUM(1)`
   - Execute test transaction
   - Review trace for unexpected errors or file operation failures
   - Disable trace: `CEMT SET TRAN(xxxx) TRACENUM(0)`

#### 8.6.3.5 Release Management Process

**NO FORMAL RELEASE MANAGEMENT**

CardDemo uses Git tags for version identification but lacks formal release processes:

**Version Tagging:**

```bash
git tag -a CardDemo_v1.0 -m "CardDemo version 1.0"
git push origin CardDemo_v1.0
```

**Release Documentation:**

No release notes, changelogs, or deployment runbooks maintained in repository. Production systems typically maintain:

- **Release Notes:** Feature enhancements, bug fixes, breaking changes
- **Deployment Runbook:** Step-by-step deployment procedures with validation checkpoints
- **Rollback Plan:** Detailed rollback procedures with decision criteria
- **Communication Plan:** Stakeholder notifications for downtime or functionality changes

### 8.6.4 CI/CD Modernization Patterns

Organizations modernizing mainframe development typically implement:

**Phase 1: Source Control Integration**
- Implement Git-based source control for all mainframe assets
- Establish branch protection rules and pull request workflows
- Automate source upload to mainframe via Zowe CLI or DBB

**Phase 2: Build Automation**
- Implement Jenkins or GitLab CI with z/OS agents
- Automate JCL submission and compilation through pipelines
- Collect compiler listings and return codes for build verification

**Phase 3: Testing Integration**
- Implement automated unit testing with Micro Focus Unit Testing Framework
- Execute regression tests via terminal emulation frameworks
- Integrate code quality analysis (SonarQube with COBOL plugin)

**Phase 4: Deployment Automation**
- Automate CICS NEWCOPY through pipeline scripts
- Implement blue-green deployment with CICS regions
- Automate rollback based on health check failures

**Phase 5: Cloud-Native CI/CD**
- Migrate to AWS CodePipeline or GitHub Actions
- Containerize applications with Docker multi-stage builds
- Deploy to Amazon EKS with Helm chart-based deployment
- Implement progressive delivery with Flagger or Argo Rollouts

These patterns represent modernization trajectories evaluated during migration planning.

## 8.7 Infrastructure Monitoring

### 8.7.1 Monitoring Strategy Overview

CardDemo implements a **native mainframe monitoring strategy** relying exclusively on z/OS and CICS infrastructure facilities. This approach authentically represents typical mainframe operational practices where platform-level monitoring provides comprehensive system visibility without custom application instrumentation.

As documented in `Section 6.5.1.1 Applicability Statement`, the system intentionally excludes modern observability capabilities including APM integration, distributed tracing, custom metrics collection, real-time dashboards, and automated alerting systems.

### 8.7.2 Resource Monitoring Approach

#### 8.7.2.1 CICS Transaction Statistics

CICS Transaction Server automatically collects comprehensive performance metrics without application-level instrumentation:

| Metric Category | Metrics Collected | Access Method | Typical Use Case |
|----------------|-------------------|---------------|------------------|
| **Transaction Volume** | Count, TPS, peak rates | CEMT INQ TASK, CMF reports | Capacity planning, workload trending |
| **Response Time** | Average, min/max, 95th percentile | CMF, CMON | SLA verification, performance analysis |
| **Resource Consumption** | CPU time, elapsed time, dispatch count | RMF reports | Cost allocation, optimization |
| **File Operations** | READ/WRITE/BROWSE counts | CEMT INQ FILE | Performance tuning, bottleneck identification |

**Operational Access:**

Operations staff access statistics through:

- **CEMT Commands:** `CEMT INQ TASK`, `CEMT INQ TRAN(xxxx)`, `CEMT INQ FILE(filename)`
- **CICS Monitoring Facility (CMF):** Records detailed statistics to SMF datasets
- **CMON Transaction:** Online transaction monitoring with real-time display

#### 8.7.2.2 VSAM File Statistics

CICS collects file-level metrics for each of the 13 VSAM KSDS datasets:

| Metric | Description | Performance Implication | Monitoring Threshold |
|--------|-------------|------------------------|---------------------|
| **Buffer Hit Ratio** | % I/O satisfied from LSR buffer pools | Higher ratios reduce physical I/O | Target: >90% |
| **String Waits** | Requests waiting for VSAM strings | Concurrency contention | Alert: >100/hour |
| **Record Waits** | Time waiting for locked records | Record-level lock contention | Alert: >500ms average |
| **I/O Request Count** | Total READ/WRITE/BROWSE operations | Capacity planning baseline | Trend analysis |

**LSR Buffer Pool Configuration (from `app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD`):**

```
FILE LSRPOOLNUM(1) 
     DATABUFFERS(2) 
     INDEXBUFFERS(1)
     READINTEG(UNCOMMITTED)
     STRINGS(1)
```

Operations staff monitor buffer pool effectiveness through `CEMT INQ FILE` commands displaying hit ratios and adjust buffer allocations based on observed performance.

#### 8.7.2.3 Batch Job Accounting

z/OS JES automatically captures execution metrics for all batch jobs:

| Metric Category | Data Captured | Source | Purpose |
|----------------|---------------|--------|---------|
| **Job Timing** | Elapsed time, start/end timestamps | JES job log (JESMSGLG) | Batch window management, SLA tracking |
| **CPU Consumption** | CPU seconds per step, zIIP usage | SMF Type 30 records | Cost allocation, performance analysis |
| **I/O Operations** | EXCP count, physical I/O, DASD access time | SMF records | I/O subsystem capacity planning |
| **Return Codes** | Step RC, abend codes, system completion codes | JES job log | Success/failure determination |

**Key Batch Jobs Monitored:**

- **POSTTRAN.jcl (CBTRN02C):** Transaction posting from DALYTRAN to TRANSACT/ACCTFILE
- **INTCALC.jcl (CBACT02C):** Interest calculation and account balance updates
- **CREASTMT.JCL (CBSTM03A):** Multi-step statement generation with SORT and REPRO

#### 8.7.3.2 Logging Architecture

**CICS Auxiliary Trace:**

CICS automatically records detailed transaction execution traces:

| Trace Category | Data Recorded | Analysis Tool | Purpose |
|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------|
| **CICS Commands** | EXEC CICS READ/WRITE with parameters and RESP codes | DFHTU690 (CICS trace utility) | Command-level debugging |
| **Program Control** | XCTL, LINK, RETURN with COMMAREA lengths | CICS trace formatting | Program flow analysis |
| **Terminal I/O** | SEND MAP, RECEIVE MAP with field data | IPCS trace analysis | Screen interaction verification |
| **Timing Data** | Timestamps for operation start/end | Performance analysis tools | Response time breakdown |

**CICS Transaction Dumps:**

Abnormal termination triggers automatic dumps capturing:

| Dump Component | Information Captured | Diagnostic Value |
|---------------|---------------------|------------------|
| **Working Storage** | All program variables with current values | Variable state inspection at failure point |
| **COMMAREA Structure** | Session state including user context | Session flow analysis |
| **CICS Control Blocks** | Task control area, file control blocks | Resource state at failure |
| **Execution Trace** | Backward trace of program flow | Logic flow leading to failure |

Dumps stored in CICS dump datasets (DFHDUMPxx), formatted using CICS dump utilities (DFHDU670) or IPCS.

**Batch Program Logging:**

Batch programs write structured operational messages via COBOL DISPLAY statements:

```cobol
DISPLAY 'CBTRN02C: Transaction posting started'
DISPLAY 'CBTRN02C: Processing DALYTRAN records'
DISPLAY 'CBTRN02C: Total records processed: ' WS-RECORD-COUNT
DISPLAY 'CBTRN02C: Total records rejected: ' WS-REJECT-COUNT
DISPLAY 'CBTRN02C: Transaction posting completed'
```

Logs accessible via SDSF (System Display and Search Facility) for online review of JES spool output.

### 8.7.4 Cost Monitoring and Optimization

**Traditional Mainframe Billing Model:**

Cost monitoring differs fundamentally from cloud granular billing:

| Cost Component | Measurement | Billing Frequency | Optimization Strategy |
|---------------|-------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| **CPU Consumption** | MIPS (Million Instructions Per Second) or MSU (Million Service Units) | Monthly | Optimize COBOL programs, reduce I/O, leverage zIIP engines |
| **Storage Consumption** | DASD cylinders allocated | Monthly | Delete unused datasets, compress sequential files, reorganize VSAM |
| **Software Licensing** | Based on CPU capacity or usage | Annual | Consolidate CICS regions, optimize batch workloads |

**No Granular Per-Transaction Costing:**

Unlike cloud environments with per-request pricing (Lambda invocations, API Gateway calls), mainframe billing aggregates all consumption:

- No cost allocation per transaction type
- No real-time cost dashboards (CloudWatch, Cost Explorer)
- No automated cost anomaly detection
- No tagging-based cost allocation

**Capacity Planning Focus:**

Operations teams focus on capacity utilization trends:

- Monitor SMF Type 30 records for CPU time trends
- Analyze RMF reports for LPAR utilization patterns
- Project future capacity requirements based on workload growth
- Schedule LPAR CPU/memory upgrades quarterly or annually

### 8.7.5 Security Monitoring

**Limited Security Monitoring:**

CardDemo implements minimal security monitoring appropriate for demonstration purposes:

| Security Aspect | Monitoring Capability | Production Gap |
|----------------|----------------------|---------------|
| **Authentication Attempts** | None - no logging of USRSEC file reads | Production systems log all RACF authentication attempts |
| **Failed Login Tracking** | None - no account lockout | Production systems track failed attempts with lockout after threshold |
| **Data Access Auditing** | None - no audit trail for file operations | Production systems log all sensitive data access (PCI-DSS, SOX) |
| **Privileged Operations** | None - no logging of admin functions | Production systems audit all administrative actions |

**RACF Integration in Production:**

Production mainframe systems integrate RACF for comprehensive security monitoring:

- **SMF Type 80 Records:** Authentication attempts with success/failure indication
- **SMF Type 81 Records:** Resource access attempts with authorization decisions
- **RACF Audit Reports:** Daily/weekly security audit reports
- **Violation Notifications:** Real-time alerts for security policy violations

### 8.7.6 Compliance Auditing

**NOT IMPLEMENTED**

CardDemo lacks compliance auditing capabilities:

- No automated compliance reporting
- No audit log aggregation
- No evidence collection for auditors
- Manual review of transaction dumps and logs required

**Production Compliance Patterns:**

Organizations subject to regulatory compliance implement:

- **PCI-DSS:** Card data access logging, encryption verification, vulnerability scanning
- **SOX:** Financial data modification audit trails, segregation of duties verification
- **HIPAA:** PHI (Protected Health Information) access tracking, breach detection
- **GDPR:** Personal data access logging, data retention policy enforcement

### 8.7.7 Operational Monitoring Tools

#### 8.7.7.1 CICS Resource Management Tools

| Tool | Access Method | Primary Functions | Monitoring Capabilities |
|------|--------------|-------------------|------------------------|
| **CEMT** | CICS transaction from 3270 terminal | File/transaction/program status | Real-time resource state, OPEN/CLOSE files, NEWCOPY programs |
| **CEDA** | CICS transaction from 3270 terminal | Resource definition management | Create/modify/delete CICS resources |
| **CECI/CECS** | CICS transactions | Command interpreter | Test EXEC CICS commands, verify syntax |

#### 8.7.7.2 z/OS System Management Tools

| Tool | Access Method | Primary Functions | Monitoring Capabilities |
|------|--------------|-------------------|------------------------|
| **SDSF** | TSO/ISPF application | Job output viewing, console commands | Browse SYSOUT, submit jobs, view JES spool |
| **RMF** | Batch reports or real-time monitor | Resource measurement and reporting | CPU utilization, I/O activity, storage usage |
| **IPCS** | TSO/ISPF application | Dump analysis | Format transaction dumps, analyze system dumps |

#### 8.7.7.3 VSAM Management Tools

| Tool | Access Method | Primary Functions | Monitoring Capabilities |
|------|--------------|-------------------|------------------------|
| **IDCAMS** | Batch JCL invocation | Dataset definition, backup, maintenance | LISTCAT for attributes, VERIFY for integrity, REPRO for backup |
| **IEBGENER** | Batch JCL invocation | Sequential dataset copy | Copy VSAM exports, generate copybooks |

### 8.7.8 Monitoring Gaps and Modernization Opportunities

As documented in `Section 6.5.7.1 Intentional Monitoring Gaps`, CardDemo's monitoring approach reflects pre-cloud mainframe patterns. The following modern capabilities are explicitly absent:

| Missing Capability | Production Equivalent | Modernization Approach |
|-------------------|---------------------|----------------------|
| **APM Integration** | AppDynamics, Dynatrace, New Relic | Instrument COBOL with APM agents |
| **Custom Business Metrics** | Transaction amount tracking, balance trending | Emit CloudWatch/DataDog metrics |
| **Distributed Tracing** | OpenTelemetry, Zipkin, Jaeger | Add correlation IDs during microservices decomposition |
| **Real-Time Dashboards** | Grafana, Kibana, CloudWatch dashboards | Create dashboards from APM data |
| **Automated Alerting** | PagerDuty, OpsGenie, ServiceNow | Configure threshold alerts in CloudWatch |
| **SLA Monitoring** | Automated SLA compliance tracking | Define SLOs, track SLI metrics |
| **Audit Logging** | Security event logging for compliance | Implement application audit logs to CloudWatch Logs |
| **Health Check Endpoints** | HTTP /health and /ready for orchestrators | Add REST API health endpoints |

## 8.9 Infrastructure Cost Estimates

### 8.9.1 Traditional Mainframe Cost Model

**Demonstration System Cost Profile:**

CardDemo as a demonstration system with synthetic data (50 records) represents minimal resource consumption. Cost estimates below reflect production-scale deployments for reference.

| Resource Category | Demonstration | Small Production | Medium Production | Enterprise |
|------------------|---------------|------------------|-------------------|------------|
| **MIPS Capacity** | <1 MIPS | 100 MIPS | 500 MIPS | 2,000+ MIPS |
| **DASD Storage** | 500 MB | 50 GB | 500 GB | 5+ TB |
| **CICS Region Memory** | 512 MB | 1 GB | 4 GB | 16+ GB |
| **Monthly Cost (USD)** | $0 (shared system) | $50K-$100K | $250K-$500K | $1M+ |

**Cost Components:**

1. **CPU/MIPS Consumption:**
   - Billed based on Million Instructions Per Second (MIPS) or Million Service Units (MSU)
   - Typical range: $2,000-$5,000 per MIPS per month
   - CardDemo demonstration: <0.1 MIPS (negligible cost)

2. **DASD Storage:**
   - Billed per gigabyte of disk storage allocated
   - Typical range: $50-$200 per GB per month (varies by storage tier)
   - CardDemo demonstration: <1 GB total

3. **Software Licensing:**
   - CICS Transaction Server: $100K-$500K annually (capacity-based)
   - IBM COBOL compiler: $50K-$200K annually
   - z/OS operating system: $200K-$1M+ annually

4. **Personnel Costs:**
   - Mainframe developers: $100K-$150K annually
   - Mainframe operations staff: $80K-$120K annually
   - Mainframe architects: $150K-$200K+ annually

### 8.9.2 AWS Mainframe Modernization Cost Model

**AWS M2 Managed Runtime Pricing (Reference Only):**

Organizations migrating to AWS Mainframe Modernization service encounter different cost structures:

| Component | Pricing Model | Typical Monthly Cost |
|-----------|--------------|---------------------|
| **Managed Runtime Environment** | Per-hour instance pricing | $5K-$20K (depends on instance size) |
| **Storage** | EBS volumes, S3 storage | $500-$5K (depends on data volume) |
| **Data Transfer** | Ingress/egress charges | $100-$1K (depends on usage patterns) |
| **Backup Storage** | S3 backup retention | $100-$500 (depends on retention policy) |

**Cost Optimization Strategies:**

1. **Right-Sizing:** Select appropriate AWS M2 instance types based on workload profiles
2. **Reserved Capacity:** Purchase 1-year or 3-year reserved instances for predictable workloads
3. **Storage Tiering:** Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering for infrequently accessed data
4. **Batch Optimization:** Execute batch jobs during off-peak hours with spot instances

### 8.9.3 Cloud-Native Modernization Cost Model

**Fully Modernized Microservices Architecture:**

Organizations rewriting mainframe applications as cloud-native microservices encounter additional cost structures:

| Component | AWS Service | Typical Monthly Cost |
|-----------|------------|---------------------|
| **Compute (Containers)** | Amazon EKS with Fargate | $5K-$20K (depends on pod count) |
| **Database** | Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL | $2K-$10K (depends on instance size) |
| **API Gateway** | Amazon API Gateway | $500-$5K (depends on request volume) |
| **Monitoring** | Amazon CloudWatch, X-Ray | $500-$2K (depends on metrics/traces) |
| **Load Balancing** | Application Load Balancer | $200-$1K |
| **Total Monthly (Estimated)** | | $10K-$40K+ |

### 8.10.2 Runtime Dependencies

| Dependency | Purpose | Integration Method | Fallback Strategy |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|------------------|
| **VSAM Access Method** | Data storage and retrieval | Native z/OS file system | None - critical dependency |

### 8.10.3 No External Service Dependencies

CardDemo has **no external service dependencies**:

- No external databases (uses VSAM files)
- No message queues (MQ Series, Kafka, SQS)
- No external APIs (REST, SOAP, GraphQL)
- No cloud services (S3, DynamoDB, Lambda)
- No third-party SaaS platforms

This self-contained design simplifies deployment and eliminates external service availability risks.

## 8.11 Resource Sizing Guidelines

### 8.11.1 CICS Region Sizing

**Memory Allocation:**

| Workload Profile | CICS Region Size | MAXTASKS | DSA Size | ERDSA Size |
|-----------------|------------------|----------|----------|------------|
| **Demonstration (CardDemo)** | 512 MB | 50 | 128 MB | 64 MB |
| **Small Production** | 1 GB | 200 | 256 MB | 128 MB |
| **Medium Production** | 4 GB | 1,000 | 1 GB | 512 MB |
| **Enterprise** | 16 GB+ | 5,000+ | 4 GB+ | 2 GB+ |

**Sizing Factors:**

- **Concurrent Users:** Each terminal session consumes CICS task control block storage
- **Program Working Storage:** Reentrant programs (RENT) minimize per-task storage
- **LSR Buffer Pools:** Larger buffer pools improve performance but consume DSA storage
- **Temporary Storage Queues:** TS queue storage consumes ERDSA

### 8.11.2 VSAM Dataset Sizing

**Primary and Secondary Allocations:**

| File Type | Primary (Cylinders) | Secondary (Cylinders) | Extents Allowed | Growth Pattern |
|-----------|-------------------|---------------------|----------------|----------------|
| **Master Files (CUSTFILE, ACCTFILE)** | 5 | 1 | 15 | Slow growth (1-5% monthly) |
| **Transaction Files (TRANSACT)** | 10 | 2 | 15 | Fast growth (10-20% monthly) |
| **Reference Files (DISCGRP, TRANTYPE)** | 1 | 1 | 5 | Minimal growth |
| **Cross-Reference Files (XREFFILE, CARDFILE)** | 3 | 1 | 10 | Moderate growth (5-10% monthly) |

**Reorganization Thresholds:**

Execute VSAM reorganization when:
- **CA Splits:** >20% control area splits indicating poor free space management
- **CI Splits:** >30% control interval splits indicating fragmentation
- **Extents:** >10 extents indicating excessive extension activity
- **Performance Degradation:** String waits increasing, buffer hit ratios declining

### 8.11.3 Batch Window Sizing

**Job Duration Estimates:**

| Batch Job | Demonstration (50 records) | Small Production (10K records) | Medium Production (1M records) | Enterprise (100M records) |
|-----------|---------------------------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|--------------------------|
| **POSTTRAN** | 5 seconds | 5 minutes | 30 minutes | 4 hours |
| **INTCALC** | 3 seconds | 3 minutes | 20 minutes | 3 hours |
| **CREASTMT** | 10 seconds | 10 minutes | 1 hour | 8 hours |
| **Total Batch Window** | 30 seconds | 20 minutes | 2 hours | 16 hours |

**Batch Window Planning:**

- **Traditional Overnight Window:** 10 PM - 6 AM (8 hours)
- **Extended Weekend Window:** Friday 6 PM - Monday 6 AM (60 hours)
- **Continuous Processing:** Eliminate batch windows through incremental update patterns

### 8.12.2 File Coordination Procedures

**Batch Window Coordination (from `README.md` lines 162-183):**

1. **Close Files for Batch Processing:**
   - Execute `app/jcl/CLOSEFIL.jcl`
   - CEMT commands close VSAM files in CICS region
   - Online transactions gracefully fail with "file unavailable" messages

2. **Execute Batch Jobs in Sequence:**
   - POSTTRAN.jcl: Post daily transactions from DALYTRAN
   - INTCALC.jcl: Calculate interest and update account balances
   - CREASTMT.JCL: Generate customer statements
   - TRANBKP.jcl: Backup transaction files to GDG

3. **Reopen Files for Online Processing:**
   - Execute `app/jcl/OPENFIL.jcl`
   - CEMT commands reopen VSAM files for CICS
   - Online transactions resume normal processing

**Critical Success Factors:**

- Coordinate batch window with business operations (end-of-day, weekend)
- Validate all batch jobs complete successfully (RC=0) before reopening files
- Monitor CICS message log for file open/close confirmation messages
- Execute test transactions after reopening to verify online availability

### 8.12.3 Program Maintenance Procedures

**CICS Program Refresh:**

1. Modify COBOL source code in Git repository
2. Upload source to mainframe via FTP or Zowe CLI
3. Submit compilation JCL (CICCMP.jcl)
4. Verify successful compilation (RC=0 in SYSOUT)
5. Execute `CEMT SET PROG(programname) NEWCOPY`
6. Test transaction execution via 3270 terminal
7. Monitor CICS auxiliary trace for errors

**BMS Map Refresh:**

1. Modify BMS map source
2. Upload source to mainframe
3. Submit map compilation JCL (BMSCMP.jcl)
4. Verify physical map and copybook generation
5. Recompile programs referencing modified copybook
6. Execute `CEMT SET MAPSET(mapname) NEWCOPY`
7. Execute `CEMT SET PROG(programname) NEWCOPY` for all programs using map
8. Test screen displays via 3270 terminal

**Batch Program Refresh:**

1. Modify batch COBOL source
2. Upload source to mainframe
3. Submit batch compilation JCL (BATCMP.jcl)
4. Verify successful compilation and linkage editing
5. No NEWCOPY required (JES loads latest version at job execution)
6. Test by submitting batch job in test environment
7. Review job output in SDSF for successful execution

### 8.12.4 VSAM Dataset Maintenance

**Dataset Reorganization Procedure:**

1. Execute `CLOSEFIL.jcl` to quiesce online activity
2. Backup dataset using IDCAMS REPRO to backup cluster
3. Define new cluster with optimized space allocation
4. REPRO data from old cluster to new cluster
5. Delete old cluster using IDCAMS DELETE
6. Rename new cluster to production name
7. Rebuild alternate indexes using BLDINDEX
8. Execute `OPENFIL.jcl` to resume online processing
9. Verify reorganization success through LISTCAT statistics

**Space Management:**

Monitor and manage DASD space consumption:

- Review IDCAMS LISTCAT output for extent counts
- Identify datasets approaching 15 extents (reorganization threshold)
- Compress PDS/PDSE libraries to reclaim unused space
- Archive old data to tape for long-term retention
- Delete obsolete datasets and GDG generations

### 8.13.4 Key Infrastructure Findings

**Traditional Mainframe Infrastructure:**
- CardDemo operates on native z/OS mainframe infrastructure with CICS Transaction Server V5.6 and JES batch processing
- No modern cloud infrastructure (containers, orchestration, cloud services) in current implementation
- Single-region monolithic deployment eliminates distributed systems complexity

**Manual Deployment Model:**
- All deployment activities performed through manual JCL job submission, CEMT/CEDA commands, operator intervention
- No automated CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI)
- Intentional absence reflects traditional mainframe development paradigm

**Native Monitoring Approach:**
- Monitoring relies exclusively on z/OS and CICS native facilities (CEMT, CMF, SDSF, RMF, IPCS)
- No modern APM integration (AppDynamics, Dynatrace, New Relic)
- No distributed tracing, custom metrics, real-time dashboards, or automated alerting

**AWS Mainframe Modernization Target:**
- Repository contains AWS M2 runtime packages (Micro Focus, UniKix) indicating future migration path
- Packages represent deployment artifacts for future state, not current operational infrastructure

**Infrastructure as Code Patterns:**
- Infrastructure defined through JCL dataset definitions using IDCAMS commands
- CICS resources defined in CARDDEMO.CSD file processed by DFHCSDUP utility
- No Terraform, CloudFormation, or other modern IaC tooling

**Disaster Recovery Approach:**
- VSAM backup using IDCAMS REPRO to backup clusters
- GDG versioning for transaction reject files with LIMIT(5) retention
- Manual recovery procedures with no automated failover or geographic redundancy
- No defined RPO/RTO objectives (demonstration system characteristics)

**Cost Model:**
- Traditional MIPS-based or MSU-based mainframe billing
- No granular per-transaction costing or real-time cost monitoring
- Capacity planning focus rather than automated cost optimization

**External Dependencies:**
- Self-contained application with no external service dependencies
- Native z/OS dependencies only (COBOL compiler, CICS runtime, VSAM, JES)
- No databases, message queues, APIs, or cloud services

This Infrastructure section documents the authentic traditional mainframe deployment patterns that CardDemo represents as a pre-modernization reference implementation.

### 9.1.2 Build and Compilation Procedures

The CardDemo application employs IBM Enterprise COBOL for z/OS V6.3 with specific compilation parameters optimized for CICS transaction processing and batch execution environments.

#### Online Program Compilation Standards

Online CICS programs utilize the `BUILDONL.prc` procedure with the following specifications:

**Compiler Configuration:**
- **Compiler Program**: IGYCRCTL (IBM Enterprise COBOL V6.3 compiler driver)
- **Compiler Library**: IGY.SIGYCOMP.V63 (compiler load modules)
- **CICS Preprocessor Library**: OEM.CICSTS.V05R06M0 (CICS Transaction Server V5.6 translator)

**Compilation Parameters:**
- `CICS` - Enables CICS command-level API recognition and generates required control blocks
- `NODYNAM` - Disables dynamic CALL statement resolution, requiring static linking of all subprograms
- `RENT` - Produces reentrant object code enabling multiple concurrent executions of the same program instance
- `NOSEQ` - Ignores sequence number columns (73-80), treating them as comment space

**Linkage Editor Configuration:**
- **Binder Program**: HEWL (z/OS Program Management Binder)
- **Parameters**: 
  - `LIST` - Produces link-edit listing showing module composition
  - `XREF` - Generates cross-reference of external symbols
  - `LET` - Allows unresolved external references (marked for runtime resolution)
  - `MAP` - Creates load module memory map
  - `AMODE(31)` - Specifies 31-bit addressing mode
  - `RMODE(ANY)` - Permits load module placement anywhere in virtual storage

#### Batch Program Compilation Standards

Batch programs utilize the `BUILDBAT.prc` procedure with modified parameters suitable for non-CICS execution:

**Compilation Parameters:**
- `APOST` - Specifies apostrophe as literal delimiter instead of quotation marks
- `LIST` - Generates source listing with embedded diagnostics
- `MAP` - Produces data division map showing storage allocation
- `NUMBER` - Processes sequence numbers in columns 1-6
- `NOSEQ` - Ignores sequence numbers in columns 73-80

#### BMS Assembly Procedures

BMS source files undergo two-phase assembly producing both executable map load modules and COBOL symbolic map copybooks:

**Phase 1: Load Module Generation**
- **Assembler**: ASMA90 (High Level Assembler for z/OS)
- **Parameter**: `SYSPARM(MAP)` - Generates load modules for runtime screen rendering
- **Output**: Physical mapsets loaded into CICS region

**Phase 2: Copybook Generation**
- **Parameter**: `SYSPARM(DSECT)` - Generates COBOL data structure definitions
- **Output**: Symbolic map copybooks (AI/AO pattern) for program compilation

### 9.1.3 CICS Resource Configuration Standards

The CICS System Definition file (`CARDDEMO.CSD`) establishes consistent configuration standards across all file, program, mapset, and transaction resources.

#### File Definition Standards

All VSAM file resources share common performance and integrity parameters:

**Buffer Management:**
- **LSRPOOLNUM**: 1 - All files participate in Local Shared Resource pool 1, enabling efficient buffer sharing across concurrent transactions
- **STRINGS**: 1 - Single concurrent I/O operation permitted per file, adequate for demonstration workloads
- **DATABUFFERS**: 2 - Two control interval buffers allocated for data access
- **INDEXBUFFERS**: 1 - Single control interval buffer allocated for index access

**Concurrency and Integrity:**
- **READINTEG**: UNCOMMITTED - Read operations do not acquire locks, permitting maximum concurrency with potential for non-repeatable reads
- **DSNSHARING**: ALLREQS - Dataset may be shared across multiple CICS regions and batch jobs
- **UPDATEMODEL**: LOCKING - Updates acquire exclusive record locks preventing lost updates

**Recovery Configuration:**
- **JOURNAL**: NO - File changes are not logged to CICS journals
- **RECOVERY**: NONE - No automatic transaction backout for file updates
- **BACKUPTYPE**: STATIC - Backup operations require file quiescence

#### Resource Definition Inventory

The CICS System Definition encompasses:

**File Resources (13 definitions):**
- `ACCTDAT` - Account master file
- `CARDAIX` - Card alternate index by customer number
- `CARDDAT` - Card master file
- `CCXREF` - Card-to-customer cross-reference
- `CUSTDAT` - Customer master file
- `CXACAIX` - Customer-to-account alternate index
- `TRANSACT` - Transaction history file
- `USRSEC` - User security credentials
- `TRANCATG` - Transaction category definitions
- `TRANTYPE` - Transaction type definitions
- `DISCGRP` - Disclosure group definitions
- `TCATBALF` - Transaction category balance file
- `DALYTRAN` - Daily transaction work file

**Program Resources (28 definitions):**
- 16 online transaction programs supporting interactive processing
- 11 batch programs performing file maintenance and reporting
- 1 utility program for administrative functions

**Mapset Resources (17 definitions):**
- One mapset per BMS source file, each containing one or more screen maps

**Transaction Resources (20+ definitions):**
- Transaction codes linking terminal input to program execution
- Configured with appropriate security, priority, and execution characteristics

### 9.1.4 Test Data Specifications

The repository provides comprehensive test datasets in both ASCII and EBCDIC encodings to support development across diverse platform environments.

#### ASCII Format Test Data

Located in `app/data/ASCII/`, these files contain human-readable test records:

**Customer and Account Data:**
- `custdata.txt` - 50 customer records, 500 bytes per record containing customer demographics, contact information, credit scores, and account relationship data
- `acctdata.txt` - 50 account records, 300 bytes per record containing account numbers, balances, credit limits, interest rates, and account status indicators
- `carddata.txt` - 50 card records, 150 bytes per record containing card numbers (masked), expiration dates, CVV codes, and card status information
- `cardxref.txt` - 50 cross-reference records, 50 bytes per record (34 characters used) linking card numbers to customer identifiers

**Transaction Data:**
- `dailytran.txt` - Daily transaction file with 220-byte records capturing transaction date, time, card number, merchant details, amounts, and authorization codes
- `tcatbal.txt` - 50 transaction category balance records tracking spending by category for rewards and analytics

**Reference Data:**
- `trancatg.txt` - 18 transaction category definitions (e.g., Groceries, Gas, Dining, Travel) with category codes and descriptions
- `trantype.txt` - 7 transaction type definitions (80 bytes each) including Purchase, Cash Advance, Payment, Balance Transfer, Fee, Interest, and Credit
- `discgrp.txt` - 3 disclosure groups: `A` (standard terms), `DEFAULT` (baseline disclosure), `ZEROAPR` (promotional zero-interest terms)

#### EBCDIC Format Test Data

Located in `app/data/EBCDIC/`, these files contain equivalent records in mainframe-native character encoding:

**Dataset Naming Convention:**
- **Prefix**: `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO` - High-level qualifier identifying AWS Mainframe Modernization environment and application
- **Pattern**: `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.{filename}.VSAM.KSDS` - Complete dataset name including file type and organization
- **Example**: `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.ACCTDATA.VSAM.KSDS` - Account data file as Key-Sequenced Data Set

**Character Encoding Considerations:**
- EBCDIC files require character set conversion when accessed from ASCII platforms
- Numeric fields in COMP-3 (packed decimal) format maintain platform independence
- Binary fields (COMP) require endianness consideration during cross-platform access

CardDemo supports deployment across multiple target platforms, each with specific configuration requirements and runtime dependencies.

#### Supported Platform Environments

**Native z/OS Deployment:**
- Traditional mainframe environment with CICS Transaction Server V5.6 or higher

#### Dataset Naming Conventions

**High-Level Qualifier Strategy:**
- **Standard Format**: `{HLQ}.{APPLICATION}.{FILENAME}.{FILETYPE}.{ORGANIZATION}`
- **AWS M2 HLQ**: `AWS.M2` - Identifies AWS Mainframe Modernization environment
- **Application Qualifier**: `CARDDEMO` - Application identifier
- **Organization Suffix**: `VSAM.KSDS` - Virtual Storage Access Method, Key-Sequenced Data Set

**Example Dataset Names:**
- `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.ACCTDATA.VSAM.KSDS` - Account master file
- `AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CARDDAT.VSAM.KSDS` - Card master file
